assessments.title: Issues are for actual problems only
assessments.applicabilityRationale: This is a general review-output classification rule that applies across Hosted implementation, testing, and documentation findings.
assessments.summary: Add a missing global rule that limits `ISSUES` to evidence-backed defects and excludes stylistic or speculative blockers.
assessments.impactDescription: This would keep Hosted reviews from escalating preferences or unsupported concerns into merge-blocking findings and would align issue output with demonstrated defects.
assessments.currentHostedCoverage: Current Hosted rules require evidence on individual surfaces through `IMPL-EVID-001`, `TEST-EVID-001`, and `DOCS-EVID-001`, but no active rule defines what is eligible for `ISSUES`.
assessments.proposedText: Classify a concern as an Issue only when current-run evidence shows a real defect, regression, policy violation, missing requirement, or correctness risk. Do not place stylistic preferences or unsupported speculation in Issues.
assessments.selectionRationale: severity 4 fits because bad issue gating directly distorts review outcomes; frequency 5 fits because every review classifies findings; breadth 5 fits because the rule applies across all Hosted review surfaces; hostedDetectability 4 fits because issue text and supporting evidence are observable in the review output; evidenceStrength 3 fits because the candidate is clear but not tied to an existing upstream rule citation; falsePositiveRisk 1 fits because the rule only excludes unsupported or stylistic blockers; redundancy 1 fits because current Hosted rules do not already define issue eligibility.

assessments.title: Blocking classification requires concrete current-run harm
assessments.applicabilityRationale: This candidate defines the threshold between blocking and non-blocking findings, which is core Hosted review classification behavior.
assessments.summary: Add a missing blocking-threshold rule so Hosted reviews distinguish proven present harm from evidence-backed but non-blocking risk.
assessments.impactDescription: This would reduce overclassification of architectural risk, uncertainty, and residual-shape concerns while preserving a path for truly blocking defects.
assessments.currentHostedCoverage: The catalog has no active rule that says when an evidence-backed concern must stay in `ISSUES` versus move to `OBSERVATIONS`; current rules describe defect families but not the general blocking threshold.
assessments.proposedText: Keep a concern in Issues only when current-run evidence proves present blocking harm. If evidence shows only architectural risk, request-shape risk, uncertainty, or another non-blocking mismatch, classify it as an Observation unless another Hosted rule makes that concern blocking by definition.
assessments.selectionRationale: severity 5 fits because the blocking threshold controls whether reviews improperly fail code; frequency 4 fits because many reviews surface mixed-strength concerns; breadth 5 fits because the distinction spans all review surfaces; hostedDetectability 4 fits because available evidence and final classification are inspectable; evidenceStrength 3 fits because the source is precise but not corroborated by existing catalog provenance; falsePositiveRisk 2 fits because the rule still requires concrete evidence before downgrading or escalating; redundancy 2 fits because existing Hosted rules imply severity in spots but do not state this global threshold.

assessments.title: Certain variant-ownership and lifecycle defects are blocking by definition
assessments.applicabilityRationale: This is a specialized but enforceable rule for classifying a concrete implementation defect family that is not represented in the current Hosted catalog.
assessments.summary: Add a rule that treats concrete foreign-variant admission and foreign-variant lifecycle asymmetry as blocking findings.
assessments.impactDescription: This would make Hosted reviews reliably escalate ownership-boundary and delete-symmetry defects on variant-constrained surfaces instead of leaving them to reviewer discretion.
assessments.currentHostedCoverage: No active Hosted rule covers variant ownership boundaries or lifecycle symmetry for generic ID, importer, validator, or lookup paths; the nearest workflow rules such as `IMPL-WF-002B` and `IMPL-WF-002C` address different create/import concerns.
assessments.proposedText: For a variant-constrained managed surface, treat it as a blocking issue when current-run evidence shows that a generic identifier, validator, importer, or lookup path can admit a foreign variant before subtype enforcement, or when delete or another later lifecycle window can still mutate or destroy that foreign variant after earlier windows apply a discriminator guard. Do not downgrade these concrete ownership-boundary or lifecycle-symmetry defects merely because no live foreign-variant fixture ran.
assessments.selectionRationale: severity 5 fits because these defects can let the wrong remote object be adopted or destroyed; frequency 2 fits because the pattern is limited to variant-constrained surfaces; breadth 2 fits because it is narrow to implementation review; hostedDetectability 3 fits because the relevant ID, lookup, and lifecycle guards are inspectable but require cross-window reading; evidenceStrength 3 fits because the candidate describes a specific defect signature even without existing catalog support; falsePositiveRisk 2 fits because the rule still depends on concrete current-run evidence; redundancy 1 fits because the current Hosted catalog does not cover this defect family.

assessments.title: Concrete optional-state drift on user-managed fields is blocking by definition
assessments.applicabilityRationale: This candidate sharpens an existing Hosted implementation rule about state round-tripping rather than introducing a separate rule family.
assessments.summary: Update `IMPL-SCHEMA-001` to explicitly cover user-managed map/object drift and import-ignore evidence as round-trip defects.
assessments.impactDescription: This would make Hosted implementation reviews consistently treat undeclared API rehydration and import-ignore workarounds as actionable state drift instead of leaving them under a vague generic round-trip standard.
assessments.currentHostedCoverage: `IMPL-SCHEMA-001` already says to flag schema or lifecycle behavior that cannot round-trip state, but it does not explicitly call out user-managed map/object drift or import verification ignores as evidence.
assessments.proposedText: Required, optional, computed, ForceNew, defaults, conflicts, and validation must match actual API and lifecycle behavior. Flag schema or state handling that permits invalid requests, rejects valid configuration, or cannot round-trip user-managed state. Treat user-managed map or object fields that can rehydrate undeclared API-added keys or values through Read or Import, or that already require import-ignore workarounds to verify state, as round-trip defects unless current-run evidence proves the field is not user-managed.
assessments.selectionRationale: severity 5 fits because silent user-managed state drift is a correctness defect; frequency 3 fits because the pattern is meaningful but not universal; breadth 3 fits because it mainly affects implementation and import review; hostedDetectability 4 fits because Read and Import behavior plus ignore signals are inspectable in code and tests; evidenceStrength 4 fits because the candidate is a direct refinement of the already-active round-trip rule; falsePositiveRisk 2 fits because the update still requires current-run evidence of user-managed drift; redundancy 4 fits because the behavior belongs inside `IMPL-SCHEMA-001`, which supports an update instead of a separate new rule.

assessments.title: Observations are non-blocking
assessments.applicabilityRationale: This is a general review classification rule for how Hosted reviews should preserve non-blocking concerns.
assessments.summary: Add a global rule that reserves `OBSERVATIONS` for evidence-backed non-blocking concerns.
assessments.impactDescription: This would give Hosted reviews a consistent non-blocking lane for design concerns, uncertainty, and follow-up ideas without forcing them into `ISSUES` or dropping them entirely.
assessments.currentHostedCoverage: No active Hosted rule defines the purpose of `OBSERVATIONS`; current per-surface rules describe what to flag, not where non-blocking findings belong.
assessments.proposedText: Use Observations for evidence-backed design concerns, preferences, uncertainty, or follow-up ideas that are not clearly blocking. If the implementation is acceptable on current evidence, keep the concern out of Issues even when another design could be better.
assessments.selectionRationale: severity 3 fits because the rule shapes output quality more than defect detection; frequency 5 fits because many reviews contain non-blocking concerns; breadth 5 fits because the rule spans all review surfaces; hostedDetectability 5 fits because final classification is directly observable; evidenceStrength 3 fits because the source is clear even without matching catalog provenance; falsePositiveRisk 1 fits because the rule only channels already-evidenced non-blocking concerns; redundancy 1 fits because the current catalog does not define the observation lane.

assessments.title: Evidence-backed non-blocking concerns must remain visible
assessments.applicabilityRationale: This candidate governs retention of legitimate non-blocking findings in Hosted review output.
assessments.summary: Add a rule that prevents Hosted reviews from suppressing evidence-backed observations just because they do not change the overall verdict.
assessments.impactDescription: This would preserve useful non-blocking review signal even when a stronger issue already exists or the reviewer is incentivized to shorten the output.
assessments.currentHostedCoverage: The current catalog has no active rule requiring evidence-backed non-blocking concerns to remain visible once found.
assessments.proposedText: When review work produces an evidence-backed non-blocking concern, keep it visible as an Observation. Do not omit it solely because another issue already blocks merge, it does not change the verdict, or a shorter review would be more convenient.
assessments.selectionRationale: severity 3 fits because lost observations reduce review completeness rather than directly causing code defects; frequency 4 fits because mixed blocking and non-blocking findings are common; breadth 4 fits because the rule applies wherever Hosted reviews surface findings; hostedDetectability 4 fits because omissions can be judged against available evidence and final output; evidenceStrength 3 fits because the source is explicit but not tied to an existing upstream citation; falsePositiveRisk 2 fits because the rule only retains already-evidenced concerns; redundancy 2 fits because it complements but does not duplicate a general observations rule.

assessments.title: Update-shape and residual-state risks default to observations unless concrete harm is proven
assessments.applicabilityRationale: This candidate extends the existing Hosted residual-state rule with a broader review classification case for evidence-backed but not yet destructive update-shape risk.
assessments.summary: Update `IMPL-PATCH-001` so Hosted reviews keep broader residual-state risk visible as an observation even when present destructive harm is not yet proven.
assessments.impactDescription: This would let Hosted implementation reviews surface `PUT` versus `PATCH` and request-shape residual-state risks without forcing reviewers to overclaim proven corruption or stay silent.
assessments.currentHostedCoverage: `IMPL-PATCH-001` covers the concrete stale-state defect caused by omitting a required clear value, but it does not address broader evidence-backed update-shape risk when destructive harm is still unproven.
assessments.proposedText: If Azure PATCH preserves omitted properties, removing Terraform configuration must expand an explicit disabled, empty, or sentinel value that clears the remote feature. Returning `nil` is a defect when SDK serialization would omit the field and preserve stale Azure state. When current-run evidence instead shows only a broader `PUT` versus `PATCH` or request-shape residual-state risk without proven present destructive behavior, keep the concern visible as an observation rather than suppressing it.
assessments.selectionRationale: severity 4 fits because residual-state bugs can leave remote objects in unsafe or surprising states; frequency 3 fits because update-shape mismatches are meaningful but service-specific; breadth 3 fits because the effect is mostly implementation review; hostedDetectability 4 fits because HTTP method choice and request construction are inspectable; evidenceStrength 4 fits because the candidate expands an already-active residual-state rule; falsePositiveRisk 2 fits because the added clause still requires current-run evidence and only changes classification to observation; redundancy 4 fits because the right place is an update to `IMPL-PATCH-001`, not a separate overlapping rule.

assessments.title: Strengths must be factual
assessments.applicabilityRationale: This is a review-output quality rule that is independent of code surface and enforceable from the final Hosted review text.
assessments.summary: Add a lightweight rule that keeps `STRENGTHS` evidence-based instead of generic praise.
assessments.impactDescription: This would improve signal quality in Hosted review output by making positive callouts concrete and auditable.
assessments.currentHostedCoverage: The current Hosted catalog has no rule for when positive findings belong in `STRENGTHS`.
assessments.proposedText: List a Strength only when current-run evidence shows a concrete positive property or safeguard. Do not pad reviews with generic praise.
assessments.selectionRationale: severity 1 fits because this is output-quality guidance rather than defect prevention; frequency 4 fits because many reviews include positive callouts; breadth 4 fits because the rule applies across all review surfaces; hostedDetectability 5 fits because strengths text is directly inspectable; evidenceStrength 3 fits because the candidate is clear even without upstream cross-citation; falsePositiveRisk 1 fits because the rule only blocks empty praise; redundancy 0 fits because the current catalog has no overlapping strengths guidance.

assessments.title: One finding, one classification
assessments.applicabilityRationale: This candidate governs deduplication and severity assignment in Hosted review output, which is independently enforceable.
assessments.summary: Add a rule that prevents the same concern from appearing as both an issue and an observation.
assessments.impactDescription: This would reduce contradictory or padded Hosted reviews and give reviewers a clear downgrade rule when severity is uncertain.
assessments.currentHostedCoverage: No active Hosted rule prevents duplicate classification of the same underlying concern or directs reviewers to choose the lower justified severity when uncertain.
assessments.proposedText: Do not report the same underlying concern as both an Issue and an Observation. When severity is uncertain, use the lower justified classification and explain the evidence that keeps it there.
assessments.selectionRationale: severity 4 fits because duplicate or inflated classification degrades review trust and actionability; frequency 4 fits because related findings often straddle severity boundaries; breadth 5 fits because the rule applies to any surfaced concern; hostedDetectability 4 fits because duplicated output and justification are visible; evidenceStrength 3 fits because the candidate is straightforward but not backed by matching catalog evidence; falsePositiveRisk 1 fits because the rule addresses only clearly duplicated underlying concerns; redundancy 1 fits because no current Hosted rule covers this classification discipline.

assessments.title: Fixes must be deterministic
assessments.applicabilityRationale: This is a review-output rule for how Hosted issues should describe corrections, independent of any one code surface.
assessments.summary: Add a rule that keeps issue remediation concrete instead of presenting multiple competing fixes by default.
assessments.impactDescription: This would make Hosted issues easier to act on and would reduce ambiguity when the user did not ask for solution options.
assessments.currentHostedCoverage: The current catalog has no rule about whether an issue should point to one correction path or present alternatives.
assessments.proposedText: Each Issue should point to one concrete correction path. Do not present multiple alternative fixes unless the user explicitly asked for options.
assessments.selectionRationale: severity 2 fits because this improves actionability more than defect detection; frequency 3 fits because many issues include remediation guidance but not all do; breadth 4 fits because the rule applies to any Hosted issue regardless of surface; hostedDetectability 4 fits because proposed fixes are visible in the review text; evidenceStrength 3 fits because the candidate is precise enough to encode; falsePositiveRisk 2 fits because some situations legitimately support options and the rule preserves that exception; redundancy 1 fits because current Hosted rules do not constrain remediation shape.

assessments.title: Final moderation owner integration boundary
assessments.applicabilityRationale: This candidate assigns responsibility among internal routed skills and contracts rather than defining an independently enforceable Hosted review rule.
assessments.summary: Exclude this candidate because it is workflow ownership metadata, not portable Hosted review guidance.
assessments.impactDescription: Keeping it out avoids coupling the Hosted rule catalog to internal moderator and advocate routing details that are better handled by orchestration.
assessments.currentHostedCoverage: The current Hosted catalog has no routed-owner or skill-boundary surface; it stores review rules, not internal ownership assignments between reviewer roles.
assessments.proposedText: Each surviving concern in the final review output must resolve to exactly one final classification, and supplementary reviewer commentary must not leave competing visible classifications for the same concern.
assessments.selectionRationale: severity 1 fits because missing this from the catalog does not reduce defect detection; frequency 1 fits because it matters only in specialized routed workflows; breadth 1 fits because it does not govern repository content review directly; hostedDetectability 1 fits because ownership boundaries are weakly observable from final review text; evidenceStrength 2 fits because the source is explicit but internal; falsePositiveRisk 5 fits because encoding orchestration ownership as a review rule would misfire in runs that do not use those routed roles; redundancy 3 fits because the concern belongs in workflow configuration rather than the Hosted rule set.

assessments.title: Build a deterministic coverage matrix before findings
assessments.applicabilityRationale: This candidate defines repository-level review coverage planning that the current Hosted catalog does not yet encode.
assessments.summary: Add a repository-level rule that requires a structured, deterministic coverage plan before findings are drafted.
assessments.impactDescription: This would make Hosted reviews more systematic by forcing explicit coverage of file families, control windows, overlap surfaces, and issue-class checks instead of relying on ad hoc reading order.
assessments.currentHostedCoverage: Current Hosted rules define defect checks on implementation, testing, and documentation surfaces, but no active rule requires building a repository-level coverage plan before findings.
assessments.proposedText: Build a deterministic, structured coverage matrix before drafting findings. The matrix must enumerate the applicable implementation families, required lifecycle or control windows, overlap surfaces, and mandatory issue-class checks for the current review scope instead of relying on ad hoc prose or memory.
assessments.selectionRationale: severity 4 fits because missed coverage planning can hide major defects; frequency 4 fits because every nontrivial review needs some coverage strategy; breadth 5 fits because the rule spans repository routing and all substantive review surfaces; hostedDetectability 3 fits because coverage behavior is inferable but less direct than output classification; evidenceStrength 3 fits because the candidate is specific even without existing catalog support; falsePositiveRisk 2 fits because the rule requires structure but not a brittle single implementation; redundancy 1 fits because the current catalog has no comparable repository-level planning rule.

assessments.title: Matrix build and matrix completion are separate phases
assessments.applicabilityRationale: The underlying review-workflow idea is in scope for Hosted guidance, but this candidate depends on a specific matrix lifecycle model that the current catalog does not yet define.
assessments.summary: Defer this candidate because the phase split is useful but depends on a matrix-state model that is not yet represented in the Hosted catalog.
assessments.impactDescription: Deferral avoids locking the catalog to a two-phase completion lifecycle before the broader repository-level review orchestration surface is designed.
assessments.currentHostedCoverage: No active Hosted rule models a coverage-matrix lifecycle, standards-loading checkpoints, or a distinction between initial construction and later completion.
assessments.proposedText: Build the required review coverage plan before drafting findings, but do not mark coverage complete until the repository standards and scoped guidance needed for standards-dependent checks are loaded. Block findings finalization until that completion check succeeds.
assessments.selectionRationale: severity 3 fits because phase discipline can matter for review completeness but is secondary to having a coverage plan at all; frequency 3 fits because only structured multi-step reviews would use it; breadth 4 fits because it touches repository, implementation, testing, and documentation workflow state; hostedDetectability 2 fits because the phased lifecycle is hard to validate without explicit workflow instrumentation; evidenceStrength 2 fits because the source is internal and assumes unmodeled machinery; falsePositiveRisk 4 fits because encoding the split too early could create brittle failures; redundancy 3 fits because a more general coverage-planning rule can land first while this lifecycle detail waits.

assessments.title: Changed implementation files use a fixed review order
assessments.applicabilityRationale: This candidate establishes a repository-level method for systematically reviewing changed implementation files and related windows.
assessments.summary: Add a deterministic implementation-file review order so Hosted coverage of lifecycle windows is consistent.
assessments.impactDescription: This would reduce drift in cold-review behavior by ensuring Hosted reviews inspect the same control windows and companion surfaces in a stable order.
assessments.currentHostedCoverage: The current Hosted catalog contains implementation defect rules, but no active rule specifies review order across changed `internal/**/*.go` files or across lifecycle/control windows.
assessments.proposedText: For changed `internal/**/*.go` implementation files, review applicable surfaces in a fixed order: sort files lexically, then inspect Importer, Create, Read, Update, Delete, CustomizeDiff, validation or ownership helpers, and companion registration, tests, docs, and association surfaces when present. Mark missing windows not applicable instead of reordering around them.
assessments.selectionRationale: severity 3 fits because review-order mistakes mainly cause missed evidence rather than direct false findings; frequency 4 fits because most implementation reviews traverse multiple lifecycle windows; breadth 3 fits because the rule is specific to implementation routing; hostedDetectability 3 fits because read order is somewhat inferable from workflow behavior; evidenceStrength 3 fits because the candidate provides a concrete deterministic method; falsePositiveRisk 2 fits because the rule still allows not-applicable windows instead of forcing nonexistent paths; redundancy 1 fits because no current Hosted rule defines this review order.

assessments.title: New resources require overlap and ownership scans
assessments.applicabilityRationale: This is a repository-level review coverage rule for new managed surfaces that can overlap unchanged siblings.
assessments.summary: Add a rule that forces Hosted reviews of new resources to inspect unchanged overlapping sibling surfaces.
assessments.impactDescription: This would close a common blind spot where a new resource can conflict with existing resources, data sources, or helpers that are not changed in the diff.
assessments.currentHostedCoverage: No active Hosted rule requires review of unchanged overlap surfaces when a brand-new managed surface is added under `internal/**/*.go`.
assessments.proposedText: When a review adds a brand-new managed surface under `internal/**/*.go`, inspect overlapping unchanged sibling surfaces that can manage or describe the same remote object. Materialize those overlap surfaces as explicit coverage entries instead of assuming the diff alone is sufficient.
assessments.selectionRationale: severity 5 fits because missing overlap review can hide ownership and destructive-behavior defects; frequency 2 fits because it only triggers on brand-new managed surfaces; breadth 3 fits because it affects repository routing and implementation inspection; hostedDetectability 3 fits because overlapping anchors are inspectable but require cross-file reasoning; evidenceStrength 3 fits because the candidate states a concrete and reviewable obligation; falsePositiveRisk 2 fits because the rule is limited to plausible overlap surfaces; redundancy 1 fits because the current Hosted catalog does not require this broader scan.

assessments.title: Variant-constrained ownership surfaces prioritize ownership and lifecycle first
assessments.applicabilityRationale: This candidate describes a specialized but enforceable first-pass review priority for a concrete implementation defect family that the Hosted catalog currently misses.
assessments.summary: Add a rule that makes ownership-boundary and lifecycle-symmetry checks the first-pass priority on variant-constrained managed surfaces.
assessments.impactDescription: This would steer Hosted reviews toward the highest-risk implementation defects on discriminator-bound resources before lower-severity polish findings consume attention.
assessments.currentHostedCoverage: The current Hosted catalog has no rule that prioritizes ownership-boundary and lifecycle-symmetry analysis for variant-constrained surfaces, and no active rule says generic resolution before subtype enforcement must immediately materialize a concern.
assessments.proposedText: For a new or materially changed variant-constrained managed surface, check ownership-boundary and lifecycle-symmetry behavior before secondary concerns. Explicitly verify whether import, ID validation, lookup, read, update, and delete can admit, mutate, or destroy foreign variants; if generic resolution reaches a foreign variant before subtype enforcement, materialize that concern immediately at the justified classification.
assessments.selectionRationale: severity 5 fits because ownership-boundary and lifecycle defects can target the wrong objects; frequency 2 fits because the rule is limited to variant-constrained surfaces; breadth 2 fits because it is a narrow implementation-review priority rule; hostedDetectability 3 fits because the relevant lifecycle and lookup paths are inspectable but require synthesis; evidenceStrength 3 fits because the candidate supplies a coherent trigger and priority rule; falsePositiveRisk 2 fits because the rule still demands concrete evidence from the inspected paths; redundancy 2 fits because it complements, rather than duplicates, the proposed blocker-classification rule for the same defect family.

assessments.title: Provider reviews have mandatory issue-class checks
assessments.applicabilityRationale: This candidate defines cross-surface review methodology for ensuring Hosted reviews execute the full set of relevant issue-class checks and retain each supported concern.
assessments.summary: Add a cross-surface rule that requires explicit completion of applicable issue-class checks and forbids suppressing evidence-backed concerns because a stronger one exists.
assessments.impactDescription: This would make Hosted reviews more complete by requiring coverage of recurring provider defect families and by preserving each justified concern at its proper classification.
assessments.currentHostedCoverage: Existing `IMPL-*`, `TEST-*`, and `DOCS-*` rules encode many individual defect families, but no active Hosted rule requires the reviewer to execute the full applicable set or keep every supported concern visible once found.
assessments.proposedText: For changed provider resources, data sources, and list resources, explicitly complete the applicable issue-class checks for ownership overlap, lifecycle-gating symmetry, destructive-path gating, poller terminal failures, validator-to-doc parity, companion artifacts, list-resource exceptions, companion test or docs coverage, residual-state behavior, optional-state drift, and docs-example correctness when docs change. Keep each evidence-backed concern visible at its justified classification instead of suppressing it because another concern is stronger.
assessments.selectionRationale: severity 5 fits because omitted issue-class checks can miss blocking defects entirely; frequency 4 fits because provider reviews routinely span several defect families; breadth 5 fits because the rule crosses implementation, testing, documentation, and review output behavior; hostedDetectability 3 fits because completion discipline is somewhat inferable but not as direct as single-finding rules; evidenceStrength 3 fits because the candidate aligns multiple existing rule families without inventing new defect semantics; falsePositiveRisk 2 fits because the rule only requires explicit treatment of applicable checks; redundancy 2 fits because current surface rules supply the defect content but not this coordinating obligation.

assessments.title: Active-file bias is forbidden for initial routing
assessments.applicabilityRationale: This candidate depends on editor and search-result context that the Hosted rule catalog does not receive or control as part of its review inputs.
assessments.summary: Exclude this candidate because it is environment-specific routing hygiene, not portable Hosted review guidance.
assessments.impactDescription: Keeping it out avoids adding a rule that references active-editor state unavailable to many Hosted runs and not encoded anywhere in the catalog.
assessments.currentHostedCoverage: The current Hosted catalog has no editor-context surface and no mechanism for observing active-file or search-result ordering state.
assessments.proposedText: Determine initial review scope from changed content and required coverage, not from the active editor file, search-result order, or PR wording. The active file may guide navigation only after the required scope is established.
assessments.selectionRationale: severity 1 fits because omission from the catalog does not reduce defect-detection semantics; frequency 1 fits because the condition arises only in interactive editor-driven workflows; breadth 1 fits because it does not govern repository content review directly; hostedDetectability 0 fits because Hosted rules cannot observe active-editor state from the catalog inputs; evidenceStrength 2 fits because the source is explicit but environment-bound; falsePositiveRisk 5 fits because any encoded rule would be hard to apply reliably without the missing context; redundancy 2 fits because general deterministic coverage rules can stand without importing this editor-specific detail.

assessments.title: Family grouping prefers explicit code anchors over filename intuition
assessments.applicabilityRationale: This candidate defines repository-level grouping logic for related implementation surfaces, which is relevant to Hosted review coverage.
assessments.summary: Add a repository-level rule that groups related files by explicit code anchors instead of filename intuition alone.
assessments.impactDescription: This would improve Hosted review coverage of unchanged but related surfaces by using shared parsers, helpers, registrations, and SDK methods to identify real family boundaries.
assessments.currentHostedCoverage: The current Hosted catalog has no active rule for how to group files into a review family or when unchanged overlap surfaces must be added based on explicit anchors.
assessments.proposedText: Group related files by explicit code anchors such as shared ID parsers, validation helpers, registration entries, ownership helpers, ARM ID types, and shared SDK methods or resource paths that manage the same remote object; do not rely on filename intuition alone. When those anchors show an unchanged overlap surface, add it to review coverage explicitly.
assessments.selectionRationale: severity 4 fits because bad family grouping can cause important related surfaces to be skipped; frequency 3 fits because the need appears regularly but not in every review; breadth 3 fits because it primarily affects repository routing and implementation analysis; hostedDetectability 3 fits because shared anchors are inspectable but require synthesis across files; evidenceStrength 3 fits because the candidate gives concrete anchor types; falsePositiveRisk 2 fits because the rule prefers explicit code evidence over loose intuition; redundancy 1 fits because the current Hosted catalog does not already define grouping by anchors.

assessments.title: Findings cannot freeze before coverage completion
assessments.applicabilityRationale: The semantic goal is in scope for Hosted review workflow guidance, but this candidate is tightly coupled to matrix-state fields and handoff bookkeeping that the current catalog does not model.
assessments.summary: Defer this candidate because its completeness and linkage requirements depend on unmodeled coverage-matrix and handoff-record data structures.
assessments.impactDescription: Deferral avoids adding brittle Hosted wording that references workflow state the current catalog cannot define, persist, or validate consistently.
assessments.currentHostedCoverage: The current Hosted catalog has no active rule for matrix completion, emitted-record linkage, or hard-stop behavior before final findings are frozen.
assessments.proposedText: Do not freeze findings or final review output until all required coverage and issue-class checks are complete from current-run evidence. Every evidence-backed concern must appear in the findings set or carry an explicit evidence-backed not-applicable justification.
assessments.selectionRationale: severity 4 fits because premature freeze can hide missed concerns across the whole review; frequency 3 fits because the problem mainly affects multi-stage structured reviews; breadth 5 fits because the candidate spans repository coverage, output gating, and all substantive review surfaces; hostedDetectability 1 fits because the referenced linkage and completion state is not visible in the current catalog model; evidenceStrength 2 fits because the source is internal and assumes workflow machinery that is absent today; falsePositiveRisk 4 fits because encoding it now would create brittle, hard-to-verify obligations; redundancy 3 fits because simpler coverage-planning rules can land first while this bookkeeping-heavy completion rule waits.

assessments.title: Router validation sub-phase is the canonical completion gate
assessments.applicabilityRationale: This governs an internal router orchestration step and hard-stop behavior for a multi-phase review runtime, not a reviewer-facing Hosted rule that can be enforced from repository evidence or final review output alone.
assessments.summary: Exclude this candidate because it specifies workflow-engine control flow rather than reusable Hosted review guidance.
assessments.impactDescription: Adding it would couple the catalog to one router implementation and make enforcement depend on hidden sub-phase mechanics instead of observable review behavior.
assessments.currentHostedCoverage: The current Hosted catalog intentionally contains repository and surface review rules, not internal router completion-gate requirements.
assessments.proposedText: Before findings advance to specialized review passes or final output, run one deterministic completion check that confirms required coverage and issue-class review are complete from current-run evidence. If that check cannot confirm completion, stop the review instead of continuing on prose-only judgment.
assessments.selectionRationale: severity 3 fits because premature continuation can matter but the harm is indirect; frequency 2 fits because this only appears in routed review flows; breadth 2 fits because it affects a narrow orchestration layer; hostedDetectability 1 fits because a hidden validation sub-phase is not reliably observable from review evidence; evidenceStrength 2 fits because the rule is clear but implementation-specific; falsePositiveRisk 4 fits because enforcement would require guessing unseen runtime behavior; redundancy 3 fits because user-visible coverage safeguards can be handled without encoding this router mechanism.

assessments.title: Router owns post-review handoff-linkage validation before routed roles
assessments.applicabilityRationale: This candidate defines internal handoff bookkeeping and linkage validation for routed-role orchestration, which is not an externally reviewable Hosted rule on repository content or final findings.
assessments.summary: Exclude this candidate because it is an internal multi-role coordination contract, not Hosted review guidance.
assessments.impactDescription: Including it would bind the catalog to a specific routed-review architecture and internal record-linkage model instead of a stable reviewer obligation.
assessments.currentHostedCoverage: The current Hosted catalog does not encode router-owned handoff synchronization or emitted-record linkage checks.
assessments.proposedText: Before secondary review passes or final synthesis, verify that every evidence-backed concern from the primary review is preserved as a distinct finding or carries an explicit evidence-backed not-applicable justification. Do not collapse separate concern families into one summary when current-run evidence supports separate findings.
assessments.selectionRationale: severity 4 fits because dropped concerns between passes are serious; frequency 2 fits because the scenario only exists in routed review workflows; breadth 2 fits because the rule targets a narrow orchestration stage; hostedDetectability 1 fits because record-linkage validation is largely hidden from final output; evidenceStrength 2 fits because the candidate is detailed but tied to one runtime design; falsePositiveRisk 4 fits because Hosted enforcement would have to infer missing internal handoff state; redundancy 2 fits because the catalog has no direct overlap but broader fresh-evidence rules cover the user-visible risk better.

assessments.title: Routed roles start only after coverage completion
assessments.applicabilityRationale: The rule is about sequencing internal routed roles in a particular review workflow, not about a repository-facing or reviewer-visible Hosted standard that can be checked independently of that runtime.
assessments.summary: Exclude this candidate because it codifies internal role-start sequencing rather than a standalone Hosted review rule.
assessments.impactDescription: Adding it would overfit the catalog to one multi-role execution model instead of focusing on observable review-scope completeness requirements.
assessments.currentHostedCoverage: Current Hosted rules describe what to review and how to ground findings, but they do not prescribe when hidden routed roles may start.
assessments.proposedText: Do not start specialized review passes or freeze output on a partial audit. Complete required coverage first, or stop if current-run evidence cannot support completion.
assessments.selectionRationale: severity 3 fits because partial handoff can degrade review quality but is a step removed from the final defect report; frequency 2 fits because routed-role sequencing is not universal; breadth 2 fits because it applies to one orchestration pattern; hostedDetectability 2 fits because partial coverage may sometimes be inferred but role start timing usually is not; evidenceStrength 3 fits because the failure condition is clear; falsePositiveRisk 4 fits because Hosted enforcement would still need to infer internal workflow order; redundancy 3 fits because repository-scope rules can cover the public outcome without codifying routed-role timing.

assessments.title: Do not guess when evidence is required
assessments.applicabilityRationale: This is a cross-surface evidence rule for review correctness and finding classification, and it applies equally to repository, implementation, testing, and documentation review.
assessments.summary: Add a general anti-fabrication evidence rule so Hosted review guidance stops unsupported correctness and compliance claims across all review types.
assessments.impactDescription: This closes a core review-integrity gap by requiring findings to stay evidence-backed and by steering uncertain cases toward clarification or lower-confidence framing instead of asserted defects.
assessments.currentHostedCoverage: Current Hosted evidence rules are surface-specific, such as Azure-model verification and docs accuracy checks, but no general rule bars unsupported review claims across all surfaces.
assessments.proposedText: Report a correctness or compliance issue only when current-run evidence supports it. If evidence is insufficient, state that it is unproven, request clarification, or downgrade it instead of asserting a defect.
assessments.selectionRationale: severity 5 fits because unsupported findings directly mislead users; frequency 4 fits because evidence gaps recur in normal review; breadth 5 fits because every review surface depends on this safeguard; hostedDetectability 4 fits because unsupported assertions are usually visible in the finding and surrounding evidence trail; evidenceStrength 5 fits because the candidate states a clear and enforceable boundary; falsePositiveRisk 1 fits because the rule only blocks claims lacking support; redundancy 1 fits because no current Hosted rule provides this general cross-surface protection.

assessments.title: Verify display artifacts before flagging formatting or encoding issues
assessments.applicabilityRationale: This is a review-evidence safeguard for any surface where wrapped terminal output, diff truncation, or chat rendering can misrepresent actual file content.
assessments.summary: Add a rule that requires direct file verification before reporting formatting, encoding, or line-break corruption caused by display artifacts.
assessments.impactDescription: The rule reduces false findings that come from transport noise instead of repository defects, especially for syntax- and formatting-adjacent comments.
assessments.currentHostedCoverage: The current Hosted catalog has no rule that distinguishes real file corruption from wrapped, truncated, or rendered output artifacts.
assessments.proposedText: Before reporting syntax, formatting, encoding, or line-break corruption, verify the underlying file content rather than relying on wrapped, truncated, or chat-rendered output.
assessments.selectionRationale: severity 3 fits because these mistakes waste review cycles more than they cause deep semantic harm; frequency 3 fits because display artifacts are common enough in tool-driven review; breadth 4 fits because the problem can affect any file type; hostedDetectability 3 fits because the mismatch is usually checkable but not always obvious from the report alone; evidenceStrength 4 fits because the candidate has a concrete trigger and action; falsePositiveRisk 1 fits because the rule asks for verification before escalation; redundancy 1 fits because no current Hosted rule covers this transport-artifact failure mode.

assessments.title: Attribute policies to real sources
assessments.applicabilityRationale: This candidate governs when a reviewer may treat a convention as mandatory, which is a core review-classification rule that spans all Hosted surfaces.
assessments.summary: Add a cross-surface rule that prevents reviewers from inventing mandatory policy where the repository or Hosted guidance only supports a preference.
assessments.impactDescription: This improves review accuracy by separating enforceable requirements from style opinions and by reducing unsupported 'must' language in findings.
assessments.currentHostedCoverage: Current Hosted rules define many specific requirements, but no general rule requires reviewers to ground claimed mandates in a real source or established pattern.
assessments.proposedText: Do not present a style, implementation, or testing preference as mandatory unless an active Hosted rule, current contributor guidance, repository evidence, or an established same-surface pattern makes it required.
assessments.selectionRationale: severity 4 fits because invented mandates skew review decisions and user trust; frequency 4 fits because policy overstatement is a recurring review failure mode; breadth 5 fits because it applies across all Hosted surfaces; hostedDetectability 3 fits because unsupported 'must' language is often visible but source absence can require extra checking; evidenceStrength 5 fits because the candidate draws a precise source-attribution line; falsePositiveRisk 2 fits because some conventions rely on patterns rather than single documents; redundancy 1 fits because the current catalog lacks a general source-attribution safeguard.

assessments.title: Discover contributor-guidance paths before claiming absence
assessments.applicabilityRationale: This is a repository-scope evidence rule because it governs where reviewers must look for contributor guidance before concluding that no such guidance exists.
assessments.summary: Add a repository rule that requires checking the workspace's common contributor-guidance paths before claiming the repo has no contributor instructions.
assessments.impactDescription: The rule reduces false claims about missing guidance and aligns review behavior with the catalog's own use of `contributing/README.md` as an authoritative source.
assessments.currentHostedCoverage: The current Hosted catalog cites `contributing/README.md` as a source, but it has no rule requiring reviewers to search that path before declaring contributor guidance absent.
assessments.proposedText: Before claiming repository contributor guidance is absent, check the common guidance entrypoints used in this workspace, including `CONTRIBUTING.md` and `contributing/README.md` when present.
assessments.selectionRationale: severity 2 fits because missed guidance usually causes secondary mistakes rather than direct code defects; frequency 3 fits because guidance-path assumptions recur in repository review; breadth 2 fits because the rule is repository-setup specific; hostedDetectability 4 fits because the checked and missed paths are concrete; evidenceStrength 5 fits because the candidate names exact locations with existing catalog support; falsePositiveRisk 1 fits because the obligation is a simple discovery step; redundancy 1 fits because no current Hosted repository rule covers this lookup requirement.

assessments.title: Perform post-tool verification silently
assessments.applicabilityRationale: This governs how much internal process narration appears in reviewer output, not a substantive repository or evidence standard that needs to live in the Hosted rule catalog.
assessments.summary: Exclude this candidate because it is output-style guidance about process narration rather than an independently enforceable review rule.
assessments.impactDescription: Adding it would mix response-presentation preferences into the semantic rule catalog and create style policing that is separate from finding quality.
assessments.currentHostedCoverage: The current Hosted catalog focuses on enforceable review obligations, not whether intermediate verification steps are described in the final response.
assessments.proposedText: Final review output must present evidence-backed conclusions and only the supporting evidence needed to justify them. Do not include narration of intermediate verification steps unless that process detail is itself necessary evidence.
assessments.selectionRationale: severity 1 fits because narration style rarely changes review correctness; frequency 2 fits because verbose process reporting is occasional, not constant; breadth 2 fits because it concerns response presentation rather than all review logic; hostedDetectability 5 fits because visible narration is easy to spot; evidenceStrength 4 fits because the candidate is explicit; falsePositiveRisk 3 fits because it can be unclear where useful evidence explanation ends and prohibited narration begins; redundancy 2 fits because runtime style instructions can handle this better than the Hosted semantic catalog.

assessments.title: Every invocation is a fresh audit run
assessments.applicabilityRationale: This is a foundational review-evidence rule that applies to every Hosted review invocation regardless of surface because it defines what counts as valid current-run evidence.
assessments.summary: Add a cross-surface fresh-audit rule that bars reuse of prior review output, old command results, and stale classifications as current evidence.
assessments.impactDescription: This closes a major integrity gap by forcing every review to be grounded in commands, diffs, and file reads from the current run rather than conversational carry-over.
assessments.currentHostedCoverage: The current Hosted catalog contains surface-specific evidence rules, but no general rule requires each invocation to rebuild its evidence base from the current run.
assessments.proposedText: Treat every review invocation as a fresh audit. Base findings only on commands, diffs, and file reads gathered in the current run, and do not reuse prior review output as evidence.
assessments.selectionRationale: severity 5 fits because stale evidence can invalidate an entire review; frequency 4 fits because repeated invocations and carry-over temptations are common; breadth 5 fits because the rule governs every Hosted surface; hostedDetectability 4 fits because reused output and missing current-run evidence are often visible in the review trace; evidenceStrength 5 fits because the candidate states a crisp evidentiary boundary; falsePositiveRisk 1 fits because the rule simply requires current-run support; redundancy 1 fits because no current Hosted rule establishes this general fresh-audit requirement.

assessments.title: Describe only current-run facts
assessments.applicabilityRationale: The candidate addresses user-visible evidence phrasing and is relevant to Hosted review output, but it overlaps heavily with the broader fresh-audit evidence rule.
assessments.summary: Defer this as a separate Hosted rule because its intended safeguard is better consolidated into the broader fresh-audit requirement than split into a wording-specific rule now.
assessments.impactDescription: A standalone ban on carry-over words would fragment evidence guidance and risk style-only enforcement before the broader current-run evidence rule is settled.
assessments.currentHostedCoverage: No current Hosted rule directly bans comparative carry-over wording, but the underlying problem is a narrower expression of the missing fresh-audit rule addressed by REVIEW-EVID-006.
assessments.proposedText: Describe findings only from current-run repository evidence. Do not rely on prior review state or reuse prior review body text in place of a fresh current-run explanation.
assessments.selectionRationale: severity 3 fits because misleading carry-over wording can distort findings but usually follows a larger evidence problem; frequency 3 fits because comparative language appears regularly in repeated reviews; breadth 4 fits because the wording issue spans multiple surfaces; hostedDetectability 5 fits because the prohibited phrasing is plainly visible in output; evidenceStrength 4 fits because the candidate is specific about the failure mode; falsePositiveRisk 3 fits because some comparative terms may appear in valid quotations or narrow contexts; redundancy 5 fits because a broader fresh-audit rule already captures most of the substantive risk.

assessments.title: Do not reuse prior review body text
assessments.applicabilityRationale: This candidate is relevant to Hosted review output integrity, but it is a narrower manifestation of the broader fresh-audit evidence requirement.
assessments.summary: Defer this candidate because a copy-specific rule should be evaluated only after deciding the broader fresh-audit rule that already addresses reused prior review material.
assessments.impactDescription: Adding a separate anti-reuse text rule now would duplicate evidence-integrity guidance and make enforcement more about phrasing provenance than review substance.
assessments.currentHostedCoverage: Current Hosted rules do not directly forbid prior-body reuse, but the underlying concern substantially overlaps the missing fresh-audit rule covered by REVIEW-EVID-006.
assessments.proposedText: Do not reuse, quote, paraphrase, or summarize a prior review body as the current review output, even when the change set and findings are unchanged. For each invocation, write the review body from current-run evidence and the active prompt or template requirements.
assessments.selectionRationale: severity 3 fits because reused text can misstate current evidence but usually signals a broader stale-evidence failure; frequency 2 fits because literal or paraphrased body reuse is less common than general carry-over; breadth 4 fits because it can affect any review surface; hostedDetectability 5 fits because repeated body text is highly observable; evidenceStrength 4 fits because the candidate defines a concrete prohibition; falsePositiveRisk 2 fits because most clear reuse is easy to distinguish from legitimate repeated conclusions; redundancy 5 fits because the broader fresh-audit rule already covers the substantive problem more cleanly.

assessments.title: Do not use helper scripts for trivial deterministic checks
assessments.applicabilityRationale: This is mainly tool-choice and efficiency guidance for the reviewing agent, not a stable semantic review rule about repository defects or evidence validity.
assessments.summary: Exclude this candidate because it regulates reviewer execution style rather than a Hosted review obligation tied to code or documentation quality.
assessments.impactDescription: Adding it would overconstrain legitimate validation choices and mix tool-efficiency policy into the semantic catalog.
assessments.currentHostedCoverage: The current Hosted catalog constrains evidence integrity and review conclusions, not whether the reviewer used a short script to confirm an otherwise obvious fact.
assessments.proposedText: When the diff or file content directly proves a factual claim, cite that repository evidence directly instead of treating extra script execution as required proof. Run additional tooling only when the claim cannot be established reliably from the reviewed content alone or the user explicitly requests executable validation.
assessments.selectionRationale: severity 1 fits because script choice usually affects efficiency more than review correctness; frequency 3 fits because trivial checks are common; breadth 3 fits because the behavior can arise across many surfaces; hostedDetectability 4 fits because helper-script use is often visible in the review trace; evidenceStrength 3 fits because the candidate's examples are clear but the boundary around 'trivial' is subjective; falsePositiveRisk 4 fits because legitimate edge-case validation could be mislabeled as prohibited; redundancy 2 fits because runtime operating instructions handle tool efficiency better than Hosted rules.

assessments.title: Do not invent prerequisite or validation scripts
assessments.applicabilityRationale: This is a cross-surface evidence-integrity rule because invented local scripts or entrypoints create unsupported evidence paths regardless of whether the review targets repository, implementation, testing, or documentation.
assessments.summary: Add a rule that forbids guessed repo-local validation scripts and requires reviewers to use named or directly supported evidence paths instead.
assessments.impactDescription: The rule prevents fabricated prerequisite steps and keeps review evidence grounded in the prompt, repository guidance, or user-provided commands.
assessments.currentHostedCoverage: Current Hosted rules do not generally restrict reviewers from inventing repo-local helper entrypoints when gathering evidence.
assessments.proposedText: Do not invent or execute repo-local validation scripts or helper entrypoints unless the prompt, repository guidance, or the user explicitly names them. If no approved script exists, use direct supported evidence paths instead of guessed commands.
assessments.selectionRationale: severity 4 fits because guessed scripts can produce invalid evidence paths and wrong conclusions; frequency 3 fits because repos often contain many plausible but unstated helper names; breadth 5 fits because the problem spans all Hosted review surfaces; hostedDetectability 4 fits because invented commands are usually explicit in the review trace; evidenceStrength 4 fits because the candidate gives a clear allowlist basis; falsePositiveRisk 2 fits because explicit user or repo guidance still leaves room for legitimate exceptions; redundancy 1 fits because no current Hosted rule covers invented validation entrypoints.

assessments.title: Review the full change-set in scope
assessments.applicabilityRationale: This is a repository-scope review coverage rule because it defines the minimum file set that a Hosted review must actually consider.
assessments.summary: Add a repository rule requiring every file in the chosen review scope to be considered instead of silently skipped.
assessments.impactDescription: This closes a major coverage gap by making missed files an explicit review failure unless an allowed exception is disclosed.
assessments.currentHostedCoverage: The current Hosted catalog assumes correct scoping but has no explicit repository rule that forbids silently skipping files inside the selected diff.
assessments.proposedText: Consider every file in the selected review scope. Do not silently skip changed files except for explicitly disclosed non-actionable or self-review exceptions.
assessments.selectionRationale: severity 5 fits because skipped files can hide critical defects entirely; frequency 4 fits because scope handling is part of every review; breadth 4 fits because the rule governs repository coverage across all surface types; hostedDetectability 4 fits because omitted paths can usually be compared with the selected diff; evidenceStrength 5 fits because the candidate states a clear complete-coverage requirement; falsePositiveRisk 1 fits because disclosed exceptions remain allowed; redundancy 1 fits because the current catalog lacks an explicit full-scope repository rule.

assessments.title: Classify changed files accurately
assessments.applicabilityRationale: This candidate applies to repository-scope review because correct file-status classification affects both review coverage and how the changed set is described to the user.
assessments.summary: Add a repository rule that requires accurate reporting of added, modified, deleted, staged, and untracked files in the review scope.
assessments.impactDescription: This prevents misleading scope summaries that can hide deleted files, mishandle untracked content, or distort what evidence the review actually covered.
assessments.currentHostedCoverage: Current Hosted rules do not explicitly require accurate file-status classification when establishing or describing repository review scope.
assessments.proposedText: Describe added, modified, deleted, staged, and untracked files accurately when reporting review scope; do not collapse deleted files into modified scope or treat untracked files as tracked additions.
assessments.selectionRationale: severity 3 fits because status misclassification can materially skew scope understanding without always invalidating the whole review; frequency 3 fits because file-state reporting is common in local and committed reviews; breadth 3 fits because the rule is repository-focused rather than surface-specific; hostedDetectability 4 fits because Git state usually makes misclassification easy to prove; evidenceStrength 5 fits because the candidate names concrete statuses and mistakes; falsePositiveRisk 1 fits because the rule compares directly against observable file state; redundancy 1 fits because no current Hosted repository rule covers accurate status classification.

assessments.title: Self-review recursion prevention is explicit
assessments.applicabilityRationale: This is a repository-scope review exception rule because it defines the only file-specific self-review skip and requires explicit disclosure of that skip.
assessments.summary: Add a narrow repository rule that allows skipping the active review prompt file only when that exact skip is disclosed.
assessments.impactDescription: The rule prevents broad self-review avoidance from turning into silent scope loss while still permitting the practical prompt-file exception.
assessments.currentHostedCoverage: The current Hosted catalog has no explicit rule for handling the active prompt or instruction file when it appears in the reviewed change-set.
assessments.proposedText: If the active review prompt or instruction file is itself in scope, skip only that file and disclose the skip explicitly instead of suppressing broader review coverage.
assessments.selectionRationale: severity 2 fits because this is a narrow coverage exception rather than a common defect source; frequency 2 fits because the active prompt file is only sometimes under review; breadth 2 fits because it applies to a specific repository scenario; hostedDetectability 5 fits because the file path and any disclosure are plainly visible; evidenceStrength 5 fits because the allowed and disallowed behaviors are explicit; falsePositiveRisk 1 fits because the exception is tightly bounded; redundancy 1 fits because no current Hosted rule handles this self-review edge case.

assessments.title: Local review scope should prefer the active local diff
assessments.applicabilityRationale: This candidate defines how Hosted local review should select repository scope from unstaged, staged, and untracked changes, which is a repository-level rule.
assessments.summary: Add a repository rule that makes local review scope deterministic across unstaged, staged, and untracked changes and fails closed on an empty workspace.
assessments.impactDescription: This prevents reviewing the wrong local diff, missing untracked files that should be inspected, or emitting a normal review when there is nothing to review.
assessments.currentHostedCoverage: The current Hosted catalog has no repository rule that defines local-review scope precedence or empty-workspace failure behavior.
assessments.proposedText: For local review, use the non-empty unstaged tracked diff as the primary scope; if it is empty, fall back to the staged tracked diff; inspect reviewed untracked files directly; and fail closed when no tracked or untracked changes exist.
assessments.selectionRationale: severity 4 fits because wrong scope selection can invalidate the review; frequency 4 fits because local review starts with these scope choices every time; breadth 4 fits because the rule governs repository coverage regardless of file type; hostedDetectability 5 fits because diff presence and fallback order are concrete and checkable; evidenceStrength 5 fits because the candidate provides a deterministic decision table; falsePositiveRisk 2 fits because some specialized review requests may intentionally override the default order; redundancy 1 fits because the current Hosted catalog does not define local scope precedence.

assessments.title: Committed review scope must prefer authoritative PR context
assessments.applicabilityRationale: This is a repository-scope rule because it determines how Hosted committed review establishes authoritative changed-file scope and what to do when PR context is missing, conflicting, or locally unavailable.
assessments.summary: Add a repository rule that requires committed review to prefer authoritative PR file scope, reject non-authoritative local spill artifacts, and fail closed on conflicting or unavailable scoped files.
assessments.impactDescription: This materially improves committed-review correctness by preventing branch-drift scope, cached-artifact misuse, and silent omission of scoped PR files that are missing locally.
assessments.currentHostedCoverage: The current Hosted catalog has no repository rule for authoritative PR scope resolution, conflict handling, or fail-closed local file availability checks in committed review.
assessments.proposedText: When authoritative pull request metadata exists, use that PR changed-file set as committed-review scope, ignore summaries, browser links, spilled local artifacts, and automatic local `gh` fallbacks as initial PR scope, and fail closed if explicit PR contexts conflict without an override. Fall back to `origin/main...HEAD` only when no authoritative PR context exists or the user explicitly requests branch-wide review, and fail closed if a non-deleted scoped file cannot be inspected from local committed evidence.
assessments.selectionRationale: severity 5 fits because wrong committed scope can invalidate the entire review set; frequency 3 fits because authoritative PR context is common but not universal; breadth 4 fits because the rule governs repository scoping for all committed review surfaces; hostedDetectability 4 fits because chosen scope sources and missing files are usually observable in the run; evidenceStrength 5 fits because the candidate defines clear priority and fail-closed conditions; falsePositiveRisk 2 fits because some environments expose PR context differently, so the rule needs careful application; redundancy 1 fits because the current Hosted catalog has no comparable committed-scope rule.

assessments.title: Vendored third-party files are non-actionable review scope
assessments.applicabilityRationale: This is a repository-scope review rule because it defines how to handle vendored third-party files when they appear in the selected diff.
assessments.summary: Add a repository rule that treats `vendor/**` files as non-actionable third-party scope unless repository guidance says otherwise, while still requiring disclosure.
assessments.impactDescription: This reduces noisy findings against vendored code and redirects review effort toward the actionable first-party change that introduced the vendor update.
assessments.currentHostedCoverage: The current Hosted catalog has no repository rule explaining how vendored third-party files should be counted, disclosed, and excluded from direct remediation findings.
assessments.proposedText: Treat `vendor/**` files as non-actionable third-party scope unless repository guidance says otherwise: count and disclose them, do not tell contributors to hand-edit vendored content, and trace defects to the actionable non-vendored change that introduced the vendor update.
assessments.selectionRationale: severity 3 fits because vendored-file findings often waste review effort rather than corrupting all conclusions; frequency 2 fits because vendor changes are intermittent; breadth 3 fits because the rule affects repository scope handling across languages; hostedDetectability 5 fits because vendored paths are explicit; evidenceStrength 5 fits because the candidate names a concrete path class and required behavior; falsePositiveRisk 1 fits because repository guidance can still override the default; redundancy 1 fits because the current Hosted catalog has no vendored-scope handling rule.

assessments.title: Intermediate findings use one shared semantic shape
assessments.applicabilityRationale: This candidate prescribes an internal intermediate-record schema for routed-role handoff, not a reviewer-facing Hosted rule that can be enforced from repository evidence or final review output.
assessments.summary: Exclude this candidate because it defines internal workflow data shape rather than reusable Hosted review guidance.
assessments.impactDescription: Adding it would turn the semantic rule catalog into an orchestration-schema contract and bind rule maintenance to one internal handoff format.
assessments.currentHostedCoverage: The current Hosted catalog does not encode internal routed-role record schemas or require compliance with handoff JSON shapes.
assessments.proposedText: Maintain each finding in one canonical structured form that preserves scope, evidence, reasoning, confidence, classification, and visibility until final output. Do not reduce active findings to unlabeled prose that loses those semantics.
assessments.selectionRationale: severity 2 fits because schema consistency helps workflow quality but is not directly a repository review defect; frequency 2 fits because the issue only exists in routed-review systems; breadth 2 fits because it targets a narrow internal handoff layer; hostedDetectability 1 fits because intermediate record shape is not generally visible in final review output; evidenceStrength 3 fits because the schema requirements are explicit; falsePositiveRisk 4 fits because Hosted enforcement would have to infer or inspect hidden runtime artifacts; redundancy 2 fits because broader evidence and coverage rules address the user-visible outcomes without codifying the internal schema.

assessments.title: Classification and visibility are workflow-owned fields
assessments.applicabilityRationale: This candidate governs ownership of internal routed-review record fields and moderation flow, not repository-change review criteria or user-facing Hosted review guidance.
assessments.summary: Exclude because the rule is about internal pass ownership of `classification` and `visible`, not about assessing implementation, test, documentation, or repository changes.
assessments.impactDescription: Adding this to the Hosted catalog would constrain orchestration behavior rather than improve defect detection in reviewed changes.
assessments.currentHostedCoverage: No current Hosted rule covers moderator ownership of workflow-internal record fields, and the catalog intentionally focuses repo-facing review guidance instead.
assessments.proposedText: Each final visible concern must have one authoritative classification and visibility decision. Final output must not expose conflicting classification or visibility states for the same concern.
assessments.selectionRationale: Severity is 1 because mis-owning these fields affects review plumbing more than repo defect outcomes. Frequency is 2 because routed reviews may use these fields often, but only inside the workflow. Breadth is 1 because the rule applies to a narrow internal handoff mechanism. Hosted detectability is 0 because a repo review cannot observe internal field ownership directly. Evidence strength is 1 because the candidate is active but uncited and unclassified. False-positive risk is 5 because enforcing workflow ownership as a Hosted repo rule would mislabel orchestration details as review defects. Redundancy is 1 because current Hosted rules do not already encode this exact internal ownership rule.

assessments.title: Routed passes may add or refine records, but must preserve shape
assessments.applicabilityRationale: This candidate specifies how routed review passes mutate shared intermediate records, which is workflow architecture rather than Hosted guidance for reviewing repository changes.
assessments.summary: Exclude because the rule governs structured handoff record mutation, deduplication, and lineage preservation between internal review stages.
assessments.impactDescription: Putting this into the Hosted catalog would add transport and state-management constraints, not actionable review criteria for code, tests, docs, or repository content.
assessments.currentHostedCoverage: The current Hosted catalog has no rule for intermediate record shape preservation and does not attempt to regulate internal routed-pass data models.
assessments.proposedText: When multiple review passes touch the same concern, enrich one canonical finding with added evidence or reasoning instead of cloning duplicates or replacing it with unlabeled prose. Preserve the finding's scope and classification context across passes.
assessments.selectionRationale: Severity is 1 because losing handoff structure is an orchestration problem, not a direct repo-review defect. Frequency is 3 because routed passes would touch shared records often in that workflow. Breadth is 1 because the scope is limited to the internal review pipeline. Hosted detectability is 0 because this behavior is not inferable from repository diffs alone. Evidence strength is 1 because the candidate has no cited supporting evidence in the catalog bundle. False-positive risk is 5 because converting handoff-shape expectations into Hosted rules would create many non-repo false alarms. Redundancy is 1 because the catalog does not already cover this specific workflow mechanic.

assessments.title: The handoff shape is semantic, not transport-specific
assessments.applicabilityRationale: This candidate is about allowable internal serialization formats and whether the handoff appears in final review output, which is prompt/workflow design rather than Hosted review guidance.
assessments.summary: Exclude because the rule describes transport-agnostic internal handoff semantics and suppresses workflow-internal sections from final output.
assessments.impactDescription: Including it would steer implementation details of the review system instead of improving semantic review of repository changes.
assessments.currentHostedCoverage: No current Hosted rule addresses intermediate transport format, and that omission is intentional because the catalog targets reviewable repo behavior rather than review-engine internals.
assessments.proposedText: The transport used between review stages may vary, but finding semantics must stay stable for scope, evidence, reasoning, classification, and visibility. Workflow-internal transport details must not become required reader-visible sections.
assessments.selectionRationale: Severity is 1 because serialization format choices do not directly change review conclusions about code. Frequency is 2 because transport choices matter only when that routed workflow is active. Breadth is 1 because the rule is narrowly about an internal handoff representation. Hosted detectability is 0 because repo review cannot inspect the internal transport. Evidence strength is 1 because the candidate is uncited. False-positive risk is 4 because a Hosted rule here would likely misclassify prompt-format choices as repo-review failures. Redundancy is 1 because the current catalog does not already encode this transport concern.

assessments.title: Roles communicate through schema updates, not free-form debate
assessments.applicabilityRationale: The rule controls how internal review roles communicate with each other, not how Hosted reviews should assess implementation, testing, documentation, or repository changes.
assessments.summary: Exclude because the candidate regulates communication channels between routed roles inside the review workflow.
assessments.impactDescription: A Hosted rule here would constrain the review system's collaboration mechanism rather than add an independently enforceable code-review safeguard.
assessments.currentHostedCoverage: Current Hosted rules do not address internal role-to-role communication shape, and that remains outside the scope of the repo-facing catalog.
assessments.proposedText: When reviewers disagree about a concern, resolve that disagreement by updating one canonical finding with the competing evidence and reasoning. Do not leave disconnected prose debate outside the finding record.
assessments.selectionRationale: Severity is 1 because this affects internal workflow hygiene, not direct defect review outcomes. Frequency is 2 because routed roles may dispute findings, but only in that workflow. Breadth is 1 because the scope is limited to shared-schema communication. Hosted detectability is 0 because repo review cannot observe internal debate channels. Evidence strength is 1 because the candidate is uncited and unclassified. False-positive risk is 5 because enforcing communication-channel rules in Hosted review would misfire on non-repo behavior. Redundancy is 1 because no existing Hosted rule addresses this internal concern.

assessments.title: Reviewer-to-handoff serialization is mandatory before routed roles
assessments.applicabilityRationale: This candidate defines fail-closed sequencing and serialization requirements between review stages, which belongs to workflow orchestration rather than the Hosted rule catalog for repository review.
assessments.summary: Exclude because the rule is about when findings must be serialized into an internal handoff before other routed roles execute.
assessments.impactDescription: If added, it would evaluate execution order inside the review system instead of evaluating defects in the user's repository changes.
assessments.currentHostedCoverage: The current Hosted catalog does not regulate pre-stage serialization or routed-role entry conditions, by design.
assessments.proposedText: Do not hand work to secondary review passes until every evidence-backed concern from the primary review exists in the canonical findings set. If a detected concern is missing from that set, stop rather than expecting later stages to recover it.
assessments.selectionRationale: Severity is 2 because losing serialized findings could matter inside the workflow, but it still does not define a repo-change defect. Frequency is 3 because every routed review would rely on this sequencing. Breadth is 1 because the rule is limited to staged handoff execution. Hosted detectability is 0 because repository review cannot observe whether serialization happened before another stage started. Evidence strength is 1 because no supporting evidence is cited. False-positive risk is 5 because a Hosted rule would conflate orchestration failures with repository-review failures. Redundancy is 1 because the catalog does not otherwise cover this pipeline behavior.

assessments.title: Mandatory issue-class concerns emit records immediately
