assessments.selectionRationale: severity 3 because omitted exported values reduce doc usefulness and can hide important outputs; frequency 4 because computed attributes are common; breadth 4 because the rule spans many documented objects; hostedDetectability 4 because schema-to-doc coverage comparison is straightforward; evidenceStrength 5 because the active hosted rule matches the candidate directly; falsePositiveRisk 1 because computed schema status is objective; redundancy 5 because DOCS-ATTR-002 already fully covers the requirement.
assessments.proposedText: Every user-relevant computed attribute exposed by schema must be documented under **Attributes Reference**.

assessments.title: Attribute descriptions must not include defaults/enums
assessments.applicabilityRationale: This is an enforceable documentation-content rule for what belongs in Attributes Reference descriptions.
assessments.summary: This candidate fills a hosted gap by preventing Attributes Reference entries from mixing output descriptions with input constraints or lifecycle semantics.
assessments.impactDescription: Adding it would keep attribute docs focused on exported data and avoid confusing users with defaults, enum guidance, ForceNew language, or import behavior that belongs elsewhere.
assessments.currentHostedCoverage: Current hosted docs rules require attribute coverage but do not constrain attribute-description content or prohibit lifecycle and import wording in Attributes Reference.
assessments.proposedText: Attributes Reference entries must describe exported data only. Do not include defaults, possible values, ForceNew, create/update/delete behavior, or import wording in attribute descriptions.
assessments.selectionRationale: severity 2 because this mainly protects clarity rather than core doc completeness; frequency 3 because attribute descriptions appear on most pages; breadth 3 because it applies across many resource and data source docs; hostedDetectability 4 because forbidden wording categories are visible in the doc text; evidenceStrength 2 because support is inferred from the contract structure rather than explicitly cited upstream; falsePositiveRisk 1 because defaults, enums, ForceNew, and import phrasing are objectively identifiable; redundancy 1 because no current hosted rule covers this boundary.

assessments.title: Do not special-case common fields in Attributes Reference
assessments.applicabilityRationale: This is an applicable documentation ordering and presentation rule for Attributes Reference.
assessments.summary: The special-case prohibition depends on adopting a broader attribute-ordering policy that is not yet sufficiently evidenced.
assessments.impactDescription: Adding this narrow exception rule without a confirmed base ordering rule would create brittle findings around a small set of common fields.
assessments.currentHostedCoverage: Current hosted docs rules do not prescribe attribute ordering or forbid common-field exceptions in Attributes Reference.
assessments.proposedText: Do not special-case name, resource_group_name, location, or tags under Attributes Reference; order attributes as id first, then the remaining attributes alphabetically.
assessments.selectionRationale: severity 1 because the concern is stylistic ordering, not semantic correctness; frequency 2 because only some pages expose these common fields as attributes; breadth 2 because the rule is narrow; hostedDetectability 5 because the special-casing is obvious on the page; evidenceStrength 1 because the candidate has no cited external or maintainer backing; falsePositiveRisk 4 because legitimate exceptions are not well-bounded; redundancy 5 because it largely restates and narrows the unresolved broader ordering concept from DOCS-ATTR-001.

assessments.title: Nested block attribute ordering (Attributes Reference)
assessments.applicabilityRationale: This is an applicable documentation-ordering rule for nested attribute bullets inside Attributes Reference subsections.
assessments.summary: Nested attribute ordering is enforceable but currently under-evidenced and downstream of the unresolved top-level attribute-ordering policy.
assessments.impactDescription: Prematurely codifying nested ordering would add stylistic churn, including note-movement checks, without strong source backing.
assessments.currentHostedCoverage: Current hosted docs rules cover attribute existence and accuracy, but they do not define nested attribute order inside block subsections.
assessments.proposedText: Within each Attributes Reference block subsection, list a nested id attribute first when present and order the remaining nested attributes alphabetically. Keep any note block directly attached to the attribute it qualifies when reordering.
assessments.selectionRationale: severity 1 because nested ordering is presentational; frequency 2 because nested attribute blocks are common but not universal; breadth 2 because the rule is limited to a subsection pattern; hostedDetectability 4 because ordering and attached notes are visible but require closer reading; evidenceStrength 1 because the candidate is unsupported by cited source evidence; falsePositiveRisk 3 because note-attachment and ordering exceptions are not well-specified; redundancy 3 because it depends on the same unresolved ordering theme as DOCS-ATTR-001.

assessments.title: Next-major deprecations
assessments.applicabilityRationale: This is applicable documentation-scope guidance for how coverage rules should treat next-major and legacy-only fields.
assessments.summary: The candidate identifies a useful vNext-review concept, but its advisory wording overlaps the stronger, enforceable DOCS-DEPR-002 candidate.
assessments.impactDescription: Adding this broader phrasing now would blur whether reviewers should flag omissions, extra legacy docs, or both, instead of centering one concrete failure condition.
assessments.currentHostedCoverage: Current hosted coverage rules use `relevant` and `user-relevant` language but do not explicitly encode a vNext-only documentation surface policy.
assessments.proposedText: When schema marks fields as next-major-only legacy or otherwise removed from the vNext surface, document the vNext surface area and do not require legacy-only fields to remain documented. Apply this only when repository evidence confirms the field is feature-flagged, deprecated, or removed for the next major version.
assessments.selectionRationale: severity 3 because vNext-versus-legacy confusion can distort coverage findings; frequency 2 because next-major deprecation patterns are narrower than ordinary schema coverage; breadth 3 because the concept spans arguments and attributes; hostedDetectability 2 because proving vNext-only status needs implementation context; evidenceStrength 2 because the candidate is contract-derived but not externally corroborated here; falsePositiveRisk 3 because the advisory `should focus` phrasing is not crisply testable; redundancy 5 because DOCS-DEPR-002 captures the actionable part more cleanly.

assessments.title: Legacy (non-vNext) fields must not be documented
assessments.applicabilityRationale: This is an enforceable documentation-scope rule for excluding legacy-only fields from current reference coverage.
assessments.summary: This candidate fills a real hosted gap by making vNext-surface exclusions explicit for both documentation content and coverage findings.
assessments.impactDescription: Without it, reviewers may incorrectly demand documentation for schema-exposed legacy fields or allow stale legacy-only fields to remain in current docs.
assessments.currentHostedCoverage: Current DOCS-ARG-001 and DOCS-ATTR-002 require documenting relevant schema fields, but neither explicitly tells reviewers to exclude legacy-only, non-vNext fields.
assessments.proposedText: When schema or implementation evidence shows a field is legacy-only or excluded from the vNext surface, do not document it in **Arguments Reference** or **Attributes Reference**, and do not raise a coverage finding for its omission.
assessments.selectionRationale: severity 4 because getting this wrong can create both stale docs and incorrect review findings; frequency 2 because legacy-only vNext transitions are narrower than general docs work; breadth 3 because it affects arguments, attributes, and coverage review; hostedDetectability 3 because the defect is clear once code evidence establishes legacy-only status; evidenceStrength 2 because the rule is contract-derived rather than explicitly backed by a cited upstream source here; falsePositiveRisk 2 because the proposed text requires evidence before applying the exclusion; redundancy 1 because no current hosted rule makes this exception explicit.

assessments.title: Do not guess when evidence is required
assessments.applicabilityRationale: This is a core documentation-review evidence rule that controls when reviewers may raise schema- or implementation-dependent findings.
assessments.summary: Active hosted rule DOCS-EVID-001 already captures the candidate's no-guess safeguard for documentation review findings.
assessments.impactDescription: This rule prevents unsupported findings about defaults, constraints, import IDs, lifecycle behavior, and other implementation-dependent claims.
assessments.currentHostedCoverage: DOCS-EVID-001 already states: `Do not guess about fields, constraints, defaults, conditional requirements, lifecycle behavior, or import IDs. Report a finding only when repository evidence proves the expected behavior.`
assessments.selectionRationale: severity 5 because unsupported review findings are highly damaging to trust and triage; frequency 4 because evidence-dependent documentation questions are common; breadth 5 because the safeguard spans many documentation rule areas; hostedDetectability 3 because misuse appears across varied scenarios rather than one literal pattern; evidenceStrength 4 because the active hosted rule already embodies the candidate closely; falsePositiveRisk 1 because requiring evidence is a conservative guardrail; redundancy 5 because DOCS-EVID-001 already covers the candidate's meaning.
assessments.proposedText: Do not guess about fields, constraints, defaults, conditional requirements, lifecycle behavior, or import IDs. Report a finding only when repository evidence proves the expected behavior.

assessments.title: Examples must be functional
assessments.applicabilityRationale: This is a documentation example-quality rule, and the candidate adds surface-specific expectations for the hosted docs surfaces now in scope.
assessments.summary: The current hosted rule captures example functionality at a high level, but the candidate usefully adds surface-specific expectations for resource, data source, list-resource, ephemeral-resource, and function docs.
assessments.impactDescription: Updating the rule would improve review consistency for newer documentation surfaces and prevent generic `functional example` findings that miss the correct block type or scenario.
assessments.currentHostedCoverage: DOCS-EX-000 currently says only that the primary example must be functional for its stated scenario; it does not yet spell out surface-specific expectations.
assessments.proposedText: The primary example must be functional for its stated scenario. Resource examples must be self-contained enough to run `terraform plan` without missing referenced objects; data source examples may assume the looked-up object already exists; list-resource examples must use Terraform `list` blocks for the documented object; ephemeral-resource examples must use `ephemeral` blocks; and function examples must call `provider::azurerm::<name>(...)`.
assessments.selectionRationale: severity 4 because broken or mis-scoped examples materially reduce doc usability; frequency 4 because every reference page relies on examples; breadth 5 because the rule spans all hosted documentation surfaces; hostedDetectability 3 because functional-scenario review sometimes needs contextual reading, not just literal matching; evidenceStrength 4 because the update is grounded in upstream standards plus surface-specific clarification; falsePositiveRisk 1 because the expectations are concrete and scenario-based; redundancy 1 because the active rule is only partially covering these newer surface distinctions.

assessments.title: Example Terraform config fences must be `hcl`
assessments.applicabilityRationale: This is a precise documentation formatting rule for Terraform configuration blocks inside example sections.
assessments.summary: This upstream documentation standard is not currently in hosted coverage and is precise enough to add directly.
assessments.impactDescription: Adding it would catch a common example-formatting defect that affects consistency and markdown language labeling without needing schema or implementation evidence.
assessments.currentHostedCoverage: Current hosted docs rules govern example functionality and structure, but none requires `hcl` as the language label for Terraform example fences.
assessments.proposedText: Terraform configuration fences under `Example*` headings must use the `hcl` language label, not `terraform`.
assessments.selectionRationale: severity 2 because fence labels are a formatting issue rather than a semantic doc failure; frequency 4 because example blocks are widespread; breadth 4 because the rule applies across many documentation pages; hostedDetectability 5 because fence labels are literal and easy to inspect; evidenceStrength 5 because the candidate is backed by explicit upstream contributor guidance; falsePositiveRisk 0 because the allowed label is unambiguous within the scoped example headings; redundancy 1 because current hosted coverage does not include this requirement.

assessments.title: Example Terraform CLI fences must be `shell` or `shell-session`
assessments.applicabilityRationale: This is enforceable documentation-format guidance for changed example CLI blocks, so it fits the Hosted documentation surface even though it is not strong enough to select.
assessments.summary: This is enforceable example-markdown guidance, but the batch gives little evidence that generic CLI fence selection needs a Hosted rule.
assessments.impactDescription: Using a nonstandard fence usually affects rendering and syntax highlighting more than the semantic correctness of the documented Terraform workflow.
assessments.currentHostedCoverage: DOCS-IMP-002 already requires a `shell` fence for resource import commands, so the uncovered gap is limited to other CLI snippets under example headings.
assessments.proposedText: In fenced CLI blocks under `Example` headings, use `shell` for command snippets and `shell-session` for prompt-and-output transcripts.
assessments.selectionRationale: Severity 1 fits a presentation issue that rarely changes example correctness; frequency 2 fits a recurring but not universal pattern; breadth 2 fits only pages with example CLI blocks; hostedDetectability 4 fits easy fence-label inspection in diff; evidenceStrength 1 fits the lack of upstream or maintainer support; falsePositiveRisk 2 fits mild ambiguity between command and transcript blocks; redundancy 2 fits partial overlap with DOCS-IMP-002. Those values support excluding this low-impact expansion.

assessments.title: Resource examples must be self-contained
assessments.applicabilityRationale: This is a concrete documentation-example correctness rule for resource pages and directly belongs on the Hosted documentation surface.
assessments.summary: This candidate refines the active self-containedness rule by clarifying that shared setup elsewhere on the same page is acceptable and that fixes must add declarations instead of deleting examples.
assessments.impactDescription: Without this clarification, review can either over-flag pages that intentionally share setup across examples or accept destructive remediations that remove useful example content.
assessments.currentHostedCoverage: DOCS-EX-003 already requires referenced objects to be declared, but it does not say that page-level shared declarations satisfy the rule or that missing references should be fixed by adding declarations rather than deleting the example.
assessments.proposedText: Every resource documentation page must declare on that page every resource, data source, and module referenced by its example configurations so the examples remain applyable as written. Shared declarations in Example Usage may satisfy later examples, but missing references are defects and must be fixed by adding the needed declarations rather than deleting or de-scoping the example.
assessments.selectionRationale: Severity 4 fits examples that stop being runnable or are reviewed incorrectly; frequency 4 fits a recurring docs failure mode; breadth 3 fits many resource pages but not the whole repository; hostedDetectability 4 fits direct inspection of missing references and page-local setup; evidenceStrength 4 fits strong local safeguard evidence plus an active hosted rule in the same area; falsePositiveRisk 1 fits a concrete, observable condition; redundancy 1 fits a needed refinement of an existing rule rather than a duplicate. Those values support updating DOCS-EX-003.

assessments.title: Preserve required `depends_on` verbatim when rewriting examples
assessments.applicabilityRationale: This is an enforceable documentation-example correctness safeguard for changed Terraform examples, and the Hosted docs surface can review it directly from repository evidence and diff context.
assessments.summary: The catalog lacks a direct safeguard against rewrites that drop or weaken an existing evidence-backed `depends_on`.
assessments.impactDescription: Removing required ordering can silently make an example fail or contradict accompanying documentation about why that ordering matters.
assessments.currentHostedCoverage: DOCS-EX-000 and DOCS-NOTE-002 can catch some downstream breakage, but neither rule explicitly preserves existing or prose-required `depends_on` targets during example rewrites.
assessments.proposedText: When rewriting a documentation example, preserve any existing `depends_on` entries and any prose-required `depends_on` targets unless repository evidence proves a different ordering requirement. If referenced objects are missing, add their declarations instead of removing or weakening `depends_on`.
assessments.selectionRationale: Severity 4 fits examples that can become materially wrong when required ordering is removed; frequency 2 fits a narrower rewrite-specific failure mode; breadth 2 fits only docs examples with ordering requirements; hostedDetectability 4 fits direct diff review of removed or weakened `depends_on`; evidenceStrength 3 fits repeated local-failure evidence; falsePositiveRisk 1 fits explicit existing code or notes as proof; redundancy 1 fits a missing safeguard not already stated directly. Those values support adding this rule.

assessments.title: Examples must not hard-code secrets
assessments.applicabilityRationale: This is a core documentation-example correctness and security rule that squarely belongs on the Hosted documentation surface.
assessments.summary: The active Hosted rule already matches this candidate's prohibition on hard-coded secrets in examples.
assessments.impactDescription: Adding another rule would duplicate an existing security safeguard without changing how reviewers classify the defect.
assessments.currentHostedCoverage: DOCS-EX-005 already states that examples must not hard-code secrets and should use variables for secret values.
assessments.selectionRationale: Severity 5 fits secret exposure risk; frequency 2 fits a meaningful but not constant docs issue; breadth 3 fits many example types; hostedDetectability 4 fits easy detection of secret literals in diff; evidenceStrength 3 fits a well-understood security safeguard already in the catalog; falsePositiveRisk 1 fits a concrete pattern; redundancy 0 fits exact existing coverage. Those values support keeping the current rule unchanged.
assessments.proposedText: Examples must not hard-code secrets; use input variables for secret values.

assessments.title: Example minimalism
assessments.applicabilityRationale: This candidate is editorial preference guidance with scenario-dependent exceptions rather than a stable Hosted defect rule that can be enforced consistently.
assessments.summary: This is editorial preference guidance about how much optional configuration to show, not a stable Hosted defect rule.
assessments.impactDescription: Enforcing it would create subjective comments about example brevity instead of focusing on correctness, validity, and evidence.
assessments.currentHostedCoverage: The current catalog intentionally checks whether examples are functional and accurate, not whether they are as minimal as possible.
assessments.proposedText: Example configurations should include only required arguments by default; include optional arguments only when they are necessary for a valid configuration or to demonstrate the example's stated scenario.
assessments.selectionRationale: Severity 1 fits a preference rather than a correctness issue; frequency 2 fits a recurring editorial choice; breadth 2 fits only documentation examples; hostedDetectability 1 fits hard-to-judge scenario intent; evidenceStrength 1 fits no supporting evidence; falsePositiveRisk 4 fits many legitimate reasons to include optional arguments; redundancy 3 fits overlap with existing functionality and accuracy rules at the correctness boundary. Those values support excluding it as not applicable for Hosted selection.

assessments.title: Example naming convention (nit-level)
assessments.applicabilityRationale: This candidate is explicitly nit-level style guidance and not a stable correctness rule for Hosted review.
assessments.summary: This candidate is an explicitly nit-level naming preference, not a correctness rule.
assessments.impactDescription: Selecting it would generate low-value rename comments while providing little protection against real documentation defects.
assessments.currentHostedCoverage: Current Hosted rules require example values to be valid and evidenced, but they intentionally do not standardize optional `example-` or `existing-` naming style.
assessments.proposedText: When example name-like string values follow the naming convention, resource examples should use an `example-` prefix and data source examples should use an `existing-` prefix; only recommend a deterministic rename when repository evidence proves the replacement is valid for that field.
assessments.selectionRationale: Severity 0 fits a rule the source itself says should not invalidate review; frequency 2 fits occasional rename opportunities; breadth 2 fits documentation examples only; hostedDetectability 2 fits detectable prefixes but subjective applicability; evidenceStrength 2 fits some internal rationale but no strong external mandate; falsePositiveRisk 5 fits many plausible valid names; redundancy 3 fits overlap with existing value-validity rules for anything truly wrong. Those values support excluding it as not applicable.

assessments.title: Examples must not include `terraform` or `provider` blocks
assessments.applicabilityRationale: This is a concrete documentation-example rule for reference docs and already belongs on the Hosted documentation surface.
assessments.summary: The active rule already covers this prohibition and its supported-exception model.
assessments.impactDescription: Replacing it with a more enumerated version would not materially change review outcomes and would make the catalog less compact.
assessments.currentHostedCoverage: DOCS-EX-008 already bans `terraform` and `provider` blocks in reference examples unless the documented object has an explicitly supported exception.
assessments.selectionRationale: Severity 3 fits examples that can teach the wrong reference-doc pattern; frequency 2 fits a bounded docs issue; breadth 3 fits multiple documentation object types; hostedDetectability 4 fits direct inspection of example blocks; evidenceStrength 4 fits explicit upstream guidance; falsePositiveRisk 1 fits a clear syntactic condition with explicit exceptions; redundancy 0 fits exact existing coverage. Those values support no change.
assessments.proposedText: Reference examples must not include `terraform` or `provider` blocks unless the documented object requires an explicitly supported exception.

assessments.title: Example HCL must be syntactically valid
assessments.applicabilityRationale: This is an enforceable documentation-example correctness rule, and the active primary-example rule is the right Hosted location for it.
assessments.summary: The current primary-example rule should be broadened to explicitly require valid HCL in every Terraform configuration example.
assessments.impactDescription: Malformed auxiliary examples remain uncopyable and misleading even when the primary example's overall scenario still looks correct.
assessments.currentHostedCoverage: DOCS-EX-000 covers primary-example functionality, but it does not expressly tell reviewers to flag invalid HCL in secondary example blocks.
assessments.proposedText: The primary example must be functional for its stated scenario, and every Terraform configuration example must be valid HCL.
assessments.selectionRationale: Severity 4 fits examples that users cannot copy or run; frequency 3 fits a moderate recurring docs issue; breadth 4 fits every Terraform example block across docs types; hostedDetectability 5 fits obvious syntax defects in changed snippets; evidenceStrength 2 fits limited explicit source evidence but a strong correctness expectation; falsePositiveRisk 1 fits concrete malformed HCL; redundancy 1 fits a natural expansion of the existing functional-example rule rather than a duplicate. Those values support updating DOCS-EX-000.

assessments.title: Example values must satisfy schema/implementation constraints
assessments.applicabilityRationale: This is a concrete documentation-example correctness rule, and it is a direct refinement of an existing Hosted validation rule.
assessments.summary: The active example-validation rule should be expanded to include repository-proven key spelling, casing, and literal-shape parity for the same Terraform argument.
assessments.impactDescription: Without this detail, docs can drift from implementation-backed or acceptance-test-backed user-facing map/object forms while still looking plausible.
assessments.currentHostedCoverage: DOCS-EX-010 already covers schema validation, enum casing, and cross-field requirements, but it does not explicitly treat repository-proven key casing and literal shape as binding example evidence.
assessments.proposedText: Example values must satisfy schema validation, enum casing, cross-field requirements, and repository-proven user-facing spelling, casing, and literal shape for the same Terraform argument. When implementation or acceptance-test HCL proves the keys or object form of a documented map or object literal, the example must use that exact form and must not invent an alternative without evidence.
assessments.selectionRationale: Severity 4 fits examples that can be syntactically plausible yet semantically wrong; frequency 3 fits a recurring casing-and-shape drift problem; breadth 4 fits many example values across docs; hostedDetectability 3 fits comparison work against implementation or tests; evidenceStrength 4 fits the candidate's repository-evidence framing and the active hosted rule in the same area; falsePositiveRisk 2 fits the need for same-argument proof before flagging; redundancy 1 fits an important refinement of existing validation guidance. Those values support updating DOCS-EX-010.

assessments.title: Examples must include all schema required arguments
assessments.applicabilityRationale: This is a core documentation correctness rule for the Hosted docs surface and is already represented by an active Hosted rule.
assessments.summary: The active required-argument rule already includes the primary-example requirement in this candidate.
assessments.impactDescription: Adding a second rule would duplicate a core docs correctness check without improving reviewer guidance.
assessments.currentHostedCoverage: DOCS-ARG-007 already requires every schema-required argument and nested block to be documented as required and included in the primary example.
assessments.selectionRationale: Severity 4 fits examples that fail because required inputs are missing; frequency 3 fits a common docs defect class; breadth 4 fits all documented object types with required fields; hostedDetectability 4 fits direct schema-to-example comparison; evidenceStrength 4 fits strong upstream and hosted support; falsePositiveRisk 1 fits a concrete required-field check; redundancy 0 fits exact existing coverage. Those values support keeping DOCS-ARG-007 unchanged.
assessments.proposedText: Every schema-required argument and nested block must be documented as required and included in the primary example.

assessments.title: Example sections must remain copy/pasteable Terraform
assessments.applicabilityRationale: This is an enforceable documentation-example preservation rule for changed pages, and the Hosted docs surface can apply it directly from diff and page structure.
assessments.summary: The catalog lacks an explicit rule against resolving example defects by deleting or prose-ifying Example Terraform blocks.
assessments.impactDescription: Without it, a page can keep its required top-level sections while losing copy/pasteable Terraform in example sections that users rely on.
assessments.currentHostedCoverage: DOCS-STRUCT-001 requires an Example Usage section and DOCS-EX-000 requires a functional primary example, but neither directly guards against deleting or converting other Example Terraform blocks during remediation.
assessments.proposedText: An `Example` section must retain copy/pasteable Terraform configuration. Do not resolve example defects by deleting the section or replacing its Terraform block with prose.
assessments.selectionRationale: Severity 3 fits loss of useful runnable guidance without always breaking the whole page; frequency 2 fits a narrower remediation failure mode; breadth 3 fits many docs pages with multiple example sections; hostedDetectability 4 fits visible section or fence removal in diff; evidenceStrength 3 fits local safeguard evidence from repeated failures; falsePositiveRisk 1 fits a concrete structural change; redundancy 1 fits a gap adjacent to, but not covered by, current structure and functionality rules. Those values support adding this rule.

assessments.title: Example instance name convention (style)
assessments.applicabilityRationale: This candidate is style guidance that the source itself says usually should not invalidate a page, so it is not suitable as a Hosted defect rule.
assessments.summary: This is style guidance about choosing the instance label `example`, not an actionable correctness rule.
assessments.impactDescription: Hosted enforcement would spend review capacity on cosmetic renames that the candidate itself says should not invalidate a page.
assessments.currentHostedCoverage: The current catalog deliberately avoids enforcing optional example instance-label style beyond correctness and evidence.
assessments.proposedText: Use `example` as the default Terraform instance label for resource, data source, list-resource, and ephemeral-resource blocks in documentation examples.
assessments.selectionRationale: Severity 0 fits a rule explicitly described as style-only; frequency 3 fits that many pages use example instance labels; breadth 3 fits several documentation object types; hostedDetectability 3 fits easy label inspection; evidenceStrength 1 fits no strong supporting evidence; falsePositiveRisk 4 fits many acceptable non-`example` labels; redundancy 2 fits existing rules already cover anything truly invalid about the example. Those values support excluding it as not applicable.

assessments.title: Avoid multiple examples when possible
assessments.applicabilityRationale: This candidate is editorial page-design guidance rather than a stable documentation defect rule that Hosted review can enforce consistently.
assessments.summary: This is editorial guidance about page design and example count, not a stable defect rule for changed documentation.
assessments.impactDescription: Enforcing it would second-guess legitimate teaching choices and complex scenarios rather than catch correctness issues.
assessments.currentHostedCoverage: The current catalog checks that required sections exist and that examples are accurate; it does not prescribe how many examples a page should include.
assessments.proposedText: Prefer a single inline example per page; add multiple inline examples only when distinct complex scenarios need separate coverage, and move broader scenario examples to the repository `examples/` directory.
assessments.selectionRationale: Severity 1 fits a weak editorial preference; frequency 2 fits occasional page-design decisions; breadth 3 fits many documentation pages; hostedDetectability 1 fits poor ability to judge whether multiple examples are justified; evidenceStrength 2 fits some upstream intent but not a concrete defect condition; falsePositiveRisk 5 fits many valid exceptions; redundancy 2 fits current rules already covering the correctness of any included examples. Those values support excluding it as not applicable.

assessments.title: Deterministic example name value derivation (nit-level)
assessments.applicabilityRationale: This candidate is a complex nit-level rename policy rather than a core Hosted defect rule, and it mixes style with value-generation procedure.
assessments.summary: This is a detailed nit-level rename algorithm rather than a core correctness rule.
assessments.impactDescription: Selecting it would add substantial review complexity for mostly stylistic renames and invite overconfident value generation when evidence is incomplete.
assessments.currentHostedCoverage: DOCS-EX-010 and DOCS-EVID-001 already cover the correctness boundary by requiring example values to be valid and evidence-backed.
assessments.proposedText: When renaming a name-like argument in an `Example` HCL block, derive the replacement deterministically from that block's full Terraform type suffix: use `example-<type-suffix>` for resources and `existing-<type-suffix>` for data sources, apply the rule independently to every block on the page, and change separators, casing, or length only when schema or implementation evidence proves the constraint; otherwise do not guess a replacement.
assessments.selectionRationale: Severity 1 fits mostly stylistic rename guidance; frequency 2 fits occasional repair scenarios; breadth 2 fits only name-like example values; hostedDetectability 2 fits detectable candidates but hard-to-verify fallback logic; evidenceStrength 2 fits local rationale without a broader mandate; falsePositiveRisk 4 fits many chances to overreach when constraints are incomplete; redundancy 4 fits strong overlap with existing validity and no-guessing rules for the meaningful correctness boundary. Those values support excluding it as not applicable.

assessments.title: Example values must respect ValidateFunc constraints
assessments.applicabilityRationale: This is a concrete documentation-example value-validity rule that already belongs to the Hosted documentation surface through an active Hosted rule.
assessments.summary: The active example-validation rule already covers ValidateFunc-backed constraints.
assessments.impactDescription: A second rule would repeat the same failure condition and make the documentation surface more repetitive without better guidance.
assessments.currentHostedCoverage: DOCS-EX-010 already requires example values to satisfy schema validation, enum casing, and other proven constraints.
assessments.selectionRationale: Severity 4 fits invalid example values that mislead users; frequency 3 fits a recurring validation issue; breadth 4 fits many arguments across docs; hostedDetectability 4 fits direct comparison against proven validators; evidenceStrength 4 fits strong alignment with existing Hosted validation guidance; falsePositiveRisk 1 fits a concrete proof-based check; redundancy 0 fits exact current coverage. Those values support no change.
assessments.proposedText: Example values must satisfy schema validation, enum casing, and cross-field requirements.

assessments.title: Do not introduce net-new `depends_on` without evidence
assessments.applicabilityRationale: This is an enforceable documentation-example evidence rule for changed Terraform snippets, and the Hosted docs surface can apply it using repository evidence.
assessments.summary: The catalog lacks a direct rule telling reviewers to reject speculative new `depends_on` entries in examples.
assessments.impactDescription: Unsupported ordering guidance can imply nonexistent lifecycle constraints and make examples harder to understand or maintain.
assessments.currentHostedCoverage: DOCS-EVID-001 discourages guessing generally, but it does not explicitly treat a newly added `depends_on` without repository proof as a documentation defect.
assessments.proposedText: Do not add `depends_on` to a documentation example unless schema, implementation, or surrounding evidence proves that ordering is required for the documented scenario.
assessments.selectionRationale: Severity 3 fits misleading lifecycle guidance that can change how users understand the example; frequency 2 fits a narrower edit pattern; breadth 2 fits only examples with ordering concerns; hostedDetectability 3 fits comparison between new `depends_on` and repository proof; evidenceStrength 3 fits explicit local safeguard rationale; falsePositiveRisk 2 fits the need to search for supporting evidence before flagging; redundancy 1 fits a useful specialization of the existing no-guessing principle. Those values support adding this rule.

assessments.title: Preserve example-adjacent notes when rewriting examples
assessments.applicabilityRationale: This is documentation-note correctness guidance, and the actionable defect it describes is already represented by an active Hosted documentation rule.
assessments.summary: Required sequencing or validation notes next to examples are already covered by the existing constraint-documentation rule.
assessments.impactDescription: A separate preservation rule would mostly restate that removing or making such a note inaccurate is already a documentation defect when the constraint still matters.
assessments.currentHostedCoverage: DOCS-NOTE-002 already requires cross-field requirements and diff-time constraints to stay documented and consistent with schema or implementation behavior.
assessments.selectionRationale: Severity 3 fits missing or inaccurate notes that can hide real constraints; frequency 2 fits a targeted rewrite issue; breadth 2 fits only example-adjacent notes about constraints; hostedDetectability 3 fits visible note deletion or mismatch in diff; evidenceStrength 3 fits the candidate's concrete safeguard rationale; falsePositiveRisk 2 fits the need to confirm that the note still reflects a real requirement; redundancy 1 fits that DOCS-NOTE-002 already covers the actionable failure condition. Those values support no change.
assessments.proposedText: Cross-field requirements, conflicts, and diff-time constraints that affect valid configuration must be documented and must agree with schema or implementation behavior.

assessments.title: Do not replace Terraform references with invented literals
assessments.applicabilityRationale: This is documentation-example correctness guidance, but as written it is a narrow remediation-specific slice of a broader Hosted gap.
assessments.summary: This candidate identifies a real anti-pattern, but as a standalone rule it is too narrow and overlaps a broader reference-semantics gap.
assessments.impactDescription: Keeping the shortcut-specific version would add overlap while still missing other unjustified reference-to-literal or literal-to-reference rewrites.
assessments.currentHostedCoverage: DOCS-EX-003, DOCS-EX-010, and DOCS-EVID-001 partially constrain invented literal replacements today; the remaining gap is better handled by broader reference-semantics guidance.
assessments.proposedText: Do not replace Terraform references in resource examples with invented literal strings to make the example self-contained. Declare the missing resource, data source, or module instead, unless repository evidence proves a literal is valid for an explicitly literal scenario.
assessments.selectionRationale: Severity 3 fits example repairs that can change meaning; frequency 2 fits a narrower repair shortcut; breadth 1 fits a small slice of resource-example edits; hostedDetectability 3 fits visible ref-to-literal rewrites in diff; evidenceStrength 3 fits concrete local safeguard history; falsePositiveRisk 2 fits the need to verify that a literal is truly invented rather than proven; redundancy 4 fits substantial overlap with existing rules and a better broader candidate. Those values support excluding this narrower standalone addition.

assessments.title: Example self-containedness must be transitive
assessments.applicabilityRationale: This is documentation-example correctness guidance, and the outcome it requires is already represented by the active Hosted self-containedness rule.
assessments.summary: The active self-containedness rule already requires the fully runnable end state that this candidate describes.
assessments.impactDescription: Treating transitive closure as a separate Hosted rule would mostly duplicate an outcome already required when every referenced object needed to apply the example must be declared.
assessments.currentHostedCoverage: DOCS-EX-003 already covers undeclared indirect references, and DOCS-EX-000 catches examples that still are not functional after a partial fix.
assessments.selectionRationale: Severity 4 fits examples that remain unrunnable after incomplete fixes; frequency 2 fits a narrower repair pattern; breadth 2 fits self-containedness edits on resource docs; hostedDetectability 3 fits review that traces newly introduced references; evidenceStrength 3 fits concrete local safeguard rationale; falsePositiveRisk 1 fits a specific end-state check; redundancy 1 fits that DOCS-EX-003 already expresses the required outcome. Those values support no change.
assessments.proposedText: A resource example must declare every referenced resource, data source, and module needed to apply it.

assessments.title: Preserve reference semantics in examples
assessments.applicabilityRationale: This is an enforceable documentation-example correctness rule for changed Terraform snippets, and it fills a gap not directly covered by the current Hosted catalog.
assessments.summary: The catalog lacks a direct safeguard against convenience rewrites that change an example argument between a Terraform reference and a literal without proof.
assessments.impactDescription: Those rewrites can preserve superficial validity while changing example semantics and teaching users the wrong configuration pattern.
assessments.currentHostedCoverage: DOCS-EX-003, DOCS-EX-010, and DOCS-EVID-001 cover missing declarations, value validity, and evidence discipline separately, but none directly tells reviewers to preserve reference semantics when evidence for a ref/literal swap is missing.
assessments.proposedText: Do not change a documentation example argument between a Terraform reference and a literal value unless repository evidence proves the replacement is correct for the documented scenario. Preserve reference semantics by declaring needed referenced objects on the page instead of inventing plausible literals.
assessments.selectionRationale: Severity 4 fits semantically wrong examples that can still look plausible; frequency 2 fits a targeted repair and rewrite pattern; breadth 3 fits many documentation examples that mix references and literals; hostedDetectability 3 fits review of changed arguments against repository evidence; evidenceStrength 3 fits explicit local safeguard rationale; falsePositiveRisk 2 fits the need to confirm whether the replacement is actually proven; redundancy 2 fits some adjacency to existing self-containedness and evidence rules but no direct current safeguard. Those values support adding this broader rule.

assessments.title: Data source examples should model existing-object lookups
assessments.applicabilityRationale: This is a documentation review rule for example composition in data source pages, and reviewers can enforce it by inspecting whether the primary example is written as a lookup or as unnecessary resource scaffolding.
assessments.summary: Add a data-source-specific example rule so Hosted reviewers do not treat lookup docs like resource docs.
assessments.impactDescription: Without this rule, reviews can miss overbuilt data source examples or incorrectly demand resource scaffolding that hides the intended existing-object lookup pattern.
assessments.currentHostedCoverage: DOCS-EX-000 only requires the primary example to be functional, and DOCS-EX-003 only constrains resource examples; no current Hosted rule defines the correct shape for data source lookup examples.
assessments.proposedText: A data source primary example should model an existing-object lookup: include only the arguments needed to identify the object, assume the looked-up object already exists, and do not add resource scaffolding solely to create the lookup target.
assessments.selectionRationale: Severity 2 fits because resource-style scaffolding mainly confuses lookup guidance rather than breaking provider behavior; frequency 3 and breadth 3 fit because this applies across many data source pages but not all docs; hostedDetectability 4 fits because reviewers can inspect the primary example shape directly; evidenceStrength 4 fits because the source cites upstream standards plus a clarification PR; falsePositiveRisk 2 fits because the scope is narrow and the exception is explicit; redundancy 1 fits because no current Hosted rule defines data source lookup-example shape.

assessments.title: List-resource examples must use list queries
assessments.applicabilityRationale: This is a documentation rule for list-resource pages with objective checks on block syntax and example shape.
assessments.summary: Add a Hosted rule for list-resource example syntax and query coverage.
assessments.impactDescription: Without this rule, list-resource docs can be written as ordinary resource or data examples, which misdocuments the feature and hides the intended query scenarios.
assessments.currentHostedCoverage: DOCS-EX-000 requires a functional primary example, but no current Hosted rule says list-resource docs must use Terraform `list` syntax or demonstrate list queries.
assessments.proposedText: List-resource primary examples must use Terraform `list "azurerm_<name>" "example"` syntax for the documented object and should show the base query plus any supported narrowed query instead of modeling the page as a `resource` or `data` example.
assessments.selectionRationale: Severity 3 fits because the wrong block type materially misdocuments how the feature is used; frequency 2 and breadth 2 fit because list resources are a smaller but distinct documentation surface; hostedDetectability 5 fits because reviewers can read the example blocks directly; evidenceStrength 5 fits because the candidate is backed by a published upstream contributor guide; falsePositiveRisk 1 fits because the syntax requirement is explicit; redundancy 0 fits because the current catalog has no list-resource example rule.

assessments.title: Ephemeral-resource examples must use ephemeral blocks
assessments.applicabilityRationale: This is a documentation rule for ephemeral-resource pages with a concrete, reviewable failure condition in the primary example block.
assessments.summary: Add a Hosted rule that keeps ephemeral-resource docs centered on ephemeral reads.
assessments.impactDescription: Without this rule, ephemeral-resource pages can drift toward resource or data-source examples and stop demonstrating the actual ephemeral read surface.
assessments.currentHostedCoverage: DOCS-EX-000 only requires a functional primary example; no current Hosted rule requires ephemeral-resource docs to use Terraform `ephemeral` syntax for the documented object.
assessments.proposedText: Ephemeral-resource primary examples must use Terraform `ephemeral "azurerm_<name>" "example"` syntax for the documented object. Supporting `resource` or `data` blocks are allowed only to supply inputs to that ephemeral read.
assessments.selectionRationale: Severity 3 fits because using the wrong block type makes the example fundamentally misleading; frequency 1 and breadth 1 fit because ephemeral-resource docs are still a narrow surface; hostedDetectability 5 fits because the failure is visible in the example block; evidenceStrength 3 fits because the pattern is backed by multiple current provider pages rather than a published contributor rule; falsePositiveRisk 1 fits because the primary object type is objective; redundancy 0 fits because the current catalog does not cover ephemeral-resource example syntax.

assessments.title: Function examples must call provider-defined functions
assessments.applicabilityRationale: This is a documentation rule for function pages, and the example syntax is directly reviewable from the markdown without outside inference.
assessments.summary: Add a Hosted rule for provider-defined function example syntax.
assessments.impactDescription: Without this rule, function docs can show the wrong call form and leave readers with examples that do not demonstrate how provider-defined functions are actually invoked.
assessments.currentHostedCoverage: The current Hosted documentation rules have no function-specific example rule and do not mention `provider::azurerm::...` syntax.
assessments.proposedText: Function examples must call the documented provider-defined function with `provider::azurerm::<name>(...)` syntax.
assessments.selectionRationale: Severity 3 fits because the wrong call syntax makes the example unusable; frequency 1 and breadth 1 fit because function docs are a small specialized surface; hostedDetectability 5 fits because reviewers can inspect the example call directly; evidenceStrength 3 fits because the candidate is backed by current provider function pages rather than a contributor-guide rule; falsePositiveRisk 1 fits because the syntax check is objective; redundancy 0 fits because the current catalog has no function-example syntax rule.

assessments.title: Required frontmatter keys
assessments.applicabilityRationale: This is an enforceable documentation frontmatter rule, and it already maps directly to an active Hosted rule.
assessments.summary: Current DOCS-FM-001 already covers the required frontmatter keys.
assessments.impactDescription: No catalog change is needed because the existing Hosted rule already catches missing required frontmatter keys on reference pages.
assessments.currentHostedCoverage: DOCS-FM-001 already says reference documentation must begin with YAML frontmatter containing `subcategory`, `layout`, `page_title`, and `description`.
assessments.selectionRationale: Severity 3 fits because missing required frontmatter can break or degrade page metadata; frequency 5 and breadth 5 fit because every reference page needs it; hostedDetectability 5 fits because the keys are trivial to inspect; evidenceStrength 5 fits because an active Hosted rule already preserves this requirement; falsePositiveRisk 1 fits because the check is explicit; redundancy 5 fits because the candidate is already covered almost verbatim by DOCS-FM-001.
assessments.proposedText: Reference documentation must begin with YAML frontmatter containing `subcategory`, `layout`, `page_title`, and `description`.

assessments.title: Data source `page_title` must include `Data Source:`
assessments.applicabilityRationale: This is an enforceable documentation frontmatter convention, but it is a narrow metadata-string check rather than a broader semantic defect rule.
assessments.summary: Do not add a separate Hosted rule for the exact data-source `page_title` prefix.
assessments.impactDescription: A wrong `page_title` prefix is metadata drift, but it rarely changes the technical correctness or usability of the documentation enough to justify new Hosted guidance budget.
assessments.currentHostedCoverage: DOCS-FM-001 already requires a `page_title`, but no current Hosted rule enforces the exact `Data Source:` prefix for data source pages.
assessments.proposedText: Data source docs must set `page_title` to `Azure Resource Manager: Data Source: azurerm_<name>`.
assessments.selectionRationale: Severity 1 fits because this is metadata polish more than a substantive doc defect; frequency 3 and breadth 2 fit because it applies to one common doc subtype; hostedDetectability 5 fits because the string is easy to inspect; evidenceStrength 1 fits because the candidate cites no published or confirmed standard; falsePositiveRisk 3 fits because branding or format exceptions are plausible; redundancy 3 fits because DOCS-FM-001 already requires the field, so exact-prefix enforcement adds limited protection.

assessments.title: Resource `page_title` canonical format
assessments.applicabilityRationale: This is an enforceable documentation frontmatter convention, but it is a narrow canonical-string requirement rather than a high-signal semantic review rule.
assessments.summary: Do not add a separate Hosted rule for the exact resource `page_title` string.
assessments.impactDescription: An incorrect resource `page_title` is easy to fix, but it contributes little to schema, example, or lifecycle review quality compared with the token cost of another exact-format rule.
assessments.currentHostedCoverage: DOCS-FM-001 already requires a `page_title`, but the current Hosted catalog does not enforce a specific resource-title template.
assessments.proposedText: Resource docs must set `page_title` to `Azure Resource Manager: azurerm_<name>`.
assessments.selectionRationale: Severity 1 fits because the defect is mostly presentational metadata; frequency 5 and breadth 4 fit because resource docs are numerous; hostedDetectability 5 fits because the frontmatter line is trivial to inspect; evidenceStrength 1 fits because the candidate provides no cited authority for elevating the exact string; falsePositiveRisk 2 fits because the format is objective but still susceptible to naming exceptions; redundancy 3 fits because the catalog already ensures the field exists even though it does not freeze the exact template.

assessments.title: Frontmatter descriptions must use doc-type summary style
assessments.applicabilityRationale: This is a documentation wording rule with a concrete, reviewable failure condition on the frontmatter `description` sentence.
assessments.summary: Update DOCS-WORD-003 so the canonical summary styles explicitly apply to the frontmatter `description`.
assessments.impactDescription: Without the update, reviewers know the preferred summary stems but the catalog does not clearly say that the YAML `description` must carry that summary sentence, leaving frontmatter wording under-enforced.
assessments.currentHostedCoverage: DOCS-WORD-003 already defines the canonical summary starts by doc type, but it does not explicitly bind those patterns to the frontmatter `description` field.
assessments.proposedText: Reference doc summary sentences, including the frontmatter `description`, must match the doc type: resource summaries start with `Manages`; data source summaries start with `Gets information about`; list-resource summaries start with `Lists`; ephemeral-resource summaries start with `Use this to access information about`; and function summaries describe the function behavior.
assessments.selectionRationale: Severity 2 fits because inconsistent summary wording weakens page clarity without breaking the page; frequency 5 and breadth 5 fit because every reference page has a `description`; hostedDetectability 4 fits because reviewers can inspect the field directly but still need to distinguish doc types; evidenceStrength 2 fits because the candidate offers no fresh source authority and mainly clarifies an existing Hosted convention; falsePositiveRisk 2 fits because the approved stems are already concrete; redundancy 1 fits because DOCS-WORD-003 is close but does not explicitly cover frontmatter descriptions today.

assessments.title: `subcategory` must match the service website category
assessments.applicabilityRationale: This is a documentation frontmatter rule, but enforcing exact category values depends on a stable source of truth that is not identified in the candidate.
assessments.summary: Defer a Hosted `subcategory` value rule until the repo exposes a stable, citable category authority.
assessments.impactDescription: Adding this now would create noisy reviews whenever the correct website category has to be inferred from scattered existing pages or maintainer convention instead of an explicit standard.
assessments.currentHostedCoverage: No Hosted rule validates exact `subcategory` values today; DOCS-FM-001 only requires the field to exist, and DOCS-EVID-001 prevents guessing but does not supply an allowed-category source.
assessments.proposedText: The frontmatter `subcategory` must match the documented service's established website category. Use an explicit allowed-category source or matching same-service docs as evidence, and do not guess when the correct category is unclear.
assessments.selectionRationale: Severity 2 fits because a wrong category hurts organization more than technical correctness; frequency 4 and breadth 4 fit because most docs carry subcategories; hostedDetectability 3 fits because reviewers can inspect the field but still need outside authority to judge it; evidenceStrength 1 fits because the candidate cites no definitive category source; falsePositiveRisk 4 fits because multiple plausible categories and service-history exceptions are likely; redundancy 2 fits because existing rules cover field presence and no-guessing, but not exact category choice.

assessments.title: `layout` must be `azurerm`
assessments.applicabilityRationale: This is an enforceable documentation frontmatter rule, and it already maps directly to an active Hosted rule.
assessments.summary: Current DOCS-FM-006 already covers the required `layout` value.
assessments.impactDescription: No catalog change is needed because the existing Hosted rule already catches reference pages whose frontmatter uses the wrong layout.
assessments.currentHostedCoverage: DOCS-FM-006 already says the frontmatter `layout` must be `azurerm`.
assessments.selectionRationale: Severity 2 fits because a wrong layout can break rendering or metadata behavior; frequency 5 and breadth 5 fit because all reference pages use it; hostedDetectability 5 fits because the field is direct to inspect; evidenceStrength 5 fits because an active Hosted rule already preserves the requirement; falsePositiveRisk 1 fits because the allowed value is explicit; redundancy 5 fits because the candidate is already covered verbatim by DOCS-FM-006.
assessments.proposedText: The frontmatter `layout` must be `azurerm`.

assessments.title: Frontmatter must appear at the beginning of the file
assessments.applicabilityRationale: This is an enforceable documentation structure rule, and the current Hosted frontmatter rule already includes the beginning-of-file requirement.
assessments.summary: Keep frontmatter placement folded into DOCS-FM-001 instead of creating a duplicate rule.
assessments.impactDescription: No catalog change is needed because the existing Hosted rule already flags docs that omit frontmatter or fail to begin with it.
assessments.currentHostedCoverage: DOCS-FM-001 already says reference documentation must begin with YAML frontmatter containing the required keys.
assessments.selectionRationale: Severity 3 fits because misplaced frontmatter can invalidate the page header entirely; frequency 5 and breadth 5 fit because every reference page begins with frontmatter; hostedDetectability 5 fits because placement is obvious from the file start; evidenceStrength 5 fits because DOCS-FM-001 already encodes the requirement; falsePositiveRisk 1 fits because the failure condition is objective; redundancy 5 fits because this candidate is already subsumed by DOCS-FM-001.
assessments.proposedText: Reference documentation must begin with YAML frontmatter containing `subcategory`, `layout`, `page_title`, and `description`.

assessments.title: List resource `page_title` canonical format
assessments.applicabilityRationale: This is an enforceable documentation frontmatter convention, but it is a narrow metadata-template check on a small doc subtype.
assessments.summary: Do not add a separate Hosted rule for the exact list-resource `page_title` format.
assessments.impactDescription: Exact list-resource title formatting is easy to review manually, but it adds little semantic defect coverage compared with the cost of another dedicated frontmatter-string rule.
assessments.currentHostedCoverage: DOCS-FM-001 already requires a `page_title`, but no current Hosted rule enforces a specific list-resource title template.
assessments.proposedText: List-resource docs must set `page_title` to `Azure Resource Manager: azurerm_<name>`.
assessments.selectionRationale: Severity 1 fits because the issue is presentational metadata; frequency 1 and breadth 1 fit because list-resource docs are a small surface; hostedDetectability 5 fits because the line is trivial to inspect; evidenceStrength 1 fits because the candidate cites no standard for elevating the exact title shape; falsePositiveRisk 2 fits because the format is objective but naming wrinkles remain possible; redundancy 3 fits because the catalog already requires the field even though it does not lock the exact template.

assessments.title: Ephemeral resource `page_title` canonical format
assessments.applicabilityRationale: This is an enforceable documentation frontmatter convention, but it is a narrow metadata-string rule on a very small doc surface.

assessments.impactDescription: An incorrect ephemeral-resource title is low-severity metadata drift and does not justify another dedicated exact-string rule in the Hosted catalog.
assessments.currentHostedCoverage: DOCS-FM-001 already requires a `page_title`, but the current Hosted catalog does not enforce an exact ephemeral-resource title template.
assessments.proposedText: Ephemeral-resource docs must set `page_title` to `Azure Resource Manager: azurerm_<name>`.
assessments.selectionRationale: Severity 1 fits because the defect is mostly metadata polish; frequency 1 and breadth 1 fit because ephemeral-resource docs are rare; hostedDetectability 5 fits because the field is direct to inspect; evidenceStrength 1 fits because the candidate supplies no published or confirmed standard; falsePositiveRisk 2 fits because the string check is mostly objective; redundancy 3 fits because the catalog already guarantees the field exists even though it does not freeze the exact wording.

assessments.title: Function `page_title` canonical format
assessments.applicabilityRationale: This is an enforceable documentation frontmatter convention, but it is a narrow metadata-template rule for a small specialized surface.
assessments.summary: Do not add a separate Hosted rule for the exact function `page_title` format.
assessments.impactDescription: Function-title formatting is easy to spot but low impact relative to schema accuracy, example correctness, and other higher-signal documentation review rules.
assessments.currentHostedCoverage: DOCS-FM-001 already requires a `page_title`, but no current Hosted rule enforces a specific function-title template.
assessments.proposedText: Function docs must set `page_title` to `Azure Resource Manager: <name>`.
assessments.selectionRationale: Severity 1 fits because the issue is mostly title metadata; frequency 1 and breadth 1 fit because function docs are few; hostedDetectability 5 fits because the line is straightforward to inspect; evidenceStrength 1 fits because the candidate cites no formal standard for the exact template; falsePositiveRisk 2 fits because the rule is fairly objective but still naming-sensitive; redundancy 3 fits because the catalog already requires a `page_title` even though it leaves the exact format unconstrained.

assessments.title: Canonical section intro lines
assessments.applicabilityRationale: This is a documentation formatting rule with exact, checkable intro lines, and the candidate extends an existing Hosted rule to additional doc surfaces.
assessments.summary: Update DOCS-FMT-001 to cover list-resource and ephemeral-resource intro lines in addition to resource and data source pages.
assessments.impactDescription: Without the update, Hosted reviewers enforce the canonical intro lines on resource and data source pages but stay silent on the corresponding list-resource and ephemeral-resource templates.
assessments.currentHostedCoverage: DOCS-FMT-001 already enforces the exact intro lines for resource and data source docs, but it does not cover the list-resource and ephemeral-resource variants in the candidate.
assessments.proposedText: Resource and data source docs must use the exact introductions `The following arguments are supported:` under **Arguments Reference** and `In addition to the Arguments listed above - the following Attributes are exported:` under **Attributes Reference**. List-resource docs must use `This list resource supports the following arguments:` under **Argument Reference**. Ephemeral-resource docs must use `The following arguments are supported:` under **Argument Reference** and `The following attributes are exported:` under **Attributes Reference**.
assessments.selectionRationale: Severity 2 fits because wrong intro lines are template defects rather than semantic breakage; frequency 3 and breadth 3 fit because the change affects two meaningful but not universal doc subtypes; hostedDetectability 5 fits because the required lines are exact string checks; evidenceStrength 2 fits because the candidate extends an existing Hosted convention without new cited source authority; falsePositiveRisk 1 fits because the phrases are explicit; redundancy 1 fits because current DOCS-FMT-001 stops short of the added surfaces.

assessments.title: Backticks for arguments and values
assessments.applicabilityRationale: This is an enforceable documentation style rule, but it is an editorial formatting preference rather than a high-signal semantic review safeguard.
assessments.summary: Do not add a universal Hosted rule for backticks around every argument name and specific value.
assessments.impactDescription: A blanket backtick rule would spend review budget on prose polish and create avoidable debates around ordinary language, Azure product names, and non-literal references.
assessments.currentHostedCoverage: Current Hosted documentation rules intentionally do not enforce blanket inline-code formatting for every argument, attribute, or literal value in prose.
assessments.proposedText: Wrap argument names, attribute names, and specific literal or enum values in backticks in documentation prose.
assessments.selectionRationale: Severity 1 fits because missing backticks are editorial issues; frequency 4 and breadth 4 fit because names and values appear throughout docs; hostedDetectability 5 fits because reviewers can spot formatting directly; evidenceStrength 1 fits because the candidate cites no standard for elevating this to Hosted guidance; falsePositiveRisk 4 fits because deciding which prose tokens are true literals versus narrative text is often debatable; redundancy 1 fits because the catalog does not already cover this, but the weak evidence and low severity still do not justify adding it.

assessments.title: Use the most specific code fence language
assessments.applicabilityRationale: This is an enforceable documentation formatting rule, but it is a low-severity presentation preference rather than a high-value semantic defect rule.
assessments.summary: Do not add a Hosted rule for `hcl` versus `terraform` fence labels right now.
assessments.impactDescription: Incorrect fence labels are easy to spot, but they rarely change the technical truth of the documentation enough to warrant more guarded guidance.
assessments.currentHostedCoverage: No current Hosted rule enforces code-fence language labels in documentation pages.
assessments.proposedText: Use the most specific fence language for documentation code blocks; Terraform configuration snippets must use `hcl`, not `terraform`.
assessments.selectionRationale: Severity 1 fits because fence labels affect presentation more than semantic correctness; frequency 4 and breadth 4 fit because code fences are common across docs; hostedDetectability 5 fits because the label is explicit in markdown; evidenceStrength 1 fits because the candidate cites no published or confirmed source for the rule; falsePositiveRisk 2 fits because the check is mostly objective; redundancy 1 fits because the catalog does not already cover this, but the low-severity, low-evidence nature still supports no change.

assessments.title: Outer fences must safely contain nested code fences
assessments.applicabilityRationale: This is a documentation formatting rule with an exact, inspectable failure condition and explicit upstream backing.
assessments.summary: Add a Hosted rule for four-backtick outer fences when nested triple-backtick blocks are present.
assessments.impactDescription: Without this rule, markdown examples that embed other fenced blocks can render incorrectly and break the readability of contributor-facing documentation.
assessments.currentHostedCoverage: The current Hosted documentation rules do not address nested code-fence safety.
assessments.proposedText: A code block that contains a nested triple-backtick fence must use four backticks for the outer opening and closing fences.
assessments.selectionRationale: Severity 2 fits because broken fence nesting damages rendering and readability; frequency 1 fits because nested fenced blocks are uncommon; breadth 2 fits because the issue can appear on multiple documentation pages when it occurs; hostedDetectability 5 fits because reviewers can inspect fence counts directly; evidenceStrength 5 fits because the candidate cites a published upstream contributor standard; falsePositiveRisk 1 fits because the condition is explicit; redundancy 0 fits because the current catalog has no rule for nested fence handling.

assessments.title: Import example correctness
assessments.applicabilityRationale: This is an enforceable documentation import rule, and the current Hosted catalog already covers the actionable correctness requirement.
assessments.summary: Current DOCS-IMP-001 already covers import ID correctness, and DOCS-EVID-001 already handles the no-guess guardrail.
assessments.impactDescription: No catalog change is needed because the existing Hosted rules already require import examples to match real parser or importer behavior and already forbid unsupported guesses.
assessments.currentHostedCoverage: DOCS-IMP-001 requires a resource import example to match the resource importer or typed resource ID parser exactly, and DOCS-EVID-001 already says not to guess when repository evidence is missing.
assessments.selectionRationale: Severity 4 fits because a wrong import ID yields directly broken docs; frequency 4 and breadth 4 fit because many resource pages include imports; hostedDetectability 4 fits because reviewers can compare docs to importer or parser code when present; evidenceStrength 5 fits because the existing Hosted rule already captures the requirement; falsePositiveRisk 2 fits because code evidence is usually objective but still requires verification; redundancy 5 fits because the candidate is already covered by DOCS-IMP-001 plus DOCS-EVID-001.
assessments.proposedText: A resource import example must match the resource importer or typed resource ID parser exactly.

assessments.title: Import section must include standard wording and example
assessments.applicabilityRationale: This is a documentation import-section rule, but the new content beyond the current Hosted rule is mostly exact prose and article choice rather than core functional correctness.
assessments.summary: Keep DOCS-IMP-002 focused on the actionable import command instead of exact lead-in prose.
assessments.impactDescription: Expanding this rule to enforce article choice, singularization, and a fixed sentence template would spend guarded tokens on editorial uniformity while adding little defect-detection value beyond the existing command requirement.
assessments.currentHostedCoverage: DOCS-IMP-002 already requires a resource **Import** section to include a `shell` fenced `terraform import azurerm_<type>.example <resource_id>` command; the proposed extra sentence-shape requirements are not currently selected.
assessments.selectionRationale: Severity 2 fits because missing canonical lead-in wording is less harmful than a wrong import command; frequency 4 and breadth 4 fit because many resource docs have Import sections; hostedDetectability 5 fits because section text is easy to inspect; evidenceStrength 1 fits because the candidate cites no published or confirmed standard for the exact sentence template; falsePositiveRisk 3 fits because article choice and summary-name matching create editorial edge cases; redundancy 4 fits because DOCS-IMP-002 already covers the actionable command that matters most.
assessments.proposedText: A resource **Import** section must include a `shell` fenced `terraform import azurerm_<type>.example <resource_id>` command.

assessments.title: Import example determinism (stubs and placeholders)
assessments.applicabilityRationale: Hosted already reviews import correctness and required command shape, but the proposed zero-subscription and path-key placeholder algorithm is a brittle authoring convention rather than a broadly reliable defect rule.
assessments.summary: Do not add this placeholder-determinism rule to Hosted.
assessments.impactDescription: Excluding it keeps Hosted focused on import correctness instead of fragile placeholder normalization that can misfire on varied ARM ID segment names.
assessments.currentHostedCoverage: DOCS-IMP-001 and DOCS-IMP-002 already cover importer/parser correctness and the required `.example` import command; no active rule enforces the proposed placeholder algorithm.
assessments.proposedText: Resource import examples must use the `.example` instance name, the all-zero subscription ID stub, and placeholder path values derived from the preceding ARM ID segment key by singularizing plural keys when needed, preserving key casing, and appending `1` (for example `resourceGroups/resourceGroup1`).
assessments.selectionRationale: Severity 2 fits because inconsistent placeholders are mostly a consistency problem once import correctness is preserved; frequency 2 fits because import sections are limited; breadth 3 fits because the convention would touch many resource docs; hostedDetectability 3 fits because the derivation rule is only partly mechanical; evidenceStrength 1 fits because no upstream or maintainer authority is cited; falsePositiveRisk 4 fits because pluralization and path-segment heuristics are brittle; redundancy 3 fits because current import rules already cover the substantive defect cases, so exclusion is the safer recommendation.

assessments.title: Fix obvious typos and grammar
assessments.applicabilityRationale: This is an editorial quality preference, not a strong Hosted semantic review rule, because 'obvious' grammar remains subjective even with an unambiguous-fix qualifier.
assessments.summary: Do not add a general typo-and-grammar Hosted rule.
assessments.impactDescription: Excluding it avoids broad low-signal prose policing and keeps Hosted focused on evidence-backed documentation defects.
assessments.currentHostedCoverage: No active Hosted rule targets general grammar, and the current documentation catalog intentionally concentrates on schema accuracy, required structure, examples, imports, and specific wording conventions.
assessments.proposedText: Fix obvious documentation typos and grammar when the correct replacement is unambiguous and can be stated exactly.
assessments.selectionRationale: Severity 1 fits because most typos do not create semantic defects; frequency 4 fits because prose issues are common; breadth 4 fits because every doc page contains prose; hostedDetectability 2 fits because 'obvious' grammar still requires judgment; evidenceStrength 2 fits because the quality expectation is plausible but uncited here; falsePositiveRisk 4 fits because editorial judgments vary; redundancy 1 fits because no current Hosted rule covers general grammar, so the deciding factor is low-signal subjectivity, which supports exclusion.

assessments.title: Locale-neutral Microsoft Learn links
assessments.applicabilityRationale: The proposed link-normalization rule is objective, but it is a low-severity style preference rather than a material Hosted documentation defect standard.
assessments.summary: Do not add a Hosted rule for stripping locale segments from documentation URLs.
assessments.impactDescription: Excluding it preserves instruction budget for higher-impact correctness issues instead of URL-style normalization.
assessments.currentHostedCoverage: No active Hosted rule targets locale-neutral URL variants, and existing documentation rules focus on schema accuracy, required sections, examples, imports, and proven wording constraints.
assessments.proposedText: Prefer locale-neutral Microsoft Learn URLs; remove locale segments such as `/en-us/` unless the localized path is required.
assessments.selectionRationale: Severity 1 fits because locale segments usually do not break documentation; frequency 3 fits because Learn links appear regularly but not everywhere; breadth 4 fits because the pattern could arise across many docs; hostedDetectability 5 fits because the URL text is explicit; evidenceStrength 1 fits because no upstream or maintainer source is cited; falsePositiveRisk 1 fits because the pattern is objective; redundancy 0 fits because the catalog has no comparable rule, but the weak evidence and low defect severity still support exclusion.

assessments.title: Note markers must match severity
assessments.applicabilityRationale: Hosted can enforce note syntax, but mapping note text to informational, important, or high-impact severity is too subjective for a compact review rule.
assessments.summary: Do not add a Hosted rule that assigns note markers by perceived severity.
assessments.impactDescription: Excluding it avoids subjective findings about tone and emphasis while leaving room for an objective note-format rule.
assessments.currentHostedCoverage: No active Hosted rule assigns note severity markers; the closest gap is note syntax itself, not the semantic grading of note content.
assessments.proposedText: Use `-> **Note:**` for informational guidance, `~> **Note:**` for important operational guidance or pitfalls, and `!> **Note:**` for high-impact cautions or irreversible actions.
