assessments.selectionRationale: Severity 1 fits because wrong marker choice rarely changes documentation correctness; frequency 2 fits because not every page uses notes; breadth 3 fits because the idea spans documentation broadly; hostedDetectability 2 fits because severity assignment needs interpretation; evidenceStrength 1 fits because no authority is cited; falsePositiveRisk 4 fits because reviewers can disagree on severity; redundancy 1 fits because no current Hosted rule covers this exact concern, so the main reason to exclude it is subjectivity.

assessments.title: Required conditional notes must be documented
assessments.applicabilityRationale: This candidate is a direct match for an active Hosted rule, and its additional example-alignment clause is already handled by the current example-validity rules.
assessments.summary: Keep DOCS-NOTE-002 unchanged.
assessments.impactDescription: Leaving the catalog as-is preserves coverage for missing or contradictory conditional requirements without duplicating the example-validity rules.
assessments.currentHostedCoverage: DOCS-NOTE-002 already requires cross-field requirements, conflicts, and diff-time constraints to be documented and to agree with schema or implementation behavior; DOCS-EX-000 and DOCS-EX-010 cover examples that would violate real constraints.
assessments.selectionRationale: Severity 4 fits because missing or contradictory conditional requirements can make configuration invalid; frequency 3 fits because such constraints are common but not universal; breadth 4 fits because the rule spans many resource docs with cross-field logic; hostedDetectability 4 fits because schema and implementation evidence usually proves the requirement; evidenceStrength 4 fits because the candidate aligns with existing Hosted documentation-contract coverage; falsePositiveRisk 1 fits because findings can be tied to concrete evidence; redundancy 5 fits because the active rule, together with existing example-validity rules, already covers the operative requirement, so no catalog change is warranted.
assessments.proposedText: Cross-field requirements, conflicts, and diff-time constraints that affect valid configuration must be documented and must agree with schema or implementation behavior.

assessments.title: Note formatting
assessments.applicabilityRationale: This is a concise, independently enforceable documentation rule with direct upstream evidence and no current Hosted equivalent.
assessments.summary: Add a Hosted rule for exact note-block syntax.
assessments.impactDescription: Adding it would let Hosted catch malformed note markers with a simple, evidence-backed formatting rule that does not require schema interpretation.
assessments.currentHostedCoverage: No active Hosted rule currently enforces the exact `(->|~>|!>) **Note:** <text>` syntax for note blocks.
assessments.proposedText: Note blocks must use the exact format `(->|~>|!>) **Note:** <text>`.
assessments.selectionRationale: Severity 2 fits because note syntax is mainly a readability and template-conformance issue; frequency 3 fits because note blocks are common in resource docs; breadth 3 fits because it applies across documentation pages that use notes; hostedDetectability 5 fits because the required marker format is exact text; evidenceStrength 5 fits because direct upstream contributor guidance is cited; falsePositiveRisk 1 fits because the pattern is explicit; redundancy 1 fits because no active Hosted rule already covers note-block syntax, so adding a compact new rule is justified.

assessments.title: Note correctness
assessments.applicabilityRationale: The active Hosted note-accuracy rule already covers note content that contradicts schema or implementation behavior.
assessments.summary: Keep the existing note-correctness coverage in DOCS-NOTE-002.
assessments.impactDescription: No catalog change is needed because Hosted already flags unsupported note requirements and contradictory note content.
assessments.currentHostedCoverage: DOCS-NOTE-002 already requires cross-field and diff-time documentation to agree with schema or implementation behavior, and DOCS-EVID-001 already blocks unsupported claims.
assessments.selectionRationale: Severity 3 fits because incorrect note content can mislead users about valid configuration; frequency 3 fits because notes are common but not universal; breadth 4 fits because the concern spans many documentation pages; hostedDetectability 4 fits because contradictions can usually be proven from schema or implementation; evidenceStrength 5 fits because the current Hosted rule already encodes this exact evidence-backed requirement; falsePositiveRisk 1 fits because findings depend on concrete repository evidence; redundancy 5 fits because the candidate restates existing coverage, so no-change is the correct recommendation.
assessments.proposedText: Cross-field requirements, conflicts, and diff-time constraints that affect valid configuration must be documented and must agree with schema or implementation behavior.

assessments.title: Conditional requirements must use `~> **Note:**`
assessments.applicabilityRationale: Choosing `~>` instead of `->` for conditional-requirement notes is a style preference whose boundary is too subjective for Hosted enforcement.
assessments.summary: Do not add a Hosted rule that forces `~>` for conditional-requirement notes.
assessments.impactDescription: Excluding it avoids subjective severity-marker review while preserving the substantive requirement that important constraints be documented accurately.
assessments.currentHostedCoverage: No active Hosted rule chooses note marker severity; current coverage focuses on documenting real constraints and, if added from this batch, exact note syntax only.
assessments.proposedText: Notes that document conditional requirements, conflicts, or compatibility constraints that can prevent configuration errors must use `~> **Note:**`, not `-> **Note:**`.
assessments.selectionRationale: Severity 1 fits because marker choice rarely changes correctness; frequency 2 fits because only some docs use conditional notes; breadth 2 fits because the rule affects a narrow note subset; hostedDetectability 2 fits because deciding whether text is a conditional requirement still needs interpretation; evidenceStrength 1 fits because no authority is cited; falsePositiveRisk 4 fits because reviewers can disagree about which notes qualify; redundancy 2 fits because existing Hosted rules already cover the real defect of missing or wrong constraints, which supports exclusion of this style-only refinement.

assessments.title: ForceNew guidance must use `~> **Note:**`
assessments.applicabilityRationale: Hosted already enforces the substantive ForceNew sentence, but requiring a specific note marker for related guidance is a low-value stylistic extension.
assessments.summary: Do not add a Hosted rule that prescribes `~>` for ForceNew guidance notes.
assessments.impactDescription: Excluding it keeps ForceNew review anchored to exact required wording instead of subjective note emphasis.
assessments.currentHostedCoverage: DOCS-ARG-003 already enforces the exact ForceNew sentence for resource arguments; no active Hosted rule selects note severity markers.
assessments.proposedText: Use `~> **Note:**` for ForceNew-related guidance notes, including guidance meant to prevent ForceNew surprises.
assessments.selectionRationale: Severity 1 fits because marker choice does not change the core ForceNew warning; frequency 2 fits because only some arguments need ForceNew guidance; breadth 2 fits because the rule is narrow; hostedDetectability 2 fits because determining which note is 'ForceNew-related' is interpretive; evidenceStrength 1 fits because no authority is cited; falsePositiveRisk 4 fits because the scope boundary is fuzzy; redundancy 3 fits because DOCS-ARG-003 already covers the substantive ForceNew documentation requirement, so exclusion is appropriate.

assessments.title: Do not document breaking changes as notes
assessments.applicabilityRationale: This proposal depends on release-version context and documentation ownership outside the changed page, which makes it a weak fit for compact Hosted review guidance.
assessments.summary: Do not add a Hosted rule about routing breaking changes to changelogs or upgrade guides.
assessments.impactDescription: Excluding it avoids findings that require broader release-management context rather than page-local documentation defects.
assessments.currentHostedCoverage: No active Hosted rule governs changelog or upgrade-guide placement of breaking changes; the current documentation catalog stays focused on reference-doc correctness and completeness.
assessments.proposedText: Do not document breaking changes as resource documentation notes. Put breaking changes for a minor version in the changelog and breaking changes for a major version in the upgrade guide.
assessments.selectionRationale: Severity 2 fits because misplacing breaking-change communication can matter, but it is not a common reference-doc defect; frequency 1 fits because such cases are uncommon; breadth 2 fits because the rule touches a limited subset of changes; hostedDetectability 1 fits because reviewers need external versioning and release-context evidence; evidenceStrength 2 fits because the policy is plausible but uncited here; falsePositiveRisk 4 fits because 'breaking change' and proper destination can be disputed in-context; redundancy 0 fits because no current Hosted rule covers this, yet exclusion is still right because the rule is not a clean Hosted review fit.

assessments.title: De-duplicate equivalent notes
assessments.applicabilityRationale: Detecting whether differently phrased notes are semantically equivalent is too subjective and brittle for a Hosted review rule.
assessments.summary: Do not add a Hosted rule for merging semantically equivalent notes.
assessments.impactDescription: Excluding it avoids high-noise editorial findings about prose consolidation while leaving substantive note-accuracy review intact.
assessments.currentHostedCoverage: No active Hosted rule targets note deduplication; current note coverage addresses whether required constraints are present and correct, not whether prose could be merged.
assessments.proposedText: Do not keep separate notes that state the same conditional requirement or conflict. Merge equivalent or inverse-phrased notes into one note that states the full constraint clearly.
assessments.selectionRationale: Severity 1 fits because duplicate notes are mostly an editorial clarity issue; frequency 2 fits because the situation occurs but is not pervasive; breadth 2 fits because it affects a narrow subset of pages; hostedDetectability 1 fits because semantic equivalence across differently phrased notes is hard to prove mechanically; evidenceStrength 1 fits because no authority is cited; falsePositiveRisk 5 fits because reviewers can disagree strongly about equivalence; redundancy 0 fits because no current rule covers this, and the high subjectivity is exactly why exclusion is appropriate.

assessments.title: Data source, list-resource, ephemeral-resource, and function field notes are prohibited
assessments.applicabilityRationale: The cited evidence is descriptive and local rather than clearly normative, and a blanket prohibition on field-level notes risks conflicting with the stronger requirement to document real constraints when they matter.
assessments.summary: Do not add a Hosted rule that bans field-level notes across non-resource documentation types.
assessments.impactDescription: Excluding it avoids suppressing necessary caveats in data source, list-resource, ephemeral-resource, or function docs when correctness may require extra explanation.
assessments.currentHostedCoverage: No active Hosted rule bans field-level notes in non-resource docs; DOCS-NOTE-002 instead requires real configuration constraints to be documented when needed.
assessments.proposedText: In data source, list-resource, ephemeral-resource, and function docs, argument, attribute, and nested-field entries must stay definitional only. Do not use field-level `-> **Note:**`, `~> **Note:**`, or `!> **Note:**` blocks for caveats, setup guidance, conditional requirements, or extended explanations.
assessments.selectionRationale: Severity 2 fits because note overuse is mostly a style problem unless it suppresses needed guidance; frequency 2 fits because field-level notes are not universal in these doc types; breadth 4 fits because the rule would affect several documentation surfaces; hostedDetectability 5 fits because note markers are easy to spot; evidenceStrength 2 fits because the support comes from examples and a local safeguard rather than a clear published requirement; falsePositiveRisk 4 fits because some pages may legitimately need field-level caveats; redundancy 1 fits because there is no direct current ban, and the conflict with higher-priority accuracy rules supports exclusion.

assessments.title: Prefer boolean `*_enabled` over string toggles (observation-only)
assessments.applicabilityRationale: Hosted rules should target actionable defects, not observation-only schema design preferences, especially when the candidate itself says documentation must still describe the current schema accurately.
assessments.summary: Do not add this observation-only boolean-toggle preference to Hosted.
assessments.impactDescription: Excluding it keeps Hosted focused on real documentation or implementation defects instead of advisory schema redesign commentary.
assessments.currentHostedCoverage: Current documentation rules already require docs to match the actual schema, and implementation rules already address real schema defects; no Hosted rule is needed for a non-blocking design observation.
assessments.proposedText: When a two-state string enum functions as a boolean toggle, treat the preference for a boolean `*_enabled` field as an observation about schema design only. Document the current string field accurately and do not rewrite docs to a hypothetical boolean.
assessments.selectionRationale: Severity 2 fits because awkward string toggles can affect UX but are not automatically defects; frequency 2 fits because this pattern is occasional; breadth 3 fits because it can appear across services; hostedDetectability 2 fits because deciding whether an enum is 'effectively boolean' needs judgment; evidenceStrength 2 fits because the preference is plausible but uncited; falsePositiveRisk 5 fits because tri-state and service-specific nuances make overreporting likely; redundancy 3 fits because current Hosted rules already cover the actual correctness issues, so exclusion is appropriate.

assessments.title: Block vs inline vs map parity
assessments.applicabilityRationale: This is a high-value documentation defect class that is closely related to the existing argument-existence rule but not fully covered by it today.
assessments.summary: Update DOCS-ARG-001 to include structural-shape parity with schema.
assessments.impactDescription: Expanding the existing argument-coverage rule would let Hosted catch docs that invent nested blocks, flatten real blocks into scalars, or misdescribe maps and primitive collections.
assessments.currentHostedCoverage: DOCS-ARG-001 covers documented-argument existence and schema coverage, but it does not explicitly cover structural-shape mismatches such as documenting maps or primitive collections as blocks.
assessments.proposedText: Every documented argument must exist in schema, every schema-exposed argument relevant to the documented object must be documented, and documented structural shape must match schema. Do not document scalars, maps, or primitive collections as nested blocks, and do not document nested blocks as scalar fields.
assessments.selectionRationale: Severity 4 fits because structural-shape mismatches mislead users into writing invalid configuration; frequency 3 fits because nested blocks, maps, and primitive collections are common but not universal; breadth 4 fits because the issue spans many documentation pages; hostedDetectability 4 fits because schema types usually make the expected shape clear; evidenceStrength 4 fits because the requirement is directly grounded in schema reality even without a cited wording template; falsePositiveRisk 1 fits because mismatches can be proven from schema; redundancy 2 fits because DOCS-ARG-001 is related but incomplete, so an update rather than a separate rule is the right recommendation.

assessments.title: Block placement and phrasing by section
assessments.applicabilityRationale: The meaningful section-placement defects are already covered by current rules, while the proposed exact bullet and subsection phrases are too template-specific for Hosted selection.
assessments.summary: Do not add a separate Hosted rule for exact block bullet phrasing and subsection text.
assessments.impactDescription: Excluding it avoids over-specifying prose templates while preserving current coverage for arguments, attributes, and required sections.
assessments.currentHostedCoverage: DOCS-ARG-001, DOCS-ATTR-002, DOCS-STRUCT-001, and DOCS-FMT-001 already cover the substantive failures around section presence and argument-versus-attribute documentation.
assessments.proposedText: Under **Arguments Reference**, a block argument must use `* `<block>` - (Optional) A `<block>` block as defined below.` or `(Required)` when required, and the subsection heading `A `<block>` block supports the following:`. Under **Attributes Reference**, a block attribute must use `* `<block>` - A `<block>` block as defined below.` and the subsection heading `A `<block>` block exports the following:`.
assessments.selectionRationale: Severity 2 fits because wrong section placement can confuse readers but exact phrasing is mostly template polish; frequency 3 fits because many docs contain block sections; breadth 3 fits because the convention spans documentation broadly; hostedDetectability 5 fits because headings and bullet text are explicit; evidenceStrength 1 fits because no cited source establishes these exact phrases as current Hosted requirements; falsePositiveRisk 2 fits because placement is objective even if wording preference is not; redundancy 4 fits because existing rules already catch the meaningful semantic failures, so exclusion avoids unnecessary specificity.

assessments.title: Indefinite article for block headings
assessments.applicabilityRationale: This is a minor prose polish rule with negligible semantic value for Hosted review.
assessments.summary: Do not add a Hosted rule for choosing `A` versus `An` in block headings.
assessments.impactDescription: Excluding it keeps instruction space for materially useful documentation defects instead of copyediting minutiae.
assessments.currentHostedCoverage: No active Hosted rule addresses indefinite-article grammar in headings, and the current catalog intentionally prioritizes correctness over micro-style.
assessments.proposedText: In block subsection headings, use `An` when the backtick-stripped block name starts with `a`, `e`, `i`, `o`, or `u`; otherwise use `A`.
assessments.selectionRationale: Severity 0 fits because article choice does not affect documentation correctness; frequency 3 fits because block headings are common; breadth 3 fits because the pattern can recur widely; hostedDetectability 5 fits because the text is explicit; evidenceStrength 1 fits because no authority is cited; falsePositiveRisk 1 fits because the grammar check is objective; redundancy 0 fits because no current rule covers it, yet the negligible impact still makes exclusion the right outcome.

assessments.title: Block subsections placement and ordering
assessments.applicabilityRationale: This is a deterministic formatting convention, but it is low-severity and not important enough for Hosted rule budget.
assessments.summary: Do not add a Hosted rule for alphabetical block-subsection ordering after top-level bullets.
assessments.impactDescription: Excluding it avoids spending review budget on layout normalization that does not usually change doc correctness.
assessments.currentHostedCoverage: No active Hosted rule governs alphabetical ordering of block subsections; existing documentation rules focus on required sections and accurate content.
assessments.proposedText: Within **Arguments Reference** and **Attributes Reference**, place block subsections after all top-level bullets. When a section has multiple block subsections, order them alphabetically by block name.
assessments.selectionRationale: Severity 1 fits because subsection order mainly affects readability; frequency 3 fits because many pages contain multiple blocks; breadth 3 fits because the convention could apply broadly; hostedDetectability 5 fits because ordering is explicit; evidenceStrength 1 fits because no authority is cited; falsePositiveRisk 1 fits because the ordering test is objective; redundancy 0 fits because no current rule covers it, but the low impact still supports exclusion.

assessments.title: Primitive list/set parity
assessments.applicabilityRationale: This is a real defect pattern, but it is narrower than the broader structural-shape update recommended for DOCS-ARG-001 and does not need a separate Hosted rule.
assessments.summary: Do not add a separate rule for primitive collection shape because it is subsumed by the broader schema-shape update.
assessments.impactDescription: Excluding it avoids duplicating coverage while still addressing the defect through the recommended DOCS-ARG-001 update.
assessments.currentHostedCoverage: No active Hosted rule explicitly covers primitive collections today, but the broader DOCS-ARG-001 update proposed for structural-shape parity would cover this case.
assessments.proposedText: When schema defines a list or set of primitive values, document it as a list or set of values. Do not document a primitive list or set as a nested block with named subfields.
assessments.selectionRationale: Severity 4 fits because misdocumenting primitive collections as blocks can lead directly to invalid configuration; frequency 2 fits because this schema shape is common but narrower than general argument coverage; breadth 3 fits because it affects multiple docs without spanning every page; hostedDetectability 4 fits because schema types usually prove the expected collection shape; evidenceStrength 4 fits because the defect is grounded in schema reality; falsePositiveRisk 1 fits because the mismatch is objective; redundancy 5 fits because the broader structural-shape update to DOCS-ARG-001 already covers this case, so a separate rule would be duplicative.

assessments.title: Nested block argument ordering (Arguments Reference)
assessments.applicabilityRationale: This is a deterministic ordering convention, but it is primarily formatting guidance rather than a Hosted semantic defect rule.
assessments.summary: Do not add a Hosted rule for nested-field ordering inside block subsections.
assessments.impactDescription: Excluding it keeps Hosted focused on whether nested fields are accurate and complete, not on alphabetical presentation rules.
assessments.currentHostedCoverage: No active Hosted rule governs nested-field ordering; existing documentation rules already cover whether required arguments and constraints are documented correctly.
assessments.proposedText: Inside an **Arguments Reference** block subsection, order nested fields with required arguments first alphabetically, optional arguments next alphabetically, and `tags` last when present. Keep any note block directly attached to its field after reordering.
assessments.selectionRationale: Severity 1 fits because ordering mainly affects readability rather than correctness; frequency 3 fits because many block subsections list multiple nested fields; breadth 2 fits because the rule applies only inside nested argument sections; hostedDetectability 5 fits because order and required markers are explicit; evidenceStrength 1 fits because no authority is cited; falsePositiveRisk 1 fits because the ordering check is objective; redundancy 0 fits because no current rule covers it, but the low semantic impact supports exclusion.

assessments.title: Directional block references must match subsection position
assessments.applicabilityRationale: This is a local wording safeguard with limited user impact and no strong published authority, so it is not a good Hosted rule candidate.
assessments.summary: Do not add a Hosted rule for `as defined above` versus `as defined below` inside block subsections.
assessments.impactDescription: Excluding it avoids brittle wording review for a narrow cross-reference convention while preserving more important structural and accuracy checks.
assessments.currentHostedCoverage: No active Hosted rule governs directional cross-reference phrasing within block subsections.
assessments.proposedText: For same-section block subsection cross-references, use `as defined above` when the referenced block subsection appears earlier in the section and `as defined below` when it appears later. Top-level block bullets continue to use `as defined below`.
assessments.selectionRationale: Severity 1 fits because directional phrasing mistakes rarely change configuration guidance; frequency 2 fits because only some pages contain these cross-references; breadth 2 fits because the scope is narrow; hostedDetectability 3 fits because reviewers must reason about subsection order and local references; evidenceStrength 2 fits because the candidate cites only a local safeguard rationale; falsePositiveRisk 4 fits because cross-reference intent can be ambiguous; redundancy 0 fits because no current rule covers it, and its narrow, local nature supports exclusion.

assessments.title: Block subsection separators
assessments.applicabilityRationale: This is a repository-local formatting safeguard for audit-friendly markdown edits, not a Hosted review rule about correctness, required documentation structure, or implementation behavior.
assessments.summary: Exclude this divider-placement rule from the Hosted catalog.
assessments.impactDescription: Keeping it out of Hosted preserves focus on user-visible documentation defects instead of local patch-shaping conventions.
assessments.currentHostedCoverage: The current Hosted catalog intentionally covers documentation correctness, required sections, imports, examples, and wording, but not editorial `---` separators between subsection blocks.
assessments.proposedText: In **Arguments Reference** and **Attributes Reference**, insert `---` immediately before the first block subsection heading after the top-level bullet list and between adjacent block subsections. Do not insert `---` between ordinary top-level argument or attribute bullets.
assessments.selectionRationale: severity 0 because divider placement does not change semantic correctness or user guidance; frequency 2 because these sections appear regularly but not everywhere; breadth 1 because the rule only touches two documentation sections; hostedDetectability 5 because missing separators are trivial to spot; evidenceStrength 1 because the support is local audit practice only; falsePositiveRisk 1 because the pattern is objective when present; redundancy 0 because no Hosted rule covers it, and the combination of low impact and local-only evidence supports exclusion.

assessments.title: Required sections by doc type
assessments.applicabilityRationale: Required top-level section presence by documentation type is a compact, enforceable Hosted documentation rule and the current catalog already carries a narrower version of it.
assessments.summary: Expand the existing required-sections rule to cover list-resource, ephemeral-resource, and function docs in addition to resources and data sources.
assessments.impactDescription: Updating this rule would let Hosted catch missing or forbidden top-level sections across every supported reference-doc type, including each doc type's `Import` prohibition where applicable.
assessments.currentHostedCoverage: DOCS-STRUCT-001 currently covers required sections for resources and data sources only, leaving list-resource, ephemeral-resource, and function section requirements uncovered.
assessments.proposedText: Reference docs must contain the required top-level sections for their doc type: resources need **Example Usage**, **Arguments Reference**, **Attributes Reference**, and **Import**; data sources need **Example Usage**, **Arguments Reference**, and **Attributes Reference**, and must not contain **Import**; list resources need **Example Usage** and **Argument Reference**, and must not contain **Import**; ephemeral resources need **Example Usage**, **Argument Reference**, and **Attributes Reference**, and must not contain **Import**; functions need **Example Usage**, **Signature**, and **Arguments**, and must not contain a top-level **Import** section.
assessments.selectionRationale: severity 4 because missing required sections removes essential usage or reference information; frequency 4 because every new or edited reference page can drift here; breadth 5 because the candidate spans every supported doc type; hostedDetectability 5 because section headings and file paths are explicit; evidenceStrength 3 because the contract and existing Hosted rule establish the pattern even though only part of the expanded scope has upstream citations today; falsePositiveRisk 1 because section presence and forbidden sections are objective checks; redundancy 2 because the current rule covers only a subset of the scope, so an update adds distinct coverage rather than duplicating it.

assessments.title: Section order
assessments.applicabilityRationale: Section order by doc type is independently enforceable from headings and page layout, and no current Hosted documentation rule covers this failure mode.
assessments.summary: Add a Hosted rule for required section ordering by documentation type.
assessments.impactDescription: This would let Hosted flag reference pages that include the right sections but arrange them in a nonstandard sequence that breaks contributor templates and cross-page consistency.
assessments.currentHostedCoverage: Current Hosted documentation rules check section presence, introductions, and wording, but they do not enforce doc-type-specific section order.
assessments.proposedText: Reference docs must follow doc-type section order: resources and data sources place **Example Usage** before **Arguments Reference**, then **Attributes Reference**, then **Timeouts** if present, then **Import** for resources; list resources place **Example Usage** before **Argument Reference**; ephemeral resources place the required runtime note and summary before **Example Usage**, then **Argument Reference**, then **Attributes Reference**; functions place the required runtime note and summary before **Example Usage**, any additional example sections, **Signature**, and **Arguments**.
assessments.selectionRationale: severity 2 because wrong ordering usually harms consistency more than correctness; frequency 3 because structure drift is common in hand-edited docs; breadth 5 because the rule spans all supported doc types; hostedDetectability 4 because headings are explicit, though optional sections require a small amount of sequencing judgment; evidenceStrength 2 because the support is the current contract rather than cited upstream guidance; falsePositiveRisk 1 because the required order is mostly objective; redundancy 1 because no current Hosted rule covers ordering, so the uncovered but enforceable failure mode supports adding it.

assessments.title: Timeouts section presence
assessments.applicabilityRationale: This is already an active Hosted documentation rule with the same enforceable meaning and failure condition.
assessments.summary: Keep the existing Timeouts-section gating rule unchanged.
assessments.impactDescription: No catalog change is needed because Hosted already flags unnecessary or unsupported `Timeouts` sections based on schema evidence.
assessments.currentHostedCoverage: DOCS-STRUCT-003 already matches this candidate's requirement to include **Timeouts** only when the schema defines timeouts for the documented object.
assessments.selectionRationale: severity 3 because an incorrect `Timeouts` section misstates supported behavior; frequency 2 because not every object has timeouts; breadth 3 because the rule applies across multiple documentation types but only when timeouts exist; hostedDetectability 5 because section presence and schema-backed timeout support are straightforward to verify; evidenceStrength 4 because the rule is already established in the Hosted catalog and grounded in schema evidence; falsePositiveRisk 1 because the condition is objective; redundancy 5 because the current Hosted rule already covers the requirement completely, which supports no change.
assessments.proposedText: Include **Timeouts** only when the schema defines timeouts for the documented object.

assessments.title: Document title heading by doc type
assessments.applicabilityRationale: The H1 format is explicit, doc-type-specific, and reviewable from the page alone, while the current Hosted catalog does not validate visible title headings.
assessments.summary: Add a Hosted rule for the required H1 title format by documentation type.
assessments.impactDescription: This would catch mislabelled titles that identify the wrong Terraform object or the wrong documentation class even when frontmatter is otherwise correct.
assessments.currentHostedCoverage: Current Hosted rules validate required frontmatter keys and layout, but they do not enforce the page's top-level heading format.
assessments.proposedText: Reference doc H1 must match the doc type and Terraform name: resources use `# azurerm_<name>`; data sources use `# Data Source: azurerm_<name>`; list resources use `# List resource: azurerm_<name>`; ephemeral resources use `# Ephemeral: azurerm_<name>`; functions use `# Function: <name>`.
assessments.selectionRationale: severity 3 because a wrong H1 misidentifies the documented object and degrades reference usability; frequency 3 because the title is present on every page but only changes when docs are created or reworked; breadth 5 because the rule spans every doc type; hostedDetectability 5 because the H1 and file path are explicit; evidenceStrength 2 because the rule is contract-backed but not tied here to an upstream citation; falsePositiveRisk 1 because the required strings are exact; redundancy 1 because the current Hosted catalog checks frontmatter but not the visible heading, supporting a new rule.

assessments.title: Summary sentence must appear directly below the title
assessments.applicabilityRationale: Summary-sentence presence and placement are actionable documentation requirements, and current Hosted rules cover summary wording but not where the summary must appear.
assessments.summary: Add a Hosted rule that requires the summary sentence immediately below the title or required runtime note.
assessments.impactDescription: This would make missing or displaced summaries reviewable without changing the existing summary-wording safeguards.
assessments.currentHostedCoverage: DOCS-WORD-003 governs doc-type summary wording, but no current Hosted rule requires a summary sentence directly below the H1 or below a required runtime-support note.
assessments.proposedText: Immediately below the H1, or below a required runtime-support note, include a one-sentence summary that uses the doc-type-appropriate summary style.
assessments.selectionRationale: severity 3 because missing or misplaced summaries weaken the core description of the documented object; frequency 4 because every reference page needs one; breadth 5 because the rule spans all doc types; hostedDetectability 4 because title-adjacent placement is clear, though runtime-note exceptions add slight nuance; evidenceStrength 2 because the support is contractual rather than explicitly upstream-cited here; falsePositiveRisk 1 because the expected placement is concrete; redundancy 2 because existing Hosted coverage addresses wording but not required placement, so the rule adds distinct value.

assessments.title: Reference doc path and filename must match the Terraform name
assessments.applicabilityRationale: Reference-doc location and filename are deterministic repository conventions that can be enforced from the changed path and documented object name, and the current catalog does not cover them.
assessments.summary: Add a Hosted repository rule for doc path and filename alignment with the Terraform name.
assessments.impactDescription: This would catch misplaced or misnamed reference pages before they drift from the provider's naming and routing conventions.
assessments.currentHostedCoverage: Current Hosted rules validate documentation content, not where the reference file lives or whether its filename matches the Terraform name suffix.
assessments.proposedText: Reference doc location must match the documented Terraform name: `azurerm_<name>` resources live at `website/docs/r/<name>.html.markdown`, data sources at `website/docs/d/<name>.html.markdown`, list resources at `website/docs/list-resources/<name>.html.markdown`, ephemeral resources at `website/docs/ephemeral-resources/<name>.html.markdown`, functions at `website/docs/functions/<name>.html.markdown`, and the filename must match the type or function suffix exactly.
assessments.selectionRationale: severity 4 because a wrong path or filename breaks expected discoverability and doc naming consistency; frequency 2 because creation and rename events are episodic; breadth 5 because the rule spans every supported doc type; hostedDetectability 5 because the repository path and filename are explicit; evidenceStrength 2 because the support is the current contract rather than a cited upstream rule in this batch; falsePositiveRisk 0 because the mapping is deterministic; redundancy 1 because no Hosted rule currently covers reference-doc placement, which supports adding it.

assessments.title: Ephemeral-resource runtime support note
assessments.applicabilityRationale: An exact runtime-support note for ephemeral-resource docs is independently enforceable and user-facing, and current Hosted documentation rules do not cover it.
assessments.summary: Add a Hosted rule requiring the exact Terraform 1.10 support note in ephemeral-resource docs.
assessments.impactDescription: This would prevent ephemeral-resource pages from omitting the version gate that tells users when the feature is supported.
assessments.currentHostedCoverage: Current Hosted documentation rules mention ephemeral resources in scope but do not require the Terraform 1.10 runtime-support note.
assessments.proposedText: Ephemeral-resource docs must place the exact note `~> **Note:** Ephemeral Resources are supported in Terraform 1.10 and later.` immediately below the title and before the summary sentence.
assessments.selectionRationale: severity 3 because omitting the note hides a meaningful runtime prerequisite from users; frequency 2 because ephemeral-resource pages are a smaller subset of docs; breadth 2 because the rule only applies to one doc class; hostedDetectability 5 because the exact note and placement are explicit; evidenceStrength 2 because the requirement is contract-backed but not upstream-cited here; falsePositiveRisk 0 because the expected text is exact; redundancy 1 because the current Hosted catalog does not cover this note, supporting addition.

assessments.title: Function runtime support note
assessments.applicabilityRationale: The exact runtime-support note for function docs is a concrete, user-facing documentation requirement that is currently uncovered by Hosted rules.
assessments.summary: Add a Hosted rule requiring the exact Terraform/provider-version support note in function docs.
assessments.impactDescription: This would ensure function reference pages always disclose the minimum Terraform and provider versions that support provider-defined functions.
assessments.currentHostedCoverage: Current Hosted documentation rules cover function docs in scope and summary wording, but they do not require the function runtime-support note.
assessments.proposedText: Function docs must place the exact note `~> **Note:** Provider-defined functions are supported in Terraform 1.8 and later, and are available from version 4.0 of the provider.` immediately below the title and before the summary sentence.
assessments.selectionRationale: severity 3 because missing version-support guidance can mislead users about function availability; frequency 2 because function pages are a limited subset; breadth 2 because the rule applies only to function docs; hostedDetectability 5 because the exact note and its placement are explicit; evidenceStrength 2 because the support is the current contract rather than an upstream citation in this batch; falsePositiveRisk 0 because the text is exact; redundancy 1 because no current Hosted rule enforces this requirement, supporting a new rule.

assessments.title: Duration readability
assessments.applicabilityRationale: This is an editorial readability preference for representing long timeout defaults, not a Hosted rule about correctness, required structure, or schema-backed documentation accuracy.
assessments.summary: Exclude this timeout-unit style preference from the Hosted catalog.
assessments.impactDescription: Keeping it out of Hosted avoids spending review budget on prose normalization that does not materially change documented behavior.
assessments.currentHostedCoverage: The current Hosted catalog does not govern hour-versus-minute rendering inside `Timeouts` prose, and that omission keeps the docs surface focused on correctness rather than stylistic unit preference.
assessments.proposedText: In timeout prose, express defaults greater than 60 minutes in hours and keep values of 60 minutes or less in minutes. The stated duration must still match the schema default when one exists.
assessments.selectionRationale: severity 1 because either representation communicates the same timeout value; frequency 2 because only some docs include long timeout defaults; breadth 1 because the rule affects a narrow slice of timeout prose; hostedDetectability 5 because the unit wording is easy to spot; evidenceStrength 1 because no upstream or maintainer authority is cited here; falsePositiveRisk 2 because defaults can be unknown or intentionally mirrored from schema wording; redundancy 0 because no Hosted rule covers it, and the low-severity editorial nature supports exclusion instead of adoption.

assessments.title: Timeouts link format
assessments.applicabilityRationale: Preferred timeout-reference link selection is a documentation review topic, but this candidate depends on transitional new-versus-existing page context that the current Hosted catalog does not model cleanly.
assessments.summary: Defer a Hosted decision on timeout-link selection until the transition policy is firmer.
assessments.impactDescription: A future rule could steer new or touched `Timeouts` sections toward the newer HashiCorp URL, but premature adoption would create low-value churn around legacy links.
assessments.currentHostedCoverage: No current Hosted rule governs which external timeout-reference URL to use or when a legacy timeout link may remain unchanged.
assessments.proposedText: Use `https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/resources/configure#define-operation-timeouts` in **Timeouts** sections for newly added resources. Existing resources may keep the legacy `https://www.terraform.io/language/resources/syntax#operation-timeouts` link unless the section is being updated.
assessments.selectionRationale: severity 1 because both links still point users to timeout guidance; frequency 2 because only docs with `Timeouts` sections are affected; breadth 2 because the scope is narrow; hostedDetectability 3 because the link itself is explicit but 'new page' and 'section updated' context is less direct; evidenceStrength 1 because the candidate has no cited upstream or maintainer confirmation; falsePositiveRisk 3 because transition-state judgments can misfire on modified legacy docs; redundancy 0 because no Hosted rule covers timeout-link selection, so the weak evidence and context sensitivity support deferring rather than adding it now.

assessments.title: New vs existing timeouts link enforcement
assessments.applicabilityRationale: This is review-classification guidance for documentation findings, but it relies on an Observation-versus-Issue distinction that the current Hosted rule catalog does not encode.
assessments.summary: Defer this reviewer-behavior rule until Hosted review supports the same classification nuance.
assessments.impactDescription: Adopting it later could reduce noisy timeout-link findings when new-versus-existing status is uncertain, but adding it now would force a binary decision model onto a non-binary policy.
assessments.currentHostedCoverage: DOCS-EVID-001 already tells reviewers not to guess unsupported behavior, but the current Hosted catalog has no observation-only channel for uncertain new-versus-existing timeout-link cases.
assessments.proposedText: If available review context shows a documentation page is newly added, a **Timeouts** section must use the developer.hashicorp.com timeout link and a legacy link is an Issue. If the page is existing or modified, a legacy link is allowed; if page-newness cannot be determined from available context, record only an Observation.
assessments.selectionRationale: severity 1 because the candidate governs reviewer output classification rather than a documentation defect itself; frequency 2 because it only applies to docs with timeout links; breadth 2 because the scenario is narrow; hostedDetectability 1 because determining page-newness from available context is unreliable in a compact Hosted rule; evidenceStrength 1 because no stronger authority is cited here; falsePositiveRisk 4 because misclassifying uncertain cases would generate either missed guidance or noisy issues; redundancy 1 because DOCS-EVID-001 partially covers the 'do not guess' principle but not the requested output model, which supports deferring instead of forcing a poor fit.

assessments.title: ForceNew sentence
assessments.applicabilityRationale: The exact ForceNew wording is already an active Hosted documentation rule, and the current rule also carries the related non-resource prohibition.
assessments.summary: Keep the existing Hosted ForceNew wording rule unchanged.
assessments.impactDescription: No catalog change is needed because Hosted already flags incorrect ForceNew replacement wording and misuse of ForceNew phrasing outside resource docs.
assessments.currentHostedCoverage: DOCS-ARG-003 already requires the exact sentence `Changing this forces a new resource to be created.` for resource arguments with `ForceNew: true` and also forbids ForceNew wording in non-resource docs.
assessments.selectionRationale: severity 4 because wrong ForceNew wording can misstate replacement behavior; frequency 3 because ForceNew fields are common but not universal; breadth 3 because the rule applies broadly across resource docs but not every doc type; hostedDetectability 5 because the exact sentence is easy to verify against schema evidence; evidenceStrength 5 because the candidate cites upstream guidance and the Hosted rule is already active; falsePositiveRisk 0 because the required sentence is exact; redundancy 5 because DOCS-ARG-003 already covers this requirement completely and more, which supports no change.
assessments.proposedText: A resource argument with `ForceNew: true` must end with the exact sentence `Changing this forces a new resource to be created.` Non-resource documentation must not use ForceNew wording.

assessments.title: Enum wording
assessments.applicabilityRationale: Canonical possible-values wording is already represented directly in the Hosted catalog, and the current wording already makes legacy variants noncompliant.
assessments.summary: Keep the existing canonical possible-values wording rule unchanged.
assessments.impactDescription: No update is needed because Hosted already supports findings for non-canonical enum, single-value, and numeric-range phrasing.
assessments.currentHostedCoverage: DOCS-WORD-002 already requires `Possible values are ...`, `The only possible value is ...`, and `Possible values range between ...`; legacy variants like `Valid options are` or `Possible values include` are already defects under the current rule.
assessments.selectionRationale: severity 3 because non-canonical enum wording can blur validation guidance; frequency 4 because enum and range descriptions are common; breadth 4 because the rule applies across many argument descriptions; hostedDetectability 5 because the phrasing is explicit in docs; evidenceStrength 5 because the candidate cites upstream guidance and the Hosted rule is already active; falsePositiveRisk 1 because reviewers still need schema evidence for the underlying constraint; redundancy 5 because DOCS-WORD-002 already covers the enforceable meaning completely, supporting no change.
assessments.proposedText: Use `Possible values are ...` for multiple values, `The only possible value is ...` for one value, and `Possible values range between ...` for a numeric range.

assessments.title: Resource vs data source summary sentence
assessments.applicabilityRationale: Doc-type summary wording is already a Hosted rule, but this candidate usefully broadens the positive phrasing and adds an explicit cross-type misuse guard.
assessments.summary: Update the existing summary-wording rule to preserve doc-type distinctions while explicitly forbidding cross-type summary language.
assessments.impactDescription: This would keep the current resource, data source, list-resource, ephemeral-resource, and function summary safeguards while reducing unnecessary rigidity around exact opening verbs and making wrong-doc-type wording directly reviewable.
assessments.currentHostedCoverage: DOCS-WORD-003 currently captures the doc-type summary families, but it hard-codes narrower starts and does not explicitly state that summaries must not use another doc type's wording.
assessments.proposedText: Reference doc summaries must use doc-type-appropriate wording: resources start with an action verb such as `Manages ...`; data sources start with a retrieval verb such as `Gets information about ...`; list-resource docs start with `Lists ...`; ephemeral-resource docs start with `Use this to access information about ...`; function docs describe implementation-backed behavior. Do not use wording that describes a different doc type.
assessments.selectionRationale: severity 3 because incorrect summary wording can misclassify the documented object type; frequency 4 because every reference page carries a summary; breadth 5 because the rule spans all documentation classes; hostedDetectability 4 because the opening sentence is explicit, though function behavior wording allows some judgment; evidenceStrength 3 because the contract and current Hosted rule agree on doc-type-specific summaries even though the broader verb flexibility is local; falsePositiveRisk 2 because most cases are objective but some function summaries need interpretation; redundancy 2 because DOCS-WORD-003 already covers the core pattern but misses the broader phrasing and explicit cross-type prohibition, which supports an update.

assessments.title: `*_enabled` field phrasing
assessments.applicabilityRationale: This is a plausible documentation wording convention, but it is more prescriptive and inference-heavy than the current Hosted documentation rules and lacks strong supporting evidence.
assessments.summary: Defer this `_enabled` wording pattern until there is stronger evidence and a clearer defect threshold.
assessments.impactDescription: It could standardize many boolean descriptions, but adopting it now would risk style-only comments and awkward rewrites for fields whose natural language noun phrase is not obvious from the schema name.
assessments.currentHostedCoverage: DOCS-ARG-004 already covers the separate `Defaults to ...` sentence when a schema default exists, but no current Hosted rule prescribes a specific description formula for `_enabled` fields.
assessments.proposedText: In resource and data source docs, describe boolean fields ending in `_enabled` as `Whether <thing> is enabled.`. When a default exists, add a separate `Defaults to <value>.` sentence, and derive `<thing>` by removing `_enabled`, replacing underscores with spaces, and wrapping the result in backticks.
assessments.selectionRationale: severity 1 because alternate boolean wording rarely changes semantic meaning; frequency 4 because `_enabled` fields are common; breadth 3 because the pattern spans many resource and data source docs but not all arguments; hostedDetectability 3 because the suffix is explicit, though deriving the right noun phrase is not always trivial; evidenceStrength 1 because no upstream or maintainer confirmation is cited; falsePositiveRisk 4 because field-name-derived phrasing can be awkward or wrong for some domains; redundancy 3 because the default-sentence portion overlaps with DOCS-ARG-004 even though the wording formula itself is uncovered, which supports deferring instead of adding.

assessments.title: Oxford comma for lists
assessments.applicabilityRationale: The Oxford comma requirement is already an active Hosted documentation rule with the same enforceable meaning.
assessments.summary: Keep the existing Oxford-comma rule unchanged.
assessments.impactDescription: No update is needed because Hosted already flags missing Oxford commas in documentation prose lists, including possible-value lists.
assessments.currentHostedCoverage: DOCS-WORD-005 already requires the Oxford comma in documentation prose lists of three or more items, including enum and possible-value lists.
assessments.selectionRationale: severity 1 because this is a style consistency issue rather than a semantic defect; frequency 4 because three-item prose lists are common in docs; breadth 4 because the rule applies across many documentation sections; hostedDetectability 4 because list punctuation is visible, though some sentence structures need a quick read; evidenceStrength 4 because the Hosted catalog already carries maintainer-confirmed support for this requirement; falsePositiveRisk 1 because the rule is generally straightforward; redundancy 5 because DOCS-WORD-005 already covers the requirement fully, supporting no change.
assessments.proposedText: Use the Oxford comma in every documentation prose list of three or more items, including possible-value lists.

assessments.title: Use the canonical resource name in section prose
assessments.applicabilityRationale: This targets a real documentation-accuracy concern, but the current wording depends on extracting a canonical noun phrase from the summary sentence and judging when a broader Azure object name is actually wrong.
assessments.summary: Defer this resource-name wording safeguard until it can be stated more objectively.
assessments.impactDescription: A future rule could prevent section prose from drifting to a broader service-object name than the page actually documents, but the current formulation is too inference-heavy for reliable Hosted enforcement.
assessments.currentHostedCoverage: No current Hosted documentation rule enforces canonical resource naming inside **Attributes Reference**, **Timeouts**, or **Import** prose.
assessments.proposedText: In resource docs, prose in **Attributes Reference**, **Timeouts**, and **Import** that refers to the documented object must use the page's canonical resource name from the summary sentence, not a broader generic service-object name.
assessments.selectionRationale: severity 2 because broader service-object wording can be misleading but usually does not block use of the docs; frequency 2 because the drift appears in a narrower set of section prose; breadth 2 because the scope is limited to resource docs and a few sections; hostedDetectability 3 because obvious mismatches exist, but inferring the canonical noun phrase adds judgment; evidenceStrength 1 because the support is local-safeguard evidence only; falsePositiveRisk 4 because some broader names may still be acceptable prose depending on context; redundancy 1 because the failure mode is not covered today, but the ambiguity supports deferral instead of immediate adoption.

assessments.title: Use Azure proper-name capitalization in field prose
assessments.applicabilityRationale: This is a narrow term-specific capitalization preference with contextual ambiguity between proper-name and generic usage, which makes it a poor fit for the Hosted rule catalog.
assessments.summary: Exclude this single-term capitalization preference from the Hosted catalog.
assessments.impactDescription: Keeping it out of Hosted avoids spending rule budget on a micro-style convention that is too narrow and too context-sensitive to justify a standalone review rule.
assessments.currentHostedCoverage: The current Hosted catalog does not enforce object-name capitalization for specific Azure terms, and that omission keeps documentation review focused on broader correctness and structure issues.
assessments.proposedText: When prose refers to the Azure object name, capitalize `Resource Group` rather than `resource group`, including common field descriptions such as `resource_group_name`.
assessments.selectionRationale: severity 1 because capitalization here rarely changes the substantive meaning of the docs; frequency 3 because `resource_group_name` appears often; breadth 1 because the candidate is effectively about one term; hostedDetectability 3 because the text is visible but generic-versus-proper-name usage still needs judgment; evidenceStrength 2 because there is some review and companion-guideline support but not a strong published requirement; falsePositiveRisk 4 because context can make lowercase legitimate; redundancy 0 because no Hosted rule covers it, and the narrow, ambiguous scope supports exclusion rather than adoption.

assessments.title: Avoid unnecessary comments
assessments.applicabilityRationale: Comment necessity is relevant to implementation review, but this candidate is a broad maintainability heuristic rather than a sharply bounded defect rule in the style of the current Hosted implementation catalog.
assessments.summary: Defer adding a Hosted implementation rule for unnecessary comments until the defect threshold is sharper.
assessments.impactDescription: A future rule could reduce noisy or redundant comments, but adopting this version now would likely produce style-only findings and inconsistent reviewer judgment.
assessments.currentHostedCoverage: No current Hosted implementation rule addresses whether comments are necessary, self-documenting code is sufficient, or a comment should be replaced by refactoring.
assessments.proposedText: Prefer self-documenting code. Add comments only for non-obvious Azure quirks, Azure SDK workarounds or limitations, complex business logic that cannot be made self-explanatory, or non-obvious state-management patterns; do not add comments for obvious assignments, standard Terraform or Go patterns, field mappings, or routine error and nil-check flow.
assessments.selectionRationale: severity 1 because unnecessary comments usually affect maintainability more than correctness; frequency 4 because comment quality comes up regularly in code changes; breadth 4 because the concern can appear anywhere in implementation code; hostedDetectability 3 because obviously redundant comments are visible but many cases are subjective; evidenceStrength 2 because the candidate reflects a plausible convention without strong source backing in the Hosted catalog; falsePositiveRisk 4 because reviewer opinions differ on what is 'obvious' or 'irreducible'; redundancy 2 because the catalog does not have a comment-specific rule but the concern overlaps with broader maintainability judgment, which supports deferring instead of adding a vague rule now.

assessments.title: Avoid redundant lifecycle/provider logging by default
assessments.applicabilityRationale: This is a maintainability preference about log volume and placement, not a defect-focused Hosted rule with a crisp pass/fail threshold.
assessments.summary: Exclude this from Hosted because the rule depends on subjective judgments about whether a log line adds enough diagnostic value.
assessments.impactDescription: Over-enforcing it would shift review toward taste-based arguments about verbosity instead of catching correctness defects.
assessments.currentHostedCoverage: No current Hosted rule covers lifecycle log verbosity, and the implementation catalog is intentionally scoped to correctness, schema, PATCH, identity, and error behavior.
assessments.proposedText: Do not add generic per-resource lifecycle log lines that only repeat Terraform core or provider-native logging. Add provider-side logging only when it contributes unique diagnostic value; targeted not-found or removing-from-state diagnostics are the narrow default exception.
assessments.selectionRationale: Severity is 1 because redundant lifecycle logging is usually noise rather than a functional bug; frequency is 2 because the pattern appears occasionally but is not pervasive; breadth is 2 because it affects a narrow slice of implementation review; hostedDetectability is 3 because added log strings are visible in diffs but their value is not mechanically obvious; evidenceStrength is 4 because the maintainer comments are clear; falsePositiveRisk is 5 because unique diagnostic value is highly subjective; redundancy is 1 because the catalog does not already cover this topic, which supports excluding it rather than merging it into an unrelated rule.

assessments.title: Use provider-standard error wording
assessments.applicabilityRationale: This is a core implementation error-handling rule already represented in the Hosted implementation catalog.
assessments.summary: No change: current Hosted rule IMPL-ERR-001 already preserves the candidate's wording, wrapping, and static-error requirements.
assessments.impactDescription: Consistent error wording improves diagnostics, user readability, and provider-wide review consistency.
assessments.currentHostedCoverage: IMPL-ERR-001 already requires lowercase errors, backticks for fields and values, `%+v` for wrapped errors, and `errors.New(...)` for static messages, while also retaining still-valid safeguards about context, punctuation, and `fmt.Errorf(...)` use.
assessments.selectionRationale: Severity is 4 because poor provider errors materially hurt diagnosis; frequency is 4 because error construction is common across resources and data sources; breadth is 4 because the convention applies throughout implementation code; hostedDetectability is 5 because message strings and wrappers are directly reviewable in diffs; evidenceStrength is 5 because the cited contributor guides are explicit; falsePositiveRisk is 1 because the requirements are concrete; redundancy is 5 because the active Hosted rule already contains the same safeguards, so no catalog change is needed.
assessments.proposedText: Provider errors must be lowercase, add the operation and resource context needed to diagnose the failure, wrap field names and values in backticks, avoid contractions and terminal punctuation, and use `%+v` for underlying errors. Use `errors.New(...)` for static messages that do not wrap an error or require formatting; use `fmt.Errorf(...)` only when formatting values or wrapping context.

assessments.title: Do not wrap comprehensive ID parser errors with redundant context
assessments.applicabilityRationale: This is an implementation error-handling rule already represented in the Hosted implementation catalog.
assessments.summary: No change: current Hosted rule IMPL-ERR-002 already captures the requirement to return comprehensive parser errors directly unless extra context truly helps.
assessments.impactDescription: Returning parser errors directly avoids burying already good diagnostics under repetitive wrapping noise.
assessments.currentHostedCoverage: IMPL-ERR-002 already tells reviewers to return comprehensive typed resource ID parser errors directly and to allow wrapping only when it materially improves diagnosis.
assessments.selectionRationale: Severity is 3 because redundant wrapping weakens but does not usually break diagnostics; frequency is 3 because ID parsing is common but not universal; breadth is 3 because the issue spans many Azure ID paths; hostedDetectability is 4 because return and wrap patterns are visible in code; evidenceStrength is 4 because the maintainer guidance is direct; falsePositiveRisk is 2 because comprehensiveness can be judged from the parser error text with limited ambiguity; redundancy is 5 because the active Hosted rule already matches the candidate's failure condition.
assessments.proposedText: Return already comprehensive typed resource ID parser errors directly. Wrap them only when the additional context materially improves diagnosis.

assessments.title: Do not guess API model structure
assessments.applicabilityRationale: This is a review evidence rule for implementation work and is already represented in the Hosted catalog.
assessments.summary: No change: current Hosted rule IMPL-EVID-001 already captures the core prohibition on inferring Azure model details.
assessments.impactDescription: Guessing model structure causes wrong schema mappings, bad request shapes, and follow-on CRUD defects.
assessments.currentHostedCoverage: IMPL-EVID-001 already requires reviewers to verify field types, required properties, enum values, and PATCH semantics against generated SDK models and the selected API version, which covers the candidate's central failure condition with a sharper evidence anchor.
assessments.selectionRationale: Severity is 5 because inferred Azure model details can create real implementation defects; frequency is 4 because model-mapping work is common; breadth is 5 because it applies across services and implementation models; hostedDetectability is 3 because reviewers can often spot unsupported guesses but sometimes need extra context; evidenceStrength is 1 because this candidate itself cites no supporting source; falsePositiveRisk is 2 because concrete SDK evidence usually resolves disputes; redundancy is 5 because the active Hosted rule already covers the same review behavior.
assessments.proposedText: Do not infer Azure field types, required properties, enum values, or PATCH semantics. Verify them against generated SDK models and the selected API version.

assessments.title: Use nearby implementations before inventing new patterns
assessments.applicabilityRationale: This could guide implementation review, but the evidence and threshold are not yet specific enough for reliable Hosted enforcement.
assessments.summary: Defer this rule because it points at a useful review instinct, but the candidate has no cited evidence and the 'closest pattern' threshold is too subjective for Hosted selection.
assessments.impactDescription: If selected too early, reviewers could block legitimate service-specific designs merely because they differ from a nearby example.
assessments.currentHostedCoverage: No current Hosted implementation rule requires same-service pattern reuse, although IMPL-WF-001A and the implementation introduction already push reviewers to preserve the existing implementation model.
assessments.proposedText: When changing a service, follow the nearest same-service implementation for schema shape, CRUD flow, flatten/expand patterns, and timeouts unless changed evidence shows that pattern does not fit the new scenario.
assessments.selectionRationale: Severity is 2 because pattern drift is usually a maintainability problem rather than a direct bug; frequency is 4 because reviewers often compare against nearby implementations; breadth is 4 because the idea spans many services; hostedDetectability is 2 because identifying the right comparison target is subjective; evidenceStrength is 0 because the candidate provides no supporting evidence; falsePositiveRisk is 4 because acceptable service-local deviations are common; redundancy is 3 because existing model-preservation guidance partially overlaps without fully encoding this heuristic, which supports deferring rather than adding now.

assessments.title: Explicitly disable features in PATCH flows
assessments.applicabilityRationale: This is a core Azure update-semantics rule already represented in the Hosted implementation catalog.
assessments.summary: No change: current Hosted rule IMPL-PATCH-001 already captures the need to send explicit clearing values when Azure PATCH preserves omitted state.
assessments.impactDescription: Missing explicit disable values leaves stale remote configuration behind and creates persistent drift.
assessments.currentHostedCoverage: IMPL-PATCH-001 already states that omitted properties preserved by Azure must be cleared with an explicit disabled, empty, or sentinel value and that returning `nil` is defective when serialization would omit the field.
assessments.selectionRationale: Severity is 5 because this defect causes real drift and broken disable behavior; frequency is 3 because it appears in PATCH-style features rather than every resource; breadth is 4 because Azure PATCH semantics recur across services; hostedDetectability is 4 because reviewers can inspect expand and update paths; evidenceStrength is 1 because this candidate itself cites no source; falsePositiveRisk is 1 because omitted-versus-explicit clear behavior is concrete once API semantics are known; redundancy is 5 because the active Hosted rule already covers the same defect.
assessments.proposedText: If Azure PATCH preserves omitted properties, removing Terraform configuration must expand an explicit disabled, empty, or sentinel value that clears the remote feature. Returning `nil` is a defect when SDK serialization would omit the field and preserve stale Azure state.

assessments.title: Schema requirements must match real behavior
assessments.applicabilityRationale: This is a foundational implementation schema rule already represented in the Hosted catalog.
assessments.summary: No change: current Hosted rule IMPL-SCHEMA-001 already preserves this schema-accuracy requirement and retains broader still-valid safeguards.
assessments.impactDescription: Schema declarations that do not match actual behavior lead to invalid plans, broken CRUD, and non-round-trippable state.
assessments.currentHostedCoverage: IMPL-SCHEMA-001 already covers required, optional, computed, ForceNew, defaults, conflicts, and validation, and it explicitly tells reviewers to flag schema that permits invalid requests, rejects valid configuration, or cannot round-trip state.
assessments.selectionRationale: Severity is 5 because schema mismatches create high-impact provider defects; frequency is 5 because schema work is pervasive; breadth is 5 because the rule spans resources, data sources, and models; hostedDetectability is 4 because changed schema and lifecycle flags are visible in diffs; evidenceStrength is 1 because this candidate itself is uncited; falsePositiveRisk is 2 because repository and API evidence usually settle the right behavior; redundancy is 5 because the active Hosted rule already encodes this requirement and more.
assessments.proposedText: Required, optional, computed, ForceNew, defaults, conflicts, and validation must match actual API and lifecycle behavior. Flag schema declarations that permit invalid requests, reject valid configuration, or cannot round-trip state.

assessments.title: Common field ordering should follow provider conventions
assessments.applicabilityRationale: This is a formatting and consistency convention rather than a defect-focused Hosted rule.
assessments.summary: Exclude this from Hosted because common-field ordering is a style convention, not a semantic defect threshold.
assessments.impactDescription: Enforcing field order in Hosted would spend review budget on cosmetic schema layout instead of correctness and behavior.
assessments.currentHostedCoverage: No current Hosted rule covers schema field ordering, and that omission is consistent with the catalog's defect-oriented scope.
assessments.proposedText: When common fields are present, order them to match provider conventions: keep core identifier fields first, place `location` near the top, put `tags` last, and stay consistent with nearby same-service schemas unless changed evidence justifies a different layout.
assessments.selectionRationale: Severity is 1 because ordering errors are cosmetic; frequency is 3 because common fields appear often; breadth is 3 because the convention spans many resources and data sources; hostedDetectability is 5 because ordering is trivial to see in diffs; evidenceStrength is 5 because the upstream guides are explicit; falsePositiveRisk is 4 because acceptable local deviations for readability or generated layout are plausible; redundancy is 2 because the topic is mostly uncovered, which supports an explicit exclusion rather than forcing it into a semantic rule.

assessments.title: Generic fallback validators are last-resort, not the target state
assessments.applicabilityRationale: This is an implementation validation rule whose failure condition is already covered by the existing Hosted schema-accuracy rule.
assessments.summary: No change: current Hosted rule IMPL-SCHEMA-001 already lets reviewers flag generic validators when concrete constraints are known.
assessments.impactDescription: Using fallback validators in place of real enums, ranges, formats, or ID constraints permits invalid requests and weakens practitioner feedback.
assessments.currentHostedCoverage: IMPL-SCHEMA-001 already requires validation to match actual API and lifecycle behavior, and IMPL-SCHEMA-004 separately covers evidence-backed enum helper selection, so the candidate's concrete examples are already reviewable without a catalog change.
assessments.selectionRationale: Severity is 4 because weak validation can cause real bad requests and poor UX; frequency is 4 because validator choice is common schema work; breadth is 4 because the issue spans many services; hostedDetectability is 4 because the chosen validator is visible in diffs; evidenceStrength is 5 because the upstream guidance is explicit; falsePositiveRisk is 2 because stronger constraints should be added only when evidence is known; redundancy is 5 because existing Hosted schema rules already cover this failure condition.
assessments.proposedText: Required, optional, computed, ForceNew, defaults, conflicts, and validation must match actual API and lifecycle behavior. Flag schema declarations that permit invalid requests, reject valid configuration, or cannot round-trip state.

assessments.title: Prefer SDK PossibleValues helpers for enum validation unless the real accepted subset is narrower
assessments.applicabilityRationale: This is an implementation validation rule already represented in the Hosted catalog.
assessments.summary: No change: current Hosted rule IMPL-SCHEMA-004 already captures the requirement to use SDK enum helpers only when they match the accepted set.
assessments.impactDescription: Correct enum validation prevents invalid requests while avoiding arbitrary narrowing unsupported by service evidence.
assessments.currentHostedCoverage: IMPL-SCHEMA-004 already tells reviewers to prefer generated `PossibleValuesFor...()` helpers when they match the accepted set and to require service-specific evidence for a narrower validator; that already covers the candidate's warning against mixing unrelated values.
assessments.selectionRationale: Severity is 4 because bad enum validation can create real request failures; frequency is 3 because not every field is an enum; breadth is 3 because the pattern recurs across services but only on enum-backed inputs; hostedDetectability is 4 because validators and helper choices are visible in code; evidenceStrength is 5 because the upstream validation guidance is strong; falsePositiveRisk is 2 because accepted-set evidence usually resolves the right validator; redundancy is 5 because the active Hosted rule already encodes the same selection logic.
assessments.proposedText: Prefer generated SDK `PossibleValuesFor...()` helpers for enum validation when they represent the accepted set. A narrower validator requires service-specific evidence.

assessments.title: Prefer inline composition; extract only genuinely complex bespoke validation
assessments.applicabilityRationale: This is primarily code-organization guidance about where validation logic lives, not a defect-focused Hosted review rule.
assessments.summary: Exclude this from Hosted because it governs validator placement and abstraction style rather than semantic correctness.
assessments.impactDescription: Selecting it would steer reviews toward refactoring taste and file layout instead of catching broken validation behavior.
assessments.currentHostedCoverage: No current Hosted rule addresses inline-versus-extracted validator organization, and the catalog otherwise treats validation as a correctness topic rather than a structure preference.
assessments.proposedText: Compose established validators inline in the schema when they clearly express the constraint; extract a named service-local validator and matching unit test only for genuinely bespoke logic that needs custom control flow, and do not create wrapper-only validator files or tests for readable helper composition.
assessments.selectionRationale: Severity is 1 because validator placement rarely changes runtime behavior by itself; frequency is 2 because the pattern is occasional; breadth is 2 because it affects a narrow coding-style choice; hostedDetectability is 4 because custom validator files and wrappers are easy to see; evidenceStrength is 4 because the cited review precedent is concrete; falsePositiveRisk is 5 because 'genuinely complex' is subjective; redundancy is 1 because the catalog does not otherwise cover this style concern, which supports excluding it instead of forcing a semantic rule.

assessments.title: Normalize resource IDs before setting them into state
assessments.applicabilityRationale: This is an implementation state-normalization rule already in the Hosted catalog, but the upstream guidance adds materially useful scope that the current wording only implies.
assessments.summary: Update IMPL-SCHEMA-006 to explicitly cover scoped IDs, nested-property IDs, and read/import/refresh/migration paths, not just the main Azure-returned resource ID write path.
assessments.impactDescription: Without the expansion, reviewers may miss casing drift and phantom-diff defects when IDs appear outside the primary ID field or in comparison-heavy lifecycle paths.
assessments.currentHostedCoverage: Current IMPL-SCHEMA-006 already requires canonicalizing Azure-returned IDs before writing state, but it does not explicitly state that the same normalization applies to scoped IDs, nested property IDs, and comparison paths such as import, refresh, and migrations.
assessments.proposedText: Normalize resource IDs with the shared typed parser before writing them to state or comparing Azure-returned IDs. Apply this to full resource IDs, separately scoped IDs, and nested-property IDs in read, import, refresh, and migration paths, and persist the parser's canonical `.ID()` form whenever a typed parser exists.
