assessments.selectionRationale: severity 2 because the problem is incorrect labeling rather than broken behavior; frequency 2 because every function doc needs the field but function pages are a small subset; breadth 1 because it affects only function docs; hostedDetectability 5 because the value format is exact; evidenceStrength 4 because the maintainer audit identifies this as a real missing requirement; falsePositiveRisk 1 because the distinction from resource naming is explicit; redundancy 1 because current Hosted frontmatter coverage checks only field presence.

assessments.title: Ephemeral-resource runtime support note
assessments.applicabilityRationale: This is an exact wording-and-placement requirement for a specialized doc type, which Hosted can enforce directly from the page content.
assessments.summary: Add a rule requiring the exact ephemeral-resource Terraform version support note near the top of the page.
assessments.impactDescription: Missing or altered wording can hide the Terraform version floor for ephemeral resources and mislead users about feature availability.
assessments.currentHostedCoverage: DOCS-STRUCT-001 and DOCS-WORD-003 cover required sections and summary phrasing, but no active Hosted rule requires the ephemeral-resource support note or its placement.
assessments.proposedText: Ephemeral-resource docs must include the exact note `~> **Note:** Ephemeral Resources are supported in Terraform 1.10 and later.` between the title and the summary sentence.
assessments.selectionRationale: severity 3 because the note communicates an actual version gate users need; frequency 2 because every ephemeral page needs it but the surface is narrow; breadth 1 because only ephemeral-resource docs are affected; hostedDetectability 5 because both text and placement are exact; evidenceStrength 4 because the requirement comes from the maintainer-reviewed contributor guidance; falsePositiveRisk 1 because the mandated note is explicit; redundancy 1 because no current Hosted rule covers this top-of-page runtime note.

assessments.title: Function runtime support note
assessments.applicabilityRationale: This is a deterministic top-of-page note requirement for function docs, so Hosted can review it from the changed markdown without extra policy judgment.
assessments.summary: Add a rule requiring the exact function runtime support note and placement.
assessments.impactDescription: If the note is missing or changed, function docs can misstate the Terraform and provider versions needed for provider-defined functions.
assessments.currentHostedCoverage: Current Hosted documentation rules do not require the function-specific runtime note; existing structure and wording rules do not cover this version-gating text.
assessments.proposedText: Function docs must include the exact note `~> **Note:** Provider-defined functions are supported in Terraform 1.8 and later, and are available from version 4.0 of the provider.` between the title and the summary sentence.
assessments.selectionRationale: severity 3 because the note carries real compatibility requirements; frequency 2 because every function page needs it but function docs are limited in count; breadth 1 because only function docs are affected; hostedDetectability 5 because the required sentence and position are exact; evidenceStrength 4 because the maintainer audit surfaced it as a genuine gap; falsePositiveRisk 1 because the expected wording is explicit; redundancy 1 because the current catalog has no equivalent function support-note rule.

assessments.title: Legacy (non-vNext) fields must not be documented
assessments.applicabilityRationale: This is an evidence-backed documentation-scope rule: Hosted already compares docs against schema and implementation evidence, and this candidate defines when legacy-only fields are out of scope.
assessments.summary: Add a rule that excludes legacy-only, non-vNext fields from **Arguments Reference** and **Attributes Reference**.
assessments.impactDescription: Without this rule, docs can surface fields users cannot configure or rely on in the current surface, creating misleading reference material.
assessments.currentHostedCoverage: DOCS-ARG-001 and DOCS-ATTR-002 require documenting the active surface, but no active Hosted rule explicitly forbids documenting legacy-only fields that sit outside vNext.
assessments.proposedText: When schema or implementation evidence shows a field is legacy-only and outside the vNext surface, do not document it under **Arguments Reference** or **Attributes Reference**.
assessments.selectionRationale: severity 4 because documenting unavailable fields materially misleads users; frequency 2 because the issue appears mainly on migration or legacy-boundary pages; breadth 3 because it can affect both arguments and attributes across multiple doc types; hostedDetectability 3 because reviewers need repository evidence rather than pure text matching; evidenceStrength 4 because the maintainer audit ties the rule to real source behavior; falsePositiveRisk 2 because reviewers must distinguish legacy-only from merely uncommon fields; redundancy 2 because current coverage is only partial and not explicit about vNext boundaries.

assessments.title: Preserve required `depends_on` verbatim when rewriting examples
assessments.applicabilityRationale: This is a documentation-example correctness rule with a concrete failure mode, and Hosted can apply it when changed examples rewrite existing dependency edges.
assessments.summary: Add an example-rewrite safeguard that preserves required `depends_on` edges instead of weakening or deleting them.
assessments.impactDescription: Dropping or altering an existing required dependency can make a rewritten example flaky or semantically wrong even when it looks more self-contained.
assessments.currentHostedCoverage: DOCS-EX-000 and DOCS-EX-003 require functional, declared examples, but no active Hosted rule explicitly preserves existing required `depends_on` relationships during rewrites.
assessments.proposedText: When rewriting an example, preserve any existing required `depends_on` with the same referenced objects. Make the example self-contained by declaring missing objects, not by weakening or removing `depends_on`.
assessments.selectionRationale: severity 3 because the defect changes ordering semantics and can break real usage guidance; frequency 2 because it appears mainly during rewrites rather than on every page; breadth 2 because the pattern can recur across resource examples; hostedDetectability 3 because reviewers must compare before-and-after dependencies and supporting evidence; evidenceStrength 4 because the candidate comes from a maintainer-audited convention; falsePositiveRisk 2 because some dependency edits are legitimate when behavior changes; redundancy 2 because current example rules do not directly guard this failure mode.

assessments.title: Do not introduce net-new `depends_on` without evidence
assessments.applicabilityRationale: This is an evidence-gated documentation-example rule with a specific anti-guessing requirement, which fits Hosted's docs review scope.
assessments.summary: Add a rule that blocks invented `depends_on` edges unless schema or implementation evidence proves they are required.
assessments.impactDescription: Invented ordering can cargo-cult nonexistent dependencies into examples and misteach users about actual provider or Terraform behavior.
assessments.currentHostedCoverage: DOCS-EVID-001 forbids guessing generally, but no active Hosted documentation rule specifically governs newly introduced `depends_on` in examples.
assessments.proposedText: Do not add a new `depends_on` to a documentation example unless schema or implementation evidence shows the ordering requirement is real.
assessments.selectionRationale: severity 3 because fake ordering requirements distort documented behavior; frequency 2 because the pattern is occasional and rewrite-driven; breadth 2 because it can affect many example pages but only one aspect of them; hostedDetectability 3 because reviewers need supporting evidence instead of pure text matching; evidenceStrength 4 because the maintainer audit classifies it as a genuine requirement; falsePositiveRisk 2 because some real dependencies exist and must be distinguished; redundancy 1 because current rules lack a focused `depends_on` addition guard.

assessments.title: Preserve example-adjacent notes when rewriting examples
assessments.applicabilityRationale: The candidate is a documentation-note accuracy rule, which Hosted already handles through the existing requirement to document constraints and keep them aligned with actual behavior.
assessments.summary: Leave the catalog unchanged because missing or inaccurate sequencing and validation notes are already reviewable under the existing note rule.
assessments.impactDescription: Removing a still-needed example note is harmful, but the current note-coverage rule already yields the same actionable finding when the note conveys required behavior.
assessments.currentHostedCoverage: DOCS-NOTE-002 already requires cross-field requirements, conflicts, and diff-time constraints that affect valid configuration to remain documented and accurate, which covers still-required example-adjacent sequencing or validation notes.
assessments.selectionRationale: severity 3 because losing a required note can mislead users; frequency 2 because it mainly arises during example rewrites; breadth 2 because it affects a subset of documentation notes rather than the whole page; hostedDetectability 3 because reviewers still need evidence that the note remains required; evidenceStrength 4 because the requirement is maintainer-audited; falsePositiveRisk 1 because a note tied to a real constraint is usually clear; redundancy 4 because DOCS-NOTE-002 already covers the same failure condition closely enough that no catalog change is needed.
assessments.proposedText: Cross-field requirements, conflicts, and diff-time constraints that affect valid configuration must be documented and must agree with schema or implementation behavior.

assessments.title: Do not replace Terraform references with invented literals
assessments.applicabilityRationale: This is a concrete documentation-example integrity rule that Hosted can apply to changed Terraform snippets and surrounding prose.
assessments.summary: Add a rule that forbids replacing Terraform references with invented literals when fixing example self-containedness.
assessments.impactDescription: Swapping references for made-up literals can change the resource graph, hide prerequisites, and teach users values they cannot actually derive from the documented configuration.
assessments.currentHostedCoverage: DOCS-EX-003 requires declaring referenced objects, but no active Hosted rule prevents removing those references by substituting fabricated literal values.
assessments.proposedText: Do not replace Terraform references such as `azurerm_*.example.*`, `data.*.*`, or `module.*` with invented literal values. Declare the missing referenced objects on the page instead.
assessments.selectionRationale: severity 3 because the defect changes documented semantics even when the page still renders; frequency 3 because self-containedness rewrites commonly tempt literal substitution; breadth 2 because it affects many example pages but only one rewrite pattern; hostedDetectability 4 because reference-to-literal substitutions are usually visible in the diff; evidenceStrength 4 because the maintainer audit identifies the requirement as real; falsePositiveRisk 1 because invented literals are usually easy to distinguish from legitimate values; redundancy 1 because current example rules do not specifically prohibit this shortcut.

assessments.title: Example self-containedness must be transitive
assessments.applicabilityRationale: This is fundamentally an example-functionality rule, and Hosted already evaluates whether the primary example is runnable for its stated scenario.
assessments.summary: Leave the catalog unchanged because the existing functional-example rule already requires newly added supporting declarations to be runnable.
assessments.impactDescription: Support objects missing required arguments do break docs, but they do so by making the primary example nonfunctional, which current Hosted guidance already treats as a defect.
assessments.currentHostedCoverage: DOCS-EX-000 requires the primary example to be functional for its stated scenario; added support declarations that omit required arguments or blocks already violate that rule.
assessments.selectionRationale: severity 2 because the problem matters only insofar as it breaks example functionality already covered elsewhere; frequency 2 because it appears when reviewers add support objects, not on every page; breadth 2 because it can affect many examples but only one repair pattern; hostedDetectability 4 because missing required configuration is usually visible once the added object is inspected; evidenceStrength 4 because the maintainer audit is solid; falsePositiveRisk 1 because a support object missing required pieces is usually clear; redundancy 5 because DOCS-EX-000 already captures this failure condition directly enough that a new rule would duplicate meaning.
assessments.proposedText: The primary example must be functional for its stated scenario.

assessments.title: Preserve reference semantics in examples
assessments.applicabilityRationale: This is a documentation-example semantic rule, but Hosted would need substantial contextual evidence to distinguish harmful conversions from harmless simplifications consistently.
assessments.summary: Leave the catalog unchanged; this broader reference-versus-literal preservation rule overlaps existing example-functionality coverage while introducing more reviewer judgment.
assessments.impactDescription: Incorrect conversions can matter, but a broad bidirectional rule would also catch many harmless simplifications unless reviewers reconstruct deeper scenario evidence.
assessments.currentHostedCoverage: DOCS-EX-000 and DOCS-EX-003 already catch broken simplifications when they make the example nonfunctional or remove required referenced objects, but there is no exact active rule banning every reference-to-literal or literal-to-reference conversion.
assessments.proposedText: Do not change a Terraform reference to a literal, or a literal to a Terraform reference, in an example as a convenience simplification. Make the conversion only when schema or implementation evidence shows the replacement is correct for the documented scenario.
assessments.selectionRationale: severity 2 because only some conversions create real defects; frequency 2 because the pattern is occasional; breadth 3 because the rule would reach many example edits if selected; hostedDetectability 2 because reviewers often need deeper context to know whether the conversion is wrong; evidenceStrength 3 because the candidate is plausible but broader than the clearest source-backed cases; falsePositiveRisk 3 because legitimate simplifications exist; redundancy 4 because existing functionality and self-containedness rules already cover the highest-value failures without adding a broader heuristic.

assessments.title: Data source examples should demonstrate existing-object lookups
assessments.applicabilityRationale: This is a documentation-example semantics rule for a distinct object type, and Hosted can judge it from the example's shape and surrounding explanation.
assessments.summary: Add a data-source example rule so examples demonstrate lookups of existing objects rather than provisioning the object they read.
assessments.impactDescription: Without it, data source docs can model the wrong user workflow and obscure that the looked-up object is expected to pre-exist.
assessments.currentHostedCoverage: DOCS-EX-000 checks that an example works, but no active Hosted rule checks that a data source example reflects the intended existing-object lookup pattern.
assessments.proposedText: Data source examples must demonstrate looking up an existing object, and they may assume that looked-up object already exists.
assessments.selectionRationale: severity 2 because the issue is primarily conceptual misuse of a data source rather than outright broken syntax; frequency 3 because data source pages regularly need examples and often attract this anti-pattern; breadth 2 because it applies across a full doc subtype; hostedDetectability 4 because examples that create the object they then read are usually obvious; evidenceStrength 4 because the maintainer audit marks it as a real gap; falsePositiveRisk 1 because intended lookup semantics are usually clear; redundancy 1 because no current Hosted rule captures this object-type-specific expectation.

assessments.title: List-resource examples must demonstrate list queries
assessments.applicabilityRationale: This is a specialized documentation-example rule for list resources with exact syntax and query-scope expectations that Hosted can inspect directly.
assessments.summary: Add a list-resource example rule covering `list` syntax and the expected query scopes.
assessments.impactDescription: Without this rule, list-resource docs can omit the syntax and narrowed-query behavior that users actually need to learn from the page.
assessments.currentHostedCoverage: DOCS-WORD-003 covers list-resource summary wording and TEST-WF-003 covers test coverage, but no active documentation rule governs list-resource example shape.
assessments.proposedText: List-resource examples must use `list "azurerm_<name>" "example"` syntax and show the intended query scopes, including any supported narrowed query.
assessments.selectionRationale: severity 3 because wrong list-resource examples fail to teach the surface correctly; frequency 2 because list-resource pages are fewer than ordinary resources; breadth 1 because it affects only list-resource docs; hostedDetectability 5 because the required syntax and query examples are textually visible; evidenceStrength 4 because the candidate comes from maintainer-reviewed guidance; falsePositiveRisk 1 because the expected syntax is explicit; redundancy 1 because current Hosted docs rules do not cover list-resource example semantics.

assessments.title: Ephemeral-resource examples must demonstrate ephemeral reads
assessments.applicabilityRationale: This is a subtype-specific documentation-example syntax rule, and Hosted can verify it directly from the example block.
assessments.summary: Add an ephemeral-resource example rule so the primary documented object uses ephemeral syntax.
assessments.impactDescription: Without it, ephemeral-resource docs can show the wrong block kind and teach users a nonfunctional or misleading usage pattern.
assessments.currentHostedCoverage: Current Hosted documentation rules do not require ephemeral-resource examples to use `ephemeral` syntax; existing wording rules only cover summary text.
assessments.proposedText: Ephemeral-resource examples must use `ephemeral "azurerm_<name>" "example"` syntax for the primary documented object.
assessments.selectionRationale: severity 3 because the wrong block type makes the example semantically wrong; frequency 2 because every ephemeral page needs it but the surface is still narrow; breadth 1 because it applies only to ephemeral-resource docs; hostedDetectability 5 because the syntax is explicit in the code block; evidenceStrength 4 because the maintainer audit confirmed the requirement; falsePositiveRisk 1 because the allowed form is exact; redundancy 1 because no active Hosted rule currently governs ephemeral example syntax.

assessments.title: Function examples must call provider-defined functions
assessments.applicabilityRationale: This is a precise function-doc example requirement that Hosted can evaluate directly from the example invocation.
assessments.summary: Add a function example rule so function docs call the documented provider-defined function with the canonical syntax.
assessments.impactDescription: Without it, function docs can present unsupported invocation patterns and fail to teach how users actually call the function.
assessments.currentHostedCoverage: TEST-WF-005 covers provider-defined function test strategy, but no active Hosted documentation rule checks function example invocation syntax.
assessments.proposedText: Function examples must call the documented function with `provider::azurerm::<name>(...)` syntax.
assessments.selectionRationale: severity 3 because the wrong invocation syntax makes the documentation technically wrong; frequency 2 because it applies to every function page but function pages are limited; breadth 1 because only function docs are affected; hostedDetectability 5 because the call syntax is explicit; evidenceStrength 4 because the maintainer audit identifies it as a concrete missing rule; falsePositiveRisk 1 because the required form is exact; redundancy 1 because no active Hosted documentation rule covers function example syntax.

assessments.title: Import example determinism (stubs and placeholders)
assessments.applicabilityRationale: This is a precise import-section convention that Hosted already reviews under the existing import-command rule, so the right action is to extend that rule rather than add a parallel one.
assessments.summary: Update the import-section rule to keep the existing shell-command requirement and add the all-zeros subscription stub convention.
assessments.impactDescription: Without the update, import examples can remain structurally valid while still using nondeterministic subscription placeholders that drift from contributor expectations.
assessments.currentHostedCoverage: DOCS-IMP-002 already requires a `shell` fenced `terraform import azurerm_<type>.example <resource_id>` command, but it does not say which subscription placeholder to use when the import ID includes a subscription.
assessments.proposedText: A resource **Import** section must include a `shell` fenced `terraform import azurerm_<type>.example <resource_id>` command. Use `.example` as the instance name, and when the import ID contains a subscription, use the all-zeros stub `00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000`.
assessments.selectionRationale: severity 2 because this is mostly determinism and consistency rather than a behavior bug; frequency 3 because import sections are common on resource pages; breadth 2 because it applies across all resource import examples; hostedDetectability 5 because both the command shape and placeholder value are explicit text; evidenceStrength 4 because the candidate is maintainer-audited; falsePositiveRisk 1 because the expected stub is exact; redundancy 3 because `.example` is already covered, so an update is better than a separate new rule.

assessments.title: Outer fences must contain nested code fences safely
assessments.applicabilityRationale: This is a deterministic markdown-rendering rule that Hosted can enforce directly from changed documentation content.
assessments.summary: Add a markdown-fence safety rule for code blocks that contain nested triple-backtick blocks.
assessments.impactDescription: Broken outer fences can collapse rendered examples or notes and make the page misleading or unreadable.
assessments.currentHostedCoverage: No active Hosted documentation rule checks outer-fence length when nested triple-backtick blocks appear.
assessments.proposedText: If a code block contains a nested triple-backtick block, its outer opening and closing fences must use four backticks.
assessments.selectionRationale: severity 2 because the defect primarily affects rendering rather than provider semantics; frequency 2 because nested fences are uncommon but recurring enough in docs work; breadth 2 because any doc page with embedded markdown examples can be affected; hostedDetectability 5 because the fence lengths are visible in the diff; evidenceStrength 4 because the maintainer audit treats it as a genuine requirement; falsePositiveRisk 0 because the structural condition is objective; redundancy 0 because the current catalog has no overlapping markdown-fence rule.

assessments.title: Argument bullet concision is semantic, not numeric
assessments.applicabilityRationale: This candidate controls when a documentation finding is actionable, which fits Hosted's review-classification layer better than a pure style rule.
assessments.summary: Add a false-positive control so Hosted judges argument-bullet concision semantically instead of by sentence count.
assessments.impactDescription: Without it, Hosted can overflag correct but slightly longer bullets and push maintainers toward deleting necessary defaults, value constraints, or ForceNew text.
assessments.currentHostedCoverage: DOCS-ARG-003 through DOCS-ARG-005 and DOCS-NOTE-002 govern required content, but no active rule tells Hosted not to treat sentence count alone as a defect.
assessments.proposedText: Do not treat sentence count alone as a documentation defect. Argument bullets should stay field-definitional; keep the definition, possible values, defaults, and any required ForceNew sentence in the bullet, and move caveats or conditional requirements into a note when needed.
assessments.selectionRationale: severity 2 because this rule mainly prevents bad review behavior rather than fixing broken docs directly; frequency 3 because argument bullets appear on almost every reference page and invite over-enforcement; breadth 3 because it influences many documentation reviews and the review skill itself; hostedDetectability 4 because Hosted can compare bullet content against the prohibited sentence-count heuristic; evidenceStrength 3 because the rule is a local safeguard rather than a published upstream mandate; falsePositiveRisk 2 because reviewers still need judgment about what belongs in a note; redundancy 1 because no current Hosted rule protects against this specific false-positive pattern.

assessments.title: List-resource query arguments should be ordered alphabetically
assessments.applicabilityRationale: This is an enforceable documentation-ordering convention, but it is narrow presentation guidance rather than a high-leverage semantic defect class.
assessments.summary: Leave the catalog unchanged; the ordering convention is real, but it is too narrow to justify another Hosted rule.
assessments.impactDescription: Misordered list-resource query arguments reduce consistency, but they do not usually misstate provider behavior or make the page unusable.
assessments.currentHostedCoverage: No active Hosted rule checks list-resource query-argument ordering, and the current catalog intentionally prioritizes higher-impact semantic defects over low-risk ordering conventions.
assessments.proposedText: In list-resource documentation, order query arguments with required arguments first and optional arguments second, and sort arguments alphabetically within each group.
assessments.selectionRationale: severity 1 because the issue is presentational rather than semantic; frequency 2 because every list-resource page could hit it but list-resource pages are few; breadth 1 because it affects only one doc subtype and one section ordering rule; hostedDetectability 5 because ordering is trivial to inspect; evidenceStrength 4 because the maintainer audit found a real convention; falsePositiveRisk 0 because the expected order is objective; redundancy 0 because there is no overlapping rule, but the low impact still supports leaving the catalog unchanged.

assessments.title: Function argument lists must follow function signature order
assessments.applicabilityRationale: This is a function-doc structure rule with clear ordering and formatting expectations that Hosted can verify from the changed page.
assessments.summary: Add a function-argument structure rule so function docs follow signature order and use ordered list items.
assessments.impactDescription: Without it, function docs can read like resource docs, obscuring call position and making function signatures harder for users to follow correctly.
assessments.currentHostedCoverage: No active Hosted documentation rule checks function-argument ordering or requires ordered-list formatting for function signatures.
assessments.proposedText: Function arguments must be documented in implementation signature order and rendered as ordered list items rather than resource-style argument bullets.
assessments.selectionRationale: severity 3 because wrong order or format can materially confuse how a function is called; frequency 2 because every function page needs it but function docs are a limited subset; breadth 1 because it applies only to function docs; hostedDetectability 5 because both ordering and list format are visible in the page; evidenceStrength 4 because the maintainer audit identifies it as a genuine requirement; falsePositiveRisk 1 because signature order is objective; redundancy 1 because no active Hosted rule covers function argument structure.

assessments.title: Do not special-case common fields in Attributes Reference
assessments.applicabilityRationale: This is a presentation-order convention for one documentation section, not a semantic or behavioral defect threshold that merits Hosted review guidance.
assessments.summary: Exclude this common-field ordering convention from Hosted; it governs list presentation rather than schema accuracy or user-visible behavior.
assessments.impactDescription: Including it would spend documentation rule budget on alphabetical ordering findings while leaving substantive schema and lifecycle mismatches unchanged.
assessments.currentHostedCoverage: DOCS-ATTR-002 requires attribute coverage completeness, but no active Hosted rule governs attribute ordering, and that omission is acceptable for Hosted.
assessments.proposedText: Under **Attributes Reference**, list `id` first and sort all remaining attributes alphabetically; do not special-case `name`, `resource_group_name`, `location`, or `tags`.
assessments.selectionRationale: Severity 1 because misordering common attributes mainly affects readability; frequency 2 because these fields recur often but only in Attributes Reference ordering; breadth 1 because the issue is limited to documentation; hostedDetectability 4 because ordering and special-casing are easy to inspect; evidenceStrength 3 because it is a maintained convention but not a published upstream requirement; falsePositiveRisk 4 because intentional grouping, nested attributes, and generated ordering can make a rigid rule noisy; redundancy 1 because current Hosted rules do not already encode the ordering rule, yet the low impact and high noise still support exclusion.

assessments.title: ForceNew guidance must use `~> **Note:**`
assessments.applicabilityRationale: The core ForceNew behavior is already covered semantically, and the specific callout marker is a formatting convention rather than a distinct Hosted defect rule.
assessments.summary: Exclude this note-marker convention from Hosted; the important behavior wording is already guarded, and the marker choice is a presentation detail.
assessments.impactDescription: Adding it would create formatting-only findings for ForceNew notes even when the documentation already communicates the lifecycle consequence correctly.
assessments.currentHostedCoverage: DOCS-ARG-003 already requires the exact ForceNew sentence for resource arguments and forbids ForceNew wording in non-resource docs; no active Hosted rule requires a specific note marker.
assessments.proposedText: Notes that warn about ForceNew behavior must use the `~> **Note:**` marker.
assessments.selectionRationale: Severity 2 because ForceNew guidance matters, but this candidate changes formatting rather than the underlying lifecycle warning; frequency 2 because ForceNew fields are common but not universal; breadth 1 because the issue is documentation-only; hostedDetectability 5 because the note marker is explicit in markdown; evidenceStrength 3 because it is a documented maintainer convention; falsePositiveRisk 2 because the marker itself is objective, though equivalent house styles could appear; redundancy 4 because DOCS-ARG-003 already captures the substantive ForceNew guidance that Hosted most needs to preserve.

assessments.title: De-duplicate equivalent notes
assessments.applicabilityRationale: This is a documentation clarity preference, but detecting semantic equivalence across separately worded notes is too subjective for compact Hosted review guidance.
assessments.summary: Exclude this de-duplication rule from Hosted; it is valuable editorial guidance, but not a stable standalone defect rule.
assessments.impactDescription: Including it would steer review effort toward prose consolidation decisions instead of higher-value checks for missing or incorrect constraints.
assessments.currentHostedCoverage: DOCS-NOTE-002 checks that required cross-field notes exist and match behavior, but no active Hosted rule tries to merge semantically equivalent notes.
assessments.proposedText: Do not repeat the same conditional requirement or conflict across multiple notes, including inverse phrasing; merge equivalent guidance into a single note.
assessments.selectionRationale: Severity 1 because duplicate notes usually affect concision more than correctness; frequency 2 because repeated conditions appear occasionally but not everywhere; breadth 1 because the issue is limited to documentation; hostedDetectability 3 because exact duplicates are easy to spot but inverse phrasing and partial overlap require judgment; evidenceStrength 3 because the convention is explicitly stated by maintainers; falsePositiveRisk 4 because deciding when two notes are truly equivalent is often subjective; redundancy 2 because existing Hosted note rules already cover the substantive requirement, leaving this as an editorial refinement.

assessments.title: Data source, list-resource, ephemeral-resource, and function field notes are prohibited
assessments.applicabilityRationale: This is primarily a style restriction on how certain documentation types present field descriptions, and it is too rigid for Hosted when some field-specific constraints may still need explicit explanation.
assessments.summary: Exclude this field-level note ban from Hosted; it constrains editorial style more than it protects semantic correctness.
assessments.impactDescription: A Hosted rule here could suppress useful field-specific guidance in non-resource docs while duplicating existing rules that already require real constraints to be documented correctly.
assessments.currentHostedCoverage: DOCS-NOTE-002 and the argument coverage rules already govern substantive field requirements and conflicts, but no active Hosted rule bans notes by documentation type.
assessments.proposedText: Do not use field-level note blocks in data source, list-resource, ephemeral-resource, or function field descriptions; keep those entries limited to describing the field itself.
assessments.selectionRationale: Severity 2 because excess notes can clutter docs, but the defect is usually presentation rather than wrong behavior; frequency 2 because these note blocks appear only in some documentation updates; breadth 2 because the convention spans several documentation types; hostedDetectability 3 because note blocks are visible but determining when a field description has become an impermissible note requires judgment; evidenceStrength 3 because the maintainer guidance is explicit; falsePositiveRisk 4 because a rigid ban can conflict with legitimate field-specific constraints; redundancy 3 because existing Hosted rules already cover the substantive conditions and conflicts that matter most.

assessments.title: Block vs inline vs map parity
assessments.applicabilityRationale: Schema-to-documentation structural mismatches are independently enforceable from repository evidence and directly create invalid or misleading user guidance.
assessments.summary: Add a Hosted documentation rule requiring block, scalar, and map descriptions to match the schema's structural shape.
assessments.impactDescription: This would catch docs that invent nested subfields for primitive values, flatten real nested blocks, or misdescribe maps, all of which can lead users toward invalid configuration.
assessments.currentHostedCoverage: DOCS-ARG-001 and DOCS-ATTR-002 verify presence and completeness, but no active Hosted rule requires the documented structural shape to match schema.
assessments.proposedText: Documentation must match the schema's structural shape: document nested blocks as blocks with their own nested-field sections, do not document scalars or primitive collections as named subfields, and describe `TypeMap` fields as maps.
assessments.selectionRationale: Severity 4 because shape mismatches lead users to write the wrong configuration form; frequency 3 because nested blocks, maps, and collections appear regularly in provider docs; breadth 3 because the issue can affect resource, data source, list-resource, ephemeral-resource, and function documentation; hostedDetectability 4 because schema shape and markdown structure can usually be compared directly; evidenceStrength 4 because the maintainer requirement is concrete and aligns with objective schema facts; falsePositiveRisk 1 because block, scalar, map, and primitive collection distinctions are mostly unambiguous; redundancy 1 because current Hosted rules check coverage and wording, not structural representation.

assessments.title: Primitive list/set parity
assessments.applicabilityRationale: The underlying issue is Hosted-relevant, but this candidate is too narrow to stand alone; Hosted should encode the broader structural-shape parity rule instead of a primitive-list special case.
assessments.summary: Exclude this standalone primitive collection rule and capture the defect class through a broader schema-shape parity rule instead.
assessments.impactDescription: A separate Hosted rule here would spend catalog space on one manifestation of a wider documentation-shape problem that is better enforced generically.
assessments.currentHostedCoverage: No active Hosted rule yet covers structural-shape parity; this candidate is a narrow subset of that broader uncovered gap.
assessments.proposedText: When schema exposes a list or set of primitive values, document it as a list of values, not as a nested block or named subfields.

assessments.title: Directional block references must match subsection position
assessments.applicabilityRationale: This is a prose-coherence convention about directional phrasing, not a sufficiently important semantic defect class for Hosted review guidance.

assessments.title: Use nearby implementations before inventing new patterns
assessments.applicabilityRationale: Pattern selection for implementation work is review-relevant and enforceable through same-service repository evidence, especially when changes introduce a novel local shape without justification.

assessments.proposedText: Use the nearest same-service resource or data source as the primary pattern source for schema shape, CRUD flow, expand and flatten helpers, and timeouts. Do not introduce a new local pattern when an established service pattern already covers the scenario.
assessments.selectionRationale: Severity 3 because unjustified pattern drift increases defect risk and review inconsistency across a service; frequency 4 because most implementation work extends existing services and patterns; breadth 3 because the rule affects schema, CRUD, helpers, and timeout structure across implementation reviews; hostedDetectability 2 because applying it requires cross-file comparison and judgment about what precedent is closest; evidenceStrength 4 because the maintainer convention is explicit and repository-backed by same-service examples; falsePositiveRisk 3 because some changes legitimately need a new pattern when the old one does not fit; redundancy 2 because IMPL-WF-001A partially covers model choice but not service-local pattern sourcing.

assessments.title: Ephemeral resources must follow the framework ephemeral pattern
assessments.applicabilityRationale: Ephemeral resources are a specialized provider surface with objective file, type, registration, documentation, and test requirements that Hosted can verify directly.
assessments.summary: Add a Hosted implementation rule for the required framework ephemeral-resource pattern and its companion registration, documentation, and test surfaces.

assessments.proposedText: Ephemeral resources must live in the owning service package as `*_ephemeral.go`, use the framework `sdk.EphemeralResource` pattern with `Metadata`, `Configure`, `Schema`, and `Open`, register through `Registration.EphemeralResources()`, include `website/docs/ephemeral-resources/` documentation, and add `*_ephemeral_test.go` coverage.
assessments.selectionRationale: Severity 4 because using the wrong surface model or omitting registration and companions can leave the feature broken or undiscoverable; frequency 2 because ephemeral resources are still relatively uncommon; breadth 3 because the rule spans implementation, documentation, and testing surfaces; hostedDetectability 4 because filenames, interfaces, registration hooks, docs, and tests are explicit in the repository; evidenceStrength 4 because the maintainer convention is concrete and specialized; falsePositiveRisk 1 because the expected framework pattern and companions are objective; redundancy 2 because current Hosted rules cover parts of the test and wording story but not the end-to-end implementation requirement.

assessments.title: Provider-defined functions must follow the internal provider-function pattern
assessments.applicabilityRationale: Provider-defined functions are a specialized framework surface with objective placement, interface, documentation, and test requirements that Hosted can enforce.
assessments.summary: Add a Hosted implementation rule for the required provider-defined function pattern and its companion docs and tests.
assessments.impactDescription: This would catch provider functions implemented in the wrong package, with the wrong framework interface, or without the required documentation and unit-test coverage.
assessments.currentHostedCoverage: IMPL-WF-001A covers general model classification, TEST-WF-005 covers function test conventions, and DOCS-WORD-003 covers function summary wording, but no active Hosted rule enforces the implementation location and framework pattern for provider-defined functions.
assessments.proposedText: Provider-defined functions must live under `internal/provider/function/`, use the framework `function.Function` pattern with `Metadata`, `Definition`, and `Run`, include `website/docs/functions/` documentation, and add `internal/provider/function/*_test.go` coverage.
assessments.selectionRationale: Severity 4 because the wrong implementation surface or missing companions can leave provider functions unusable or unreviewable; frequency 2 because provider-defined functions are still specialized work; breadth 3 because the rule spans implementation, documentation, and testing; hostedDetectability 4 because package location, method set, docs, and tests are explicit in the repository; evidenceStrength 4 because the maintainer convention is concrete and framework-specific; falsePositiveRisk 1 because the expected pattern is objective; redundancy 2 because current Hosted rules cover test shape and summary wording but not the full implementation requirement.

assessments.title: Prefer inline composition; extract only genuinely complex bespoke validation
assessments.applicabilityRationale: This is primarily validator organization guidance; Hosted should review validation correctness and lifecycle behavior, not whether reusable validator pieces stay inline.
assessments.summary: Exclude this validator-composition style rule from Hosted; it is about code organization more than user-visible correctness.
assessments.impactDescription: Including it would generate maintainability findings about inline versus extracted validators even when the implemented validation behavior is correct.
assessments.currentHostedCoverage: IMPL-SCHEMA-001, IMPL-SCHEMA-004, and IMPL-SCHEMA-013 already guard validation correctness and evidence-backed behavior without prescribing validator extraction style.
assessments.proposedText: Use inline composition for standard validators, including nested `validation.All(...)` and `validation.Any(...)`; extract only genuinely complex bespoke validation into the same service's `validate/` folder, and name the validator file and unit test for the validated subject.
assessments.selectionRationale: Severity 2 because poor validator factoring can hurt maintainability but usually does not change accepted configuration; frequency 3 because schema validators are common in implementation work; breadth 2 because the issue spans implementation and validation-related tests but not the wider repo; hostedDetectability 4 because inline versus extracted validation code is easy to see; evidenceStrength 3 because the maintainer convention is explicit; falsePositiveRisk 4 because whether logic is genuinely complex enough to extract is subjective; redundancy 3 because existing Hosted schema rules already cover the behavior that matters most.

assessments.title: Avoid unnecessary comments
assessments.applicabilityRationale: Comment necessity is too style-driven and subjective for Hosted, which is intended to guard actionable implementation defects rather than code cleanliness preferences.
assessments.summary: Exclude this comment-style rule from Hosted; it is a maintainability preference, not a stable semantic defect rule.
assessments.impactDescription: Adding it would create noisy findings about explanatory comments while offering little protection against actual Azure API, schema, or state defects.
assessments.currentHostedCoverage: No active Hosted implementation rule regulates comment density or placement, which is consistent with the catalog's focus on behavioral correctness.
assessments.proposedText: Comment only non-obvious Azure quirks, Azure SDK workarounds, irreducibly complex logic, or non-obvious state behavior. Do not add comments for routine assignments, struct initialization, standard Terraform or Go patterns, obvious field mappings, or routine error or nil handling.
assessments.selectionRationale: Severity 1 because unnecessary comments usually affect readability rather than runtime behavior; frequency 3 because comments appear throughout implementation work; breadth 2 because the convention spans many implementation files but not other review surfaces; hostedDetectability 5 because comments are explicit in the diff; evidenceStrength 3 because the maintainer guidance is clearly stated; falsePositiveRisk 5 because judgments about what is obvious or non-obvious vary widely by reviewer and context; redundancy 1 because current Hosted rules intentionally avoid comment-style policing.

assessments.applicabilityRationale: Generic lifecycle logging avoidance is a code-style and observability preference, not a core implementation defect boundary for Hosted review.

assessments.applicabilityRationale: This is a tiny test-helper style preference within config builders, not a meaningful acceptance-test defect boundary for Hosted review.

assessments.title: Prefer typed resource IDs over raw ID strings in logs
assessments.applicabilityRationale: The note is specific enough to review in implementation diffs, but it mainly standardizes diagnostic style and does not guard a material correctness failure, so it is not a strong Hosted rule candidate.

assessments.applicabilityRationale: The source explicitly distinguishes legacy untyped, typed `internal/sdk`, and framework-native implementations, so it provides directly enforceable guidance for how Hosted should frame implementation review comments.

Maintain the existing model unless the task is an explicit migration; use typed for current ordinary resource and data source work, and framework patterns for framework-native or specialized surfaces.

assessments.title: Keep new functionality out of deprecated shared helper packages
assessments.applicabilityRationale: The source gives a concrete placement rule for new code in deprecated packages (`helpers` and `internal/resourceid`), and reviews can verify violations from file paths, imports, and newly added helper logic.
assessments.summary: The overview marks `helpers` as deprecated for new functionality and `internal/resourceid` as deprecated in favor of `go-azure-helpers`, but the Hosted catalog does not currently enforce those package boundaries.
assessments.impactDescription: Without a Hosted rule, reviews can accept new logic in packages maintainers are trying to retire, increasing migration debt and splitting supported helper patterns from deprecated ones.
assessments.currentHostedCoverage: No active Hosted rule directly blocks new functionality in deprecated helper packages. IMPL-SCHEMA-006 only covers canonical resource ID parsing and state behavior once a parser exists.
assessments.proposedText: Do not add new functionality to deprecated shared helper packages such as `helpers` or `internal/resourceid`. Put new logic in the service package or supported shared helpers, and use `go-azure-helpers/resourcemanager/resourceids` instead of expanding deprecated resource ID implementations.
assessments.selectionRationale: Severity 3 fits because violations mainly create architectural and migration debt, but they also steer new code toward deprecated patterns; frequency 2 fits because only a subset of changes introduces new shared helper functionality; breadth 3 fits because the boundary affects multiple services and shared packages; hostedDetectability 4 fits because added files, imports, and package-local logic are visible in diffs; evidenceStrength 4 fits because the source explicitly marks both packages as deprecated and directs new functionality elsewhere; falsePositiveRisk 2 fits because the rule can be scoped to new functionality and deprecated expansion rather than routine fixes; redundancy 2 fits because IMPL-SCHEMA-006 overlaps on resource ID helper usage but does not cover the broader package-placement boundary.

assessments.title: Follow standard service package file naming for resources, data sources, and acceptance tests
assessments.applicabilityRationale: The source provides exact filename patterns for resource, data source, and acceptance-test files, so a reviewer can compare the convention against added or renamed files.
assessments.summary: The overview prescribes `{name}_resource.go`, `{name}_data_source.go`, and matching `_test.go` filenames, but it also notes exceptions used to reduce stuttering.
